title: Memory snapshots leak the LUKS DEK — luksSuspend around freeze/thaw
description:
SECURITY. Close before multi-tenancy ships; it gets harder once tenants exist.

memory_snapshot.ex:98 writes CH memory artifacts to @snapshots/<name>.mem —
the full guest address space. For any VM that has unlocked its LUKS volume the
dm-crypt DEK is in that file IN CLEARTEXT. The whole tier-3 design rests on the
DEK existing only in guest RAM; a memory snapshot makes guest RAM a host file.
Any off-box replication of .mem exports the key next to the ciphertext it
protects.

## There is no 'secure RAM region' to hide it in

A memory snapshot exists to reproduce the guest exactly. Anything reachable at
thaw is captured; anything not captured is unreachable at thaw. Rejected:
- CPU/debug registers (TRESOR-style): CH saves vCPU state to state.json — that
  is what makes restore work. Registers ARE captured.
- Excluding a CH memory zone: needs a CH patch, AND the guest cannot confine a
  dm-crypt key to one zone (copied into crypto tfm, scatterlists, slab).
- Guest kernel keyring: still ordinary kernel RAM.
- SEV-SNP / TDX: the real hardware answer, but snapshot/restore under SNP needs
  a PSP-mediated migration agent; CH support thin-to-absent. Track, don't build on.

## The fix: no key exists at capture time

cryptsetup luksSuspend suspends the dm device AND wipes the volume key from
kernel memory (it exists for suspend-to-disk).

  freeze: fsfreeze -f /mnt/secrets
          cryptsetup luksSuspend secrets     # key wiped from kernel RAM
          CH vm.pause + capture RAM          # captured RAM holds no usable key
  thaw:   CH vm.resume
          inject_secrets over vsock          # EXISTING path, vm.ex:2422
          cryptsetup luksResume secrets
          fsfreeze -u /mnt/secrets

Fits Mjolnir specifically:
1. The LUKS container is a loopback device, NOT root (root is virtio-fs), so
   luksSuspend cannot deadlock the guest — the usual footgun does not apply.
2. maybe_unlock_secrets/2 already injects the passphrase over vsock on every
   boot AND dormancy wake. Thaw = a wake plus two guest-agent calls.
3. :managed re-injects from SecretEscrow automatically. :persistent needs the
   owner's Iroh peer at thaw — same requirement it already has at boot.

## Residual, stated honestly

Plaintext DATA read before the freeze may remain in guest page cache and thus in
the captured RAM. fsfreeze + drop_caches narrows, does not eliminate. What
changes: the snapshot no longer yields a REUSABLE unlock capability. Bounded
one-time data exposure instead of total key compromise. Encrypting .mem to the
owner's key (via PRE, once the DEK-wrap child lands) closes the residue too.

## Must be structural

Wire suspend/resume into the snapshot path itself. Do not rely on callers being
careful. A :managed/:persistent VM must not be able to take a naive memory
snapshot.

Guest agent work: add luksSuspend/luksResume to native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/secrets.rs
(cryptsetup already shelled out to there).
close_reason: Implemented: guest agent luksSuspend/luksResume, inject() resumes a suspended mapper, MemorySnapshot.freeze refuses a naive secrets snapshot. Live verify is mjolnir-k8y.3.1 (needs deploy). 434c711

title: Health monitor heals long-running VMs to death: a busy guest agent is not an unreachable one
description:
Generalisation of the root cause found in mjolnir-7jb. Any VM running a long exec is exposed, not just deploy build VMs.

Health.Monitor probes the guest agent; a guest busy with a long command does not answer in time; the monitor declares it unreachable and heals it. The L1 heal is VM.rebuild_vsock_connection/1, which stops the existing Vsock.Connection — including any in-flight request. The caller's GenServer.call then exits :normal and surfaces as {:vsock_unavailable, ...} (the mjolnir-8ie wrapper).

So Mjolnir's own health system reliably destroys any operation that takes longer than the probe's patience. Observed killing a deploy build 100% of the time on the one step long enough to trigger it, while mise install and bun install completed fine.

The category error: BUSY is being read as DEAD. A guest agent occupied by a legitimate long-running command is the healthiest possible state.

Preferred fix: track in-flight execs in Mjolnir.VM state — cheap now that mjolnir-8ie moved exec into a Task with a known lifetime — and have Health treat 'exec in flight' as alive. Failing that, rebuild_vsock_connection/1 must refuse to tear down a connection with pending requests.

Also worth fixing alongside: the monitor probes Iroh on ephemeral build VMs, which never have it (iroh_connection = {:dead, :iroh_probe_timeout}). Probing capabilities a VM was never configured with produces noise that looks like failure.
acceptance_criteria: A VM executing a command that outlasts the health probe interval is not healed; a long mj exec and a deploy build both complete without the monitor interfering.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-08 (commit 3114139), deployed and verified by the thing it was breaking: startup-central now builds and deploys end to end, on the exact step that had failed 100% of the time.

Mjolnir.VM tracks in-flight exec tasks by monitor ref (cheap now that mjolnir-8ie moved exec off the mailbox), keyed to the command so an operator can see WHAT the VM is busy with. The :DOWN handler clears on completion AND on crash — a leaked flag would make a VM permanently unhealable, a worse bug than the original.

Health.corroborated_overall/4 gains :busy, short-circuiting BEFORE the TCP liveness probe (an in-flight exec is stronger evidence than a SYN-ACK, and cheaper). Applies to :degraded too. Monitor logs it at debug and does not heal. Health.heal/2 refuses outright for a busy VM, since it is public and reachable from the API and 'mj doctor --fix'.

Idle-VM verdicts unchanged and asserted explicitly, so this cannot blunt genuine death detection. 20 tests; the three corroboration tests verified to fail with the :busy branch removed.

STILL OPEN, separately: the monitor probes Iroh on ephemeral build VMs that never had it (iroh_connection = {:dead, :iroh_probe_timeout}). Noise that looks like failure. Worth narrowing probes to configured capabilities.

title: RouteReconciler startup race drops customer routes on every mjolnir restart
description:
SECOND outage of startupcentral.build on 2026-08-07, different cause from mjolnir-1pk.

Gateway.Routes.spec_to_route/4 skips any app whose service VM is not in running_vm_ids, and default_running_vm_ids/0 is Mjolnir.VM.list() filtered on state == :running. On a mjolnir restart the reconciler renders BEFORE the service VMs have finished resuming, so the route is dropped — and nothing re-triggers a render once they come up. Caught in the log with a 2-second gap:

  21:37:19.461 [warning] Gateway.Routes: skipping startupcentral.build — VM de9fe3e2 is not running/local; no route emitted
  21:37:21.543 [info]    VM identity present, skipped for VM de9fe3e2

Every restart is a coin flip on whether customer routes survive.

TWO COMPOUNDING DEFECTS:

1. The render is not retried after VMs come up. RouteReconciler.trigger/0 fires on VM lifecycle EventBus events, but by then the render has already written a route-less apps.toml, and a later trigger only helps if some other VM event happens to occur.

2. default_running_vm_ids/0 has  and . VM.list/0 polls every VM GenServer, so ONE wedged VM (mjolnir-8ie / mjolnir-75d) can make the whole call exit — yielding an EMPTY running set and therefore wiping EVERY route in one render. Failing to an empty set is exactly backwards: on an inconclusive read the reconciler should keep the previous file, never render a wipe.

Observed: with several VMs wedged/recovering, a manually triggered reconcile still would not emit the route even though GET /api/vms/de9fe3e2 reported state=running.

MITIGATION IN PLACE: a hand-managed [[route]] for startupcentral.build was added to /etc/mjolnir/gateway.toml (NOT reconciler-owned, so it survives the race). Site verified 200 with a homepage sha256 identical to the pre-outage baseline. Remove that static route once this ships.

WANTED:
- never render a wipe from an inconclusive VM read — distinguish 'no running VMs' from 'could not determine', and on the latter keep the existing file
- re-render once after boot settles (e.g. on the first successful health tick), not only on lifecycle events
- treat a render that REMOVES routes as noteworthy: log at warning with the delta, since silent route loss is the failure mode both of today's outages shared
acceptance_criteria: Restarting mjolnir with a deployed custom-domain app never leaves apps.toml without that app's route; a wedged VM cannot cause other apps' routes to be dropped; a route-removing render logs the delta.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-07 (commit d4eca11), deployed and verified.

1. Startup race: RouteReconciler now sweeps again at 15s/60s/180s after boot, sent as their own :settle_render message so they neither cancel nor are cancelled by the debounce timer. Renders are idempotent so extra passes just rewrite identical bytes. Confirmed firing in production after a real restart — Gateway.Routes wrote routes at 22:31:41 (boot), then 22:31:55, 22:32:40 and 22:34:35, matching the schedule.

2. Inconclusive read: default_running_vm_ids/0 now returns :unknown on rescue/catch instead of [], and render_and_reload/1 keeps the existing file rather than publishing a wipe. A genuine [] still renders, so 'mj domain rm' keeps working.

3. A render that removes routes logs at warning with the fqdns lost.

Tests: 4 destructive-render guards + 3 settle-sweep, including one that asserts the sweep is enabled BY DEFAULT (the others inject :settle_delays_ms and would keep passing with the default emptied — exactly the regression). Both defects reintroduced produce 2 failures.

Verified live: emergency static route REMOVED from gateway.toml first, so the reconciler alone was under test. mjolnir restarted; startupcentral route present at t+5s through t+190s, HTTP 200 throughout, homepage sha256 identical to the pre-outage baseline.

CAVEAT, stated plainly: the race did not RECUR on that restart — the boot render already saw both VMs running, because a mjolnir restart does not kill the CH processes. So this run proves the sweep mechanism is live and non-destructive, not that it rescued a reproduced race. The race path itself is covered by the unit tests.

title: Upgrade Cloud Hypervisor v50 -> v52+ (unblocks the whole memory-snapshot epic)
description:
THE unblocker. mjolnir-3y6.11 proved by experiment that CH v50.0.0 never transfers vhost-user backend state during vm.snapshot/vm.restore, so any VM with a virtio-fs rootfs — i.e. every Mjolnir VM — panics and cold-reboots on resume.

Cloud Hypervisor v52.0 (2025-05-14) fixes this and three other hazards in this epic outright:
- 'Snapshot/restore support for vhost-user devices has been filled out (#7908), including migration support for virtio-fs (#7937).'  -> fixes mjolnir-3y6.11
- 'Vsock connections are now reset on snapshot restore to avoid stale half-open connections on the guest side (#7958).'  -> fixes mjolnir-3y6.6
- 'The KVM clock is now restored before vCPUs are resumed (#7932).'  -> fixes mjolnir-3y6.7
- New memory_restore_mode populates guest memory lazily via userfaultfd instead of reading the whole snapshot before resume -> big win for mjolnir-3y6.9 (restore latency on large guests)

Upstream issue #6931 'Unable to restore a snapshot of vm using virtiofs root' is the exact hang reproduced here, and is closed.

CAUTION: this is a hypervisor upgrade on the live host under running VMs. Needs a staged rollout — verify v52 boots a normal VM with the current vm.create payload BEFORE relying on it, since the config schema may have shifted between v50 and v52. Pair with a virtiofsd floor (>=1.14) per mjolnir-3y6.14.
acceptance_criteria: cloud-hypervisor v52+ installed; an ordinary VM spawns, execs, and kills normally; and a virtio-fs-rooted VM completes pause -> snapshot -> fresh VMM -> restore -> resume with a marker process still running at the same PID.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-07. Upgraded in place on 45.76.77.97: cloud-hypervisor v50.0.0 -> v53.0 (latest, 2026-07-12; includes all the v52 fixes), virtiofsd 1.10.0 -> 1.14.0 at /usr/local/bin. Backups kept at /usr/local/bin/cloud-hypervisor.v50-backup and virtiofsd.v1.10-backup.

No vm.create schema drift — the current Mjolnir-shaped payload (fs + vsock + rng + kernel/initramfs) works on v53 unchanged. VM spawn/exec/kill verified after the swap; the three pre-existing VMs were revived by Mjolnir on restart rather than lost.

FREEZE/THAW NOW PROVEN WORKING (this closes mjolnir-3y6.1's acceptance criteria):
  pre-freeze:  counter=17 pid=776
  post-thaw:   counter=21 -> 24 -> 27 -> 30, pid=776 UNCHANGED
  i8042 reset / VM reset events in the CH log: 0
A process running before the freeze was still running after the thaw, same PID, having observed no reboot — which is exactly the gate.

Requires virtiofsd --migration-mode=find-paths (shipped in the virtiofs.ex change). virtiofsd logs 'Front-end did not announce migration to begin, so we failed to prepare for it; collecting data now. If you are doing a snapshot, that is OK' — i.e. it serializes on demand for the snapshot case.

title: Upgrade virtiofsd and re-test vm.restore with vhost-user-fs
description:
Deciding experiment for the whole epic. mjolnir-3y6.11 proved CH v50 vm.restore deadlocks on a vhost-user-fs device backed by virtiofsd 1.10.0 (Ubuntu noble's version, Jan 2024), while the identical VM without virtio-fs restores fine.

CH v50 advertises the DEVICE_STATE vhost-user protocol feature; virtiofsd 1.10.0 does not implement it. Upstream virtiofsd is at 1.14.0 (Jul 2026).

Build a current virtiofsd (cargo install virtiofsd --version 1.14.0; needs libcap-ng-dev + libseccomp-dev) and re-run the freeze/thaw against it.

IF IT WORKS: the epic proceeds on virtio-fs as designed, with a virtiofsd version floor added to the host bootstrap scripts.
IF IT DOES NOT: freezable VMs need a virtio-blk rootfs (block image on btrfs) — a significant architecture fork from the current virtio-fs design, and that decision should be written up before any more of the epic is built.
acceptance_criteria: A VM with a virtio-fs rootfs completes pause -> vm.snapshot -> fresh VMM -> vm.restore -> vm.resume, with a marker process still running and the same PID afterwards. Or, a written decision to move freezable VMs to virtio-blk.
notes: DONE — virtiofsd 1.14.0 built and tested (/opt/virtiofsd-1.14/bin/virtiofsd on the server). It is NOT the blocker: 1.14 implements device state correctly, but CH v50 never asks for it. See mjolnir-3y6.11 for the full evidence. The real fix is the CH upgrade, mjolnir-3y6.15. A virtiofsd version floor is still worth adding to the bootstrap scripts, since v52's virtio-fs migration needs a backend that can serialize.

title: SPIKE RISK: virtiofsd nodeid stability across restore
description:
Sharper than the page cache and specific to virtio-fs. The guest does not cache blocks of a disk — it holds FUSE-level state, inode IDs (nodeids) and file handles that VIRTIOFSD assigned, and that state lives in guest RAM.

On restore a FRESH virtiofsd process starts assigning nodeids from scratch while the restored guest holds the previous process's numbering. Unless the mapping is preserved or deterministic, every open file in the guest refers to the wrong inode or to nothing.

CH's 'Restoring vhost-user-fs' restores CH's OWN device state (virtqueues, config space). virtiofsd is a separate process whose state is NOT in the CH snapshot.

This is the single most likely reason mjolnir-3y6.1 fails. Determine it FIRST — it gates the shape of the whole epic.

If nodeids are not stable, the options are:
- a virtiofsd supporting vhost-user backend state transfer (VHOST_USER_PROTOCOL_F_DEVICE_STATE), or
- rootfs on virtio-blk (block image on btrfs) for freezable VMs — a significant architecture fork from the current virtio-fs design.

Current launch args (confirmed on the running host): virtiofsd --socket-path=... --shared-dir=/var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@vms/<uuid> --cache=auto --sandbox=none --thread-pool-size=4
acceptance_criteria: A file held open across freeze/thaw still reads correctly afterwards, and a fresh open of the same path returns the same inode. If it fails, the decision between virtiofsd state transfer and virtio-blk is written up with a recommendation.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-07 — NEGATIVE, and the failure is upstream of nodeids.

CH v50 vm.restore DEADLOCKS when the snapshot config contains a vhost-user-fs device backed by virtiofsd 1.10.0. It never gets as far as nodeid semantics.

Evidence:
- vm.snapshot itself succeeds (204) and writes config.json + state.json + memory-ranges (memory-ranges is exactly mem_size, uncompressed: 1GiB VM -> 1GiB file).
- On restore, virtiofsd logs 'Client connected, servicing requests' — so CH DOES reconnect to the vhost-user socket — then the vm.restore HTTP call never returns.
- Hung CH thread dump: threads _net0_ctrl, _net0_qp0, __rng exist (net + rng restored) but there is NO _fs1 thread and NO vcpu thread. The 'vmm' thread sits in unix_stream_data_wait (blocked reading the vhost-user socket) and 'http-server' in futex_wait_queue (which is why the API call hangs).

CONTROL EXPERIMENT (isolates the variable): an otherwise identical minimal VM — same kernel, same initramfs, rng device, NO virtio-fs, NO net, NO vsock — snapshots and restores cleanly: RESTORE=204, RESUME=204, STATE=Running, with a live vcpu0 in kvm_vcpu_block and healthy ep_poll event loops. So CH v50 snapshot/restore works; the vhost-user-fs device is the specific thing that breaks it.

ROOT CAUSE: CH v50's vhost-user protocol feature list includes DEVICE_STATE (confirmed in the binary's feature strings). virtiofsd 1.10.0 contains ZERO device_state/migration strings and its --help exposes no migration options. CH knows how to ask for device state; the backend cannot answer, so the handshake stalls.

virtiofsd 1.10.0 is what Ubuntu noble ships (1.10.0-1ubuntu0.1, released Jan 2024). Upstream is at 1.14.0 (Jul 2026), four minor versions ahead. Testing whether a current virtiofsd negotiates DEVICE_STATE is the deciding experiment — see mjolnir-3y6.14.
ROOT CAUSE NAILED, and the blocker is Cloud Hypervisor, not virtiofsd.

Upgraded virtiofsd 1.10.0 -> 1.14.0 (cargo install, needs libcap-ng-dev + libseccomp-dev) and re-ran the freeze/thaw. 1.14 DOES implement device state: --migration-mode {find-paths,file-handles}, src/passthrough/device_state/{serialization,deserialization,preserialization}, DEVICE_STATE in its protocol feature list. Its --help even describes this exact hazard: 'Ensure that the migration destination opens the very same inodes as the source'.

With 1.14 the symptom CHANGED but did not go away:
- 1.10.0: vm.restore hangs forever (CH vmm thread blocked in unix_stream_data_wait on the vhost-user socket).
- 1.14.0: vm.restore=204, vm.resume=204, CH logs 'Restoring virtio-pci _fs0 resources' / 'vm restored' / 'Resuming virtio-fs' / 'vm resumed' — and then immediately '<vcpu0> i8042 reset signalled' -> 'VM reset event' -> 'rebooting'. The guest kernel panics on first filesystem access and panic=1 reboot=k reboots it. Marker process frozen at counter=22, then a cold boot.

WHY: CH v50 never transfers vhost-user backend state at all.
- grep -icE 'device.state|migration|GET_DEVICE|SET_DEVICE' over CH's -vvv log: 0 hits.
- The source virtiofsd logged nothing about serializing state.
- state.json's _fs0 snapshot_data holds ONLY front-end virtio state (avail_features, acked_features, config tag) — no FUSE/backend state.

So the destination virtiofsd starts with an empty inode table while the restored guest holds nodeids from the dead source instance. Exactly the predicted hazard; it just surfaces as a guest panic rather than a hang once the backend stops deadlocking.

FIX IS AN UPSTREAM VERSION BUMP, NOT AN ARCHITECTURE FORK. Cloud Hypervisor v52.0 (2025-05-14) release notes: 'Snapshot/restore support for vhost-user devices has been filled out (#7908), including migration support for virtio-fs (#7937).' Upstream issue #6931 'Unable to restore a snapshot of vm using virtiofs root' is the same hang and is closed. We run v50.0.0.

virtio-blk fork is NOT needed. See mjolnir-3y6.15.

title: SECURITY: reseed guest entropy on every resume
description:
Restoring one memory snapshot twice yields two VMs with IDENTICAL RNG state — same session keys, same TLS nonces, same UUIDs. Real key-compromise path. Note the asymmetry: thawing once and discarding is far less exposed than FORKING N VMs from one image, and forking is a feature we want.

CORRECT MECHANISM IS VMGENID: an ACPI device holding a 128-bit generation ID the hypervisor changes on restore. Linux drivers/virt/vmgenid.c (5.18+) sees the change and reseeds the CRNG IN THE KERNEL, before userspace is scheduled. No userspace reseed can provide that property.

Neither half exists today (verified 2026-08-07):
- cloud-hypervisor v50.0.0: no VMGENID strings, not implemented
- /var/lib/mjolnir/vmlinux-ch: no vmgenid/VM_GEN_COUNTER symbols, driver not compiled in
- Mjolnir.CloudHypervisor.Config emits NO virtio-rng device at all (guest kernel does have the virtio_rng driver)

Target: CONFIG_VMGENID in our PVH kernel (cheap, we already build it) + the ACPI device in CH (upstream contribution or patched build). See mjolnir-3y6.11 and mjolnir-3y6.12.

Interim, layered, with the race stated honestly:
1. Add a virtio-rng device (mjolnir-3y6.11) — prerequisite; does not itself force a reseed.
2. Guest-agent reseed via RNDADDENTROPY ioctl on /dev/random, bytes from the host over vsock. Use the ioctl, NOT a write to /dev/urandom — a write mixes but does not credit entropy.
3. Host gates reachability (no PTY, no ticket, no network) until the agent confirms reseed. vCPUs resume all at once so the agent cannot beat userspace; this narrows exposure to processes already inside, not anything an outside caller can induce.

The residual race is unavoidable without VMGENID.
acceptance_criteria: Two VMs restored from the same snapshot produce different output from a key-generation probe. Host refuses to expose a restored VM until reseed is confirmed.
notes:
MECHANISM COMPLETE; NOT CLOSEABLE until mjolnir-3y6.4 exists, because acceptance clause 1 ('two VMs restored from the same snapshot produce different output from a key-generation probe') needs an actual restore path to run against.

Landed (c30f25d, 8ddda26):
- virtio-rng in the vm.create payload (closes the 3y6.12 prerequisite). Every VM until now booted with NO RNG DEVICE AT ALL — the guest kernel has the virtio_rng driver and nothing was giving it a device. Still only a prerequisite: a device supplies entropy but does not force a reseed at any moment.
- Guest agent 'reseed_entropy' op using the RNDADDENTROPY ioctl on /dev/random. NOT a write to /dev/urandom, which mixes but credits zero entropy so the kernel's estimate never moves.
- Answered in BOTH the full and boot vsock listeners. The boot agent rejects everything it does not implement, which for this request would leave a thawed VM permanently unreachable behind its own gate.
- Mjolnir.Entropy: fresh_seed/0 (32 bytes from the host CSPRNG), request/2, reseed/2, interpret/1. Fails closed on every ambiguous answer including ok:true with 0 bytes credited.

ORDERING CORRECTION (8ddda26): the reseed CANNOT precede vm.resume. It is serviced by the guest agent, a userspace process, which cannot run while vCPUs are stopped — a reseed issued against a paused restored VM just hangs. Real sequence: restore -> resume -> reseed -> publish reachability. The gate is on REACHABILITY (no PTY, no ticket, no gateway route), not on execution. MemorySnapshot's moduledoc had this wrong and would have misled whoever built 3y6.4.

VERIFIED on kernel 6.8.0-124: ioctl 0x40085203 is accepted, which a wrong _IOW('R',3,int[2]) encoding would not be.
NOT verified, and do not claim it was: entropy_avail saturates at 256 on modern kernels, reading 256 before and after BOTH a credited ioctl and a plain /dev/urandom write. The mix-vs-credit distinction is documented kernel behaviour, not something measured here.

PORTABILITY TRAP: libc types the ioctl request as c_ulong on glibc and c_int on musl. The agent cross-compiles to x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, so a hard-coded integer type compiles on exactly one of the two. Declared as libc::Ioctl. macOS cargo check cannot see this — it was caught only by building on the server.

REMAINING: the two-thaws-two-keys probe, once 3y6.4 can restore. The residual race (vCPUs resume all at once, so the agent cannot beat in-guest userspace to the first random byte) is unavoidable without VMGENID — mjolnir-3y6.13.
STILL OPEN after mjolnir-3y6.4 lands, and clause 1 of the acceptance is now known to be UNTESTABLE AS WRITTEN.

'Two VMs restored from the same snapshot produce different output from a key-generation probe' presupposes forking N VMs from one memory image. That is not supported and is deliberately REFUSED (verified on the host: {:virtiofsd_socket_in_use, path}). Two thaws want the same virtiofsd socket AND the same vsock CID — both baked into config.json — so the second would attach to the first VM's virtiofsd: one daemon, two guests, each believing it owns the filesystem. Enabling the fork needs per-thaw config.json rewriting plus a CID reallocation whose interaction with the vsock device state in state.json is unproven. Until then the probe has to be 'thaw, reseed, record key; destroy; thaw again, reseed, record key; compare' — sequentially, not concurrently.

Clause 2 ('host refuses to expose a restored VM until reseed is confirmed') is mechanically complete — Entropy.interpret/1 fails closed on every ambiguous answer — but NOT yet wired into the thaw path. MemorySnapshot.thaw/3 deliberately returns a running-but-unreachable VM and logs 'NOT yet reachable: entropy reseed still owed'; nothing calls reseed/2 yet because the reseed rides the guest-agent vsock connection, and whether that connection survives a restore is mjolnir-3y6.6 (open). Wiring it before 3y6.6 would be speculative.

So the real remaining work here is: 3y6.6, then adoption in 3y6.10, then the sequential two-thaw key probe.

title: Atomic disk+memory snapshot with btrfs generation pinning
description:
HAZARD 1 — the correctness keystone. Guest RAM holds a page cache that believes in a specific on-disk state; restore them out of sync and you get silent corruption, not a crash.

FLUSHING IS NOT THE FIX. do_snapshot/3 already runs sync, but sync only writes back DIRTY pages. The hazard is CLEAN cached pages: the guest keeps them and has no reason to re-read. drop_caches does not close it either — it cannot evict mmap'd or in-use pages (every running binary's text pages) and trades correctness for a cold-cache cliff.

THE FIX IS IMMUTABILITY. A stale cache is only wrong if the disk changed. If restore always presents a filesystem byte-identical to what the guest saw at snapshot, every cached page is correct by construction and cache state stops being something anyone reasons about.

Concretely: restore must NEVER point virtiofsd at the live @vms/<uuid>/ subvolume — which is exactly what it does today (--shared-dir=/var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@vms/<uuid>, confirmed on the running host). It must point at a fresh CoW clone of the @snapshots/<name>/ subvolume captured in the same pause window. Memory image + fs snapshot are ONE indivisible artifact.

Record the btrfs subvolume generation (btrfs subvolume show) in metadata and refuse to restore a mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: Restore clones from the pinned snapshot generation and never mounts the live subvolume. Snapshot metadata carries the generation; a drifted subvolume is refused with a clear error rather than booting corrupt.
notes:
MECHANISM COMPLETE AND PROVEN ON THE HOST; NOT CLOSEABLE until mjolnir-3y6.4 wires a restore path, because this bead's acceptance is phrased about what restore does and there is still no restore caller.

Landed (b92eb91, 8ddda26):
- BTRFS.subvolume_generation/1 + parse_generation/1; generation and readonly recorded in the .json sidecar by create_snapshot/3
- create_snapshot/3 :readonly option -> 'btrfs subvolume snapshot -r'. Default OFF: existing cold-boot flows (deploy layers, mj snapshot create) clone from these and some mutate them in place
- BTRFS.verify_generation/1 -> {:snapshot_drifted, name, expected, actual}
- clone_from_snapshot/3 :verify_generation (opt-in; a stale cold boot is survivable, a stale memory restore is not)
- Mjolnir.MemorySnapshot: freeze/3 takes BOTH captures inside one pause window; prepare_thaw/2 returns a fresh CoW clone under a NEW vm id and refuses on drift or on an unrecorded generation
- memory artifacts at @snapshots/<name>.mem, a SIBLING of the subvolume: CH must write config.json/state.json/memory-ranges and nesting them would force the subvolume writable, undoing the -r pin

PROVEN ON 45.76.77.97 (not asserted): a read-only snapshot held generation 207624 across repeated writes to its source subvolume; flipping it writable and appending one line moved it to 207629. So a match is real evidence of 'unchanged' and drift is detectable.

SHARP EDGE the parser test now pins: on a tampered snapshot 'Generation' moves but 'Gen at creation' keeps the ORIGINAL value. A regex matching the wrong line returns the recorded number and waves the tampered snapshot through. Verified against verbatim host output (Generation 207340 vs Gen at creation 111925).

REMAINING for this bead: 3y6.4 must call prepare_thaw/2 and point virtiofsd at the returned clone. Today the running host does --shared-dir=/var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@vms/<id>, i.e. the LIVE subvolume, which is the accident this bead exists to prevent — and it is easy to make, because pointing at the live subvolume is what every other code path correctly does.
PIN REDESIGNED (2dada84) — the Generation-based pin described in my earlier note was WRONG and is replaced.

It broke on its own first legitimate use: creating a clone FROM a read-only snapshot updates that snapshot's root item to list the clone under Snapshot(s), which advances its Generation. Measured on the host — pinned at 208309, read 208311 after ONE successful thaw, so thaw #2 refused with :snapshot_drifted on a filesystem nobody had touched. A pin that reports tampering when nothing was tampered with is worse than no pin because it teaches people to route around it.

The pin is now two facts that are actually invariant under legitimate use:
  1. gen_at_creation — fixed for the life of the subvolume; identifies THIS instance, so a snapshot deleted and recreated under the same name is caught ({:snapshot_replaced, name, expected, actual}).
  2. the readonly flag — a stray write to a read-only subvolume fails EROFS, so ACCIDENTAL drift (the hazard this bead is actually about) is structurally impossible rather than merely unobserved ({:snapshot_not_readonly, name}).
Generation is still recorded, as a diagnostic only.

RESIDUAL GAP, stated in the docs rather than papered over: a privileged operator can 'btrfs property set ro false', edit, and set it back. Not detected. Closing it needs content hashing over a multi-GiB rootfs.

Note an earlier intermediate fix (stable_generation/2, forcing a commit before reading) addressed a REAL but different problem — a generation read immediately after creation can still be the creating transaction's id and tick up by one. That code is gone because gen_at_creation does not have the problem.

ACCEPTANCE NOW DEMONSTRATED via mjolnir-3y6.4: restore clones from the pinned snapshot and virtiofsd serves the CLONE (@vms/thawprobe-thawed), never the live subvolume; a drifted/replaced snapshot is refused with a clear error rather than booting corrupt.
close_reason:
Acceptance demonstrated end-to-end on 45.76.77.97 via the mjolnir-3y6.4 thaw (2dada84).

'Restore clones from the pinned snapshot and never mounts the live subvolume' — proven: virtiofsd served /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@vms/thawprobe-thawed, a fresh CoW clone under a NEW vm id, while the socket path stayed the one config.json recorded. The live @vms/<id> subvolume is never shared. Marker process survived at the same PID (761) with zero reset events, so the restored guest's page cache and its filesystem agreed.

'Metadata carries the pin; a drifted subvolume is refused with a clear error' — met, though NOT with the Generation field the issue proposed. See the note above: Generation advances when anything clones FROM the snapshot, so a Generation pin false-positives on its own first legitimate use (208309 -> 208311 after one thaw). The pin is gen_at_creation + the readonly flag. Verified refusals on the live host: {:snapshot_not_readonly, name} and {:snapshot_replaced, name, 208321, 208325}.

Both captures happen inside one pause window, and the fs snapshot is created with 'btrfs subvolume snapshot -r' so it cannot drift afterwards — an accidental write fails EROFS rather than silently succeeding.

Residual gap, documented not hidden: a privileged operator can flip ro off, edit, flip it back. Undetected. Would need content hashing over a multi-GiB rootfs.

title: VM memory snapshot — real freeze/thaw (CH vm.snapshot/vm.restore)
description:
Mjolnir.VM.snapshot/2 is filesystem-only: do_snapshot/3 (lib/mjolnir/vm.ex:2317) syncs, pauses, btrfs-snapshots the rootfs, and resumes. Guest RAM is never captured, so 'restore' is a cold boot off a snapshotted disk. Mjolnir.CloudHypervisor.Client has no snapshot/restore function at all.

The product claim is checkpointable microVMs. CoW gives cloning; only memory snapshot gives freezing.

VERIFIED ACHIEVABLE on 45.76.77.97: cloud-hypervisor v50.0.0 exports vm.snapshot and vm.restore, and the binary contains 'Restoring vhost-user-fs' — virtio-fs restore is supported in v50, which was the historical blocker.

See docs/plans/vm-memory-snapshot.md for the CH protocol and the seven hazards.
design:
# VM Memory Snapshot — real freeze/thaw

## Status

**Not implemented.** `Mjolnir.VM.snapshot/2` is a *filesystem* snapshot only.

`do_snapshot/3` (`lib/mjolnir/vm.ex:2317`) does:

1. `sync` in the guest (flush page cache to the virtio-fs share)
2. `pause_instance` (CH `vm.pause`) — stops vCPUs so no writes race the snapshot
3. `BTRFS.create_snapshot/3` — CoW subvolume snapshot of the rootfs
4. `resume_instance` (CH `vm.resume`) in an `after` block

Guest RAM is never captured. A "restored" VM is a **cold boot off a snapshotted disk**,
not a resumed process. Everything in memory at snapshot time — running processes, tmux
servers, open sockets, an agent's loaded context, unwritten buffers — is gone.

`Mjolnir.CloudHypervisor.Client` exposes `create/boot/pause/resume/shutdown/delete/info/resize`
and has no `snapshot` or `restore` function at all.

## Why this matters

"Checkpointable microVMs" is the product claim. Filesystem CoW is the *cloning* story;
memory snapshot is the *freezing* story, and only the second one gives you:

- Park an idle agent VM to disk and thaw it mid-thought (the DormantRegistry premise)
- Sub-second cold-start from a warmed snapshot (`mjolnir-5xn`, `mjolnir-gge`)
- Fork a live VM at a decision point
- Survive a host reboot without the guest noticing

## It is achievable

Verified against the deployed hypervisor on 45.76.77.97:

- `cloud-hypervisor v50.0.0`, features `io_uring, kvm, mshv`
- Binary exports `vm.snapshot`, `vm.restore` (alongside `vm.pause` / `vm.resume`)
- Binary contains `Restoring vhost-user-fs` — **virtio-fs restore is supported in v50**,
  which was the blocker in older CH releases and the main risk to this design

## CH protocol

Snapshot (VM must be paused first):

```
PUT /api/v1/vm.pause
PUT /api/v1/vm.snapshot   {"destination_url": "file:///<dir>"}
```

Writes `config.json`, `state.json`, and memory range files into `<dir>`.

Restore requires a **fresh VMM process** — you cannot restore into a booted VM:

```
cloud-hypervisor --api-socket <new.sock>          # do NOT --vm-config
PUT /api/v1/vm.restore    {"source_url": "file:///<dir>", "prefault": false}
PUT /api/v1/vm.resume
```

## The seven hazards

Ordered by how badly they bite.

### 1. Disk/memory atomicity — the correctness keystone

Guest RAM holds a page cache that believes in a specific on-disk state. If the btrfs
subvolume snapshot and the CH memory snapshot are taken at different moments — or if the
subvolume is written after the memory snapshot — you resume a kernel whose cached inodes
disagree with the filesystem. That is silent corruption, not a crash.

Both snapshots must be taken inside a single pause window, and the restore must be
pinned to the exact subvolume generation the memory snapshot was taken against.
Store the btrfs subvolume generation (`btrfs subvolume show`) in the snapshot metadata
and refuse to restore a mismatch.

### 2. virtiofsd lifecycle

The rootfs arrives over vhost-user from a *separate host process*. CH's restore
reconnects to a vhost-user socket; it does not respawn the daemon. So restore ordering is:

1. Recreate/locate the rootfs subvolume at the pinned generation
2. Start `virtiofsd` on the **same socket path** the snapshot recorded
3. Start the new CH process
4. `vm.restore`

If virtiofsd isn't listening, restore fails or the guest wedges on first I/O.

### 3. Entropy reuse — security

Restoring one memory snapshot twice yields two VMs with **identical RNG state**. They will
generate the same session keys, the same TLS nonces, the same UUIDs. This is the classic
VM-snapshot cloning vulnerability and it is a real key-compromise path, not a theoretical one.

Mitigation: reseed at resume — virtio-rng plus an explicit guest-agent
`reseed` op writing fresh entropy to `/dev/urandom` before any userspace unfreezes.
Applies to *every* restore, including the first.

### 4. vsock reconnect

The guest agent holds a live vsock connection in restored RAM and believes it is
connected. The host-side `Mjolnir.Vsock.Connection` GenServer for the old VM is gone.
The CID must be preserved (it is derived from the VM UUID, so it is stable), but both
ends need to renegotiate. Needs an explicit post-restore handshake and a guest-agent
path that detects a dead peer and re-listens rather than hanging.

### 5. Network identity

TAP device, MAC, and IP must be recreated *before* restore and must match exactly what
the guest's in-RAM network stack believes. `Mjolnir.Network` allocation is
hash-deterministic from the VM id, which helps — but the TAP must exist and be up first,
and any host-side NAT/route entries must be re-established.

### 6. Clock jump

The guest wakes believing it is snapshot-time. Certificate validity, agent timeouts,
cron, and log timestamps all skew by the freeze duration. Needs a KVM-clock adjust or a
guest-agent time-sync step on resume, before userspace continues.

### 7. Iroh liveness

The guest's Iroh node has live QUIC connections in restored RAM that are now dead. The
node ID is stable, so tickets survive, but the failure mode is nasty: the VM reports
healthy while nothing can actually reach it. Post-restore health must probe Iroh
reachability, not just guest-agent ping.

## Cost note

A btrfs snapshot is ~free (CoW). A memory snapshot of a 2GB VM is 2GB on disk, every
time. Snapshot storage needs compression (zstd on the btrfs subvolume holding memory
ranges) and a retention policy, or a busy host fills up. This changes the economics of
"snapshot everything" and should inform where memory snapshots are used vs. plain
filesystem snapshots — they are complementary, not a replacement.

## Sequencing

Prove the mechanism before wiring it into the product surface: a paused VM captured and
resumed by hand, with a process that survives the freeze, is the gate. Only then
integrate with DormantRegistry, `mj snapshot`, and the deploy/CI warm-start paths.

Filesystem snapshot stays as its own operation. Memory snapshot is a strictly heavier,
strictly more capable sibling — callers should choose.

title: Deploy/domain endpoints have no policy enforcement (Policy.CoverageTest failing on main)
description: mix test on main fails Mjolnir.Policy.CoverageTest: POST /api/deploy, PUT /api/apps/:app/domain, DELETE /api/apps/:app/domain, GET /api/apps have no policy enforcement and are not whitelisted. Introduced with the deploy/domain work (a5239a8, gge.1.6/12.2). These sit behind Auth so a bearer token is required, but with no per-resource policy any authenticated caller can deploy to or retarget the custom domain of an app they do not own — a multi-tenancy authz hole on the exact surface that points hostnames (e.g. startupcentral.build) at VMs. Fix: add policy enforcement for each endpoint, or explicitly whitelist with justification if they are intentionally control-plane-wide. Note: this failure is the only red test on main and predates the 2026-07-21 health-probe work.
notes:
Raised to P0 on 2026-08-07. The description already names the real severity and it is sharper than 'a failing test': with no per-resource policy, ANY authenticated caller can retarget the custom domain of an app they do not own — on exactly the surface that points hostnames like startupcentral.build at VMs. That is a live multi-tenancy authz hole, not test debt. Also note it masks any NEW policy-coverage regression, since the suite's only red test is already red.
FIXED 2026-08-07 (commit 0f0e20e), deployed and verified.

Root problem was that there was nothing to authorize against: Deploy.Registry entries had no owner. 'deployer' was already threaded to stamp owner_id on the build and service VMs, but never onto the registry entry — the record that outlives any individual VM.

- Registry.Entry gains owner_id (persisted in JSON, read back on load)
- Orchestrator threads deployer -> Runtime.start(:owner_id)
- Runtime.start preserves it across redeploys via preserved_owner_id/2, mirroring custom_domain (Registry.put rebuilds the Entry from attrs, so an omitted key is wiped — a wiped owner would lock the real owner out of their own app)
- New Mjolnir.Policy.App, mirroring Policy.VM clause-for-clause
- Authz.authorize_app/4 + authorize_deploy/3; denials are 404 not 403, matching authorize_vm/4, so tenants' app names cannot be enumerated
- POST /api/deploy checked inside handle_deploy (app name only known after source extraction) and BEFORE send_chunked/2, since a chunked response cannot carry a 403/404 — required splitting the streaming body into do_deploy/6
- GET /api/apps filters via Policy.App.filter_readable/2 then strips owner_id, keeping the documented response shape

Behaviour change: PUT /api/apps/:app/domain on an unknown app now 404s even with an invalid body, because ownership resolves before body validation.

Coverage: 17 policy tests + 10 enforcement tests driving Authz directly with a non-localhost user against a real Registry (router tests all set remote_ip 127.0.0.1 and so run as localhost, bypassing ownership entirely). Verified the coverage test still catches a removed check.

SUITE IS NOW 1091 TESTS, 0 FAILURES — Policy.CoverageTest had been the only red test on main since 2026-07-21.

Verified live after deploy: all three hosted sites 200, API 401s without a token, GET /api/apps returns the documented shape with owner_id stripped.

FOLLOW-UP: the live startup-central entry still has owner_id: null, so it is localhost-only until back-filled — see mjolnir-4tr.

title: SECURITY: gateway must not proxy API to 127.0.0.1 — localhost bypass grants full control-plane scope
description: Mjolnir.API.Auth.localhost_bypass?/1 grants ALL scopes when conn.remote_ip is 127.0.0.1 and :bypass_localhost is true (MJOLNIR_AUTH_BYPASS_LOCALHOST=true in prod /etc/mjolnir/env). If mjolnir-gateway reverse-proxies /api to 127.0.0.1:4000, every proxied request appears to originate from loopback and is granted unauthenticated full admin access from the public internet. Verified NOT currently exposed (worldtree.network, startupcentral.build, mimir all 404 on /api/vms). Mitigation when adding the API route: point the gateway backend at the host's non-loopback IP (10.255.255.1:4000) so remote_ip is not loopback and token auth is enforced. Longer term: move the loopback bypass to a dedicated unix socket or loopback-only listener rather than keying on peer IP of a shared port.
notes:
VERIFIED FIXED 2026-08-07 — closing. The bead's own mitigation is live: /etc/mjolnir/gateway.toml routes api.vm.worldtree.network to 10.255.255.1:4000 (the host's VM-facing address), NOT 127.0.0.1, with a comment recording the reasoning. Confirmed from the public internet just now: GET https://api.vm.worldtree.network/api/vms returns 401 with no token AND with a bogus bearer token. The localhost bypass is not reachable through the gateway.

The longer-term item in the description — move the loopback bypass to a dedicated unix socket or loopback-only listener instead of keying on the peer IP of a shared port — is still worth doing, but it is hardening, not an open exposure. Refiled as mjolnir-3zg.

title: Runtime.start must persist custom_domain across redeploys (currently discards it -> domain wiped on cutover)
description: Deploy.Runtime.start builds registry attrs as %{release_snapshot, service_vm_id, url, port} with NO custom_domain, so registry_put on every deploy OVERWRITES the entry and wipes custom_domain. Result: even with the reconciler path set up, the FIRST redeploy drops the domain. This is the linchpin of redeploy-safety.
design: Thread custom_domain through Runtime.start (read the prior registry entry and preserve custom_domain, or accept it as an opt) so registry_put keeps it. Then Runtime.start's existing RouteReconciler.trigger() re-emits the route with the new vm_id's derived backend automatically. Verify with an actual redeploy: domain keeps serving, no gateway.toml touch.
acceptance_criteria: After 'mj domain set', a full redeploy (new service VM + IP) keeps the app serving at its fqdn with zero manual gateway edits; registry entry retains custom_domain across the cutover.
notes:
CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE (migration 2026-07-20): Runtime.start.finish/9 (runtime.ex:126) builds attrs WITHOUT :custom_domain -> Registry.put/build_entry constructs a fresh Entry with custom_domain=nil and write_atomic overwrites the JSON -> redeploy WIPES custom_domain. Then runtime.ex:134 RouteReconciler.trigger() re-renders, but desired_specs filters on is_binary(custom_domain), so the app no longer qualifies and its route is DROPPED -> app falls off the gateway after ANY redeploy. Backend re-derivation is fine (reconciler computes allocate_ip(vm_id):port from the CURRENT vm_id — verified). FIX (small): in finish/9 read the prior entry's custom_domain (ops.registry_get is already wired at runtime.ex:300) and carry it into attrs. Once fixed, redeploys auto-update the route with no gateway.toml touch. HARD PREREQUISITE for the whole domain epic. LIVE IMPACT: startupcentral.build is on the reconciler path now, so its NEXT redeploy will drop the domain until this ships.
LANDED IN CODE (main, commit 1c0f520): runtime.ex finish/ now carries custom_domain forward via preserved_custom_domain/2 (reads prior entry via ops.registry_get) + start/4 gained an explicit custom_domain: opt for first-time set. 3 tests. NOT yet deployed to server (needs orchestrator redeploy).
STATUS 2026-08-07 — code done, deployed, now properly covered. The note 'NOT yet deployed to server' is stale: three orchestrator deploys shipped today and /opt/mjolnir's runtime.ex contains preserved_custom_domain/2.

Verified on the server:
- deployed release contains preserved_custom_domain/2
- live registry entry /var/lib/mjolnir/deploy/registry/startup-central.json retains custom_domain: 'startupcentral.build'
- gateway_routes_enabled = true; apps.toml carries the apex route (subdomain = "") for startupcentral.build
- the route survived VM spawn + delete lifecycle events (reconciler is content-idempotent, so it correctly wrote nothing)

Test gap closed (commit ac94010): runtime_test.exs stubbed registry_get/put with closures, so it proved Runtime PASSES custom_domain, not that Registry KEEPS it — and the reported failure is exactly that seam (build_entry/2 rebuilds a fresh Entry via Map.get and write_atomic overwrites the JSON). Added 5 tests running real redeploy sequences against a real Registry on a tmp dir, asserting the domain survives in ETS and on disk, including one that models an orchestrator restart by opening a second Registry over the same directory. Verified to fail 6/16 with the bug reintroduced.

REMAINING: the literal acceptance line — 'a full redeploy (new service VM + IP) keeps the app SERVING at its fqdn' — still wants one live redeploy of startup-central. Not done unilaterally: it is a live customer site, and a restart already took it down once today (see mjolnir-1pk). The end-to-end fixture belongs to mjolnir-gge.9.
LIVE REDEPLOY ATTEMPTED 2026-08-07 via 'mj deploy' with a real bearer token. Got three layers deep, uncovering and fixing two genuine bugs, then hit a missing base image:

1. Gateway rejected the upload with 400 'Missing Host header' — extract_host decoded the whole read buffer as UTF-8, and a gzip tarball is not valid UTF-8. Fixed in 77da111.
2. Deploy crashed with 'Adapter functions must be called by stream owner' — on_progress chunked from inside an Agent process. Pre-existing, byte-identical at 0f0e20e^. Fixed in a8cc173.
3. Build VM cannot boot: @base/deploy-node-bun does not exist on the server. See mjolnir-gge.1.10. THIS IS THE CURRENT BLOCKER.

Progress now streams correctly ('[detect] detected bun app (node@20)', '[build] 3 layer(s); building') and ownership is stamped on the build VM (owner_id bfd22745-...), so everything up to the base-image dependency is verified working.

Every failed attempt was non-destructive exactly as Runtime.start intends: the registry entry was untouched and startupcentral.build served 200 with an unchanged homepage sha256 throughout.
ACCEPTANCE MET 2026-08-08 — verified with a real 'mj deploy' over a bearer token, end to end.

  'After mj domain set, a full redeploy (new service VM + IP) keeps the app
   serving at its fqdn with zero manual gateway edits; registry entry retains
   custom_domain across the cutover.'

Evidence after the cutover:
- startupcentral.build -> HTTP 200, three consecutive requests, 47149 bytes
- page intact: <title>Startup Central - Come build with us</title>
- registry retained custom_domain AND owner_id; release_snapshot and service_vm_id both new (67490a98)
- gateway route auto-followed to the new VM's IP: backend = 10.192.112.25:3000, matching the new VM's guest_ip
- ZERO manual gateway edits; the emergency static route had already been removed before this test

Content sha256 changed (d6bb9af8 -> f70f87cf) at identical byte size: SvelteKit regenerates content-addressed asset filenames per build. Expected, not drift.

Getting here required fixing seven other defects first, each hidden behind the one above it — see mjolnir-1pk, mjolnir-do5, mjolnir-xuv, mjolnir-8ie, mjolnir-gge.1.10, mjolnir-7jb, mjolnir-1s9, plus the gateway Host-header and deploy chunk-owner bugs.

title: exec/execute_command use :infinity vsock timeout — wedged guest blocks VM GenServer mailbox
description: VM.exec/3 and execute_command/2 call Vsock.Connection.exec with :infinity. If a guest wedges mid-exec, the call never returns and blocks the VM GenServer mailbox, so subsequent GenServer.call ops (get_state, etc.) time out and the VM shows as :unreachable. VM.reboot/1 already bypasses this via OS-level CH kill (works regardless of mailbox), so recovery is possible — but a bounded exec timeout (or async exec) would prevent the mailbox-block in the first place. Discovered while fixing mjolnir-l4i. Care: long-running CI jobs legitimately need long timeouts, so a fixed short timeout is wrong — consider a generous bound or making exec not block the GenServer.
notes:
REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY 2026-08-07 (during mjolnir-3y6.1 spike). Repro: pause a VM via the CH API long enough to do real work (PUT vm.pause; write a 1GiB vm.snapshot; PUT vm.resume — roughly 10-30s), then call exec.

Causal chain, all four steps confirmed in journalctl:
1. The long pause SEVERS the host<->guest-agent vsock connection.
2. The guest agent does not re-establish it on resume. Health.Monitor logs 'guest-agent unreachable over vsock but VM is TCP-live; attempting L1 vsock heal'.
3. The next exec hits lib/mjolnir/vm.ex:2161 Connection.exec(state.vsock_conn, command, :infinity) and blocks the VM GenServer mailbox forever.
4. Permanently wedged: 'GenServer unreachable (call timed out); skipping probe this tick' every 35s thereafter, never recovering. As monitor.ex:122-128 already notes, no heal path can help because they all go through the same GenServer.

This now BLOCKS mjolnir-3y6 (memory snapshot): the freeze pause window is inherently long — it writes RAM to disk — so every freeze would wedge the VM under current code. The generous-bound fix contemplated in the original description is the right one; combine with mjolnir-3y6.6 (vsock re-establishment after pause/restore).
FIXED 2026-08-07 (commits 7a6add3, 0cac24b), deployed and verified on 45.76.77.97.

Two compounding defects, both addressed:
1. VM.exec/3 applied its :timeout to the outer GenServer.call but passed :infinity to the inner Vsock.Connection.exec — so the caller exited on timeout while the GenServer stayed blocked forever. Even Health.GuestNetwork's careful timeout: 8_000 wedged the VM. The timeout is now threaded to the vsock request itself, defaulting to a bounded 15 minutes (:infinity still available explicitly, and the API exec endpoint keeps it, per the original note that CI needs long timeouts).
2. handle_call({:exec, ...}) ran the round-trip inline, blocking the MAILBOX. It now hands the round-trip to an unlinked Task and answers via GenServer.reply, so the caller blocks exactly as before while status/health/stop keep being served. Nothing in the clause mutates state and Connection multiplexes by request id, so no serialization was lost.

Verified against the real failure mode on the server: after a pause long enough to sever the guest-agent vsock, exec now returns a bounded error (20s) instead of hanging, GET /api/vms/:id answers 'running', and DELETE succeeds — all of which previously failed permanently, recoverable only via /reboot. A follow-up run polled reachability 12/12 over 60s.

6 regression tests in test/mjolnir/vm_exec_nonblocking_test.exs, verified to FAIL 4/6 against the old inline implementation before being committed against the fix.

NOT fully closed as a class: other handle_call clauses still do inline vsock work (health probes, terminal_*, reconfigure_*). Those are bounded (~10s) so they block transiently rather than permanently — tracked as mjolnir-75d.

title: Health.nuke/1: snapshot-before-destroy with rollback on respawn failure
description: nuke currently deletes subvolume+record then respawns; a transient respawn failure loses everything. Take a recovery btrfs snapshot before teardown, and on respawn failure restore the subvolume + re-persist the StateStore record. Finding 1.
close_reason: nuke now moves rootfs to @trash before teardown and restores + re-persists the intent record on respawn failure (rollback_nuke). Docstrings updated.

title: Soft-delete BTRFS subvolumes (trash + delayed GC) instead of hard delete
description: Add BTRFS.trash_subvolume/1 that renames a VM subvolume into @trash/<uuid>__<ts>/ (O(1) within the same filesystem) and BTRFS.reap_trash/1 that hard-deletes trash older than a retention window. Route ALL inline destructive callers through trash: vm.ex cleanup_partial_boot, cloud_hypervisor.ex cleanup/1, cleanup.ex orphan sweep. Finding 2. This is the structural fix: no inline path can cause irreversible loss.

title: VM durability: make 'disappeared forever' structurally impossible
description: A user VM (1GB) OOM'd during a build; the recovery reboot hit a transient virtiofsd resource error and the VM's BTRFS subvolume + StateStore record were permanently deleted. Root cause: multiple code paths hard-delete the rootfs subvolume (the source of truth for a VM's data), and one path (Health.nuke/1) deletes BEFORE confirming a replacement can be built. This epic hardens every destruction path so a transient failure can never cause permanent data loss.

title: inject_guest_agent is a silent no-op when guest_agent_bin is missing
description:
`config/prod.exs` sets `guest_agent_bin` to `/opt/mjolnir/native/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/mjolnir-agent`. That file does not exist on 45.76.77.97.

`Mjolnir.VM.inject_guest_agent/1` only copies when the path exists; otherwise it returns `:ok` with no log (`rescue` also swallows copy failures as a warning, but the missing-path branch never logs). Every clone therefore keeps whatever the *image* baked in.

Identikey 2026-08-27: ubuntu-24.04 boots (June 23 agent present) but managed-secrets unlock timed out at ~60s. Copying the current agent from the taskmaster VM (Aug 22, md5 `8c3e7794…`) onto the release snapshot made Runtime.start succeed. Injection was supposed to be that copy.

0e8 already said this was worth an explicit warn or a doctor check. Still unfixed. bhcr (live deploy-node-bun has the unit and no binary) is the same miss on the default *deploy* image — injection would have papered over the missing binary if the host path existed.

Fix the log, the doctor check, and put a real current `mjolnir-agent` at the configured path (or change the path to one that exists). Rebuilding images is not a substitute: even ubuntu-24.04's baked agent is too old for managed unlock.
acceptance_criteria:
- If `:guest_agent_bin` is nil or the path does not exist, spawn logs a warning that names the configured path (or that it is unset). No more silent `:ok`.
- `mj doctor` (host, no VM) reports the same: configured path missing, or unset while a default deploy image relies on injection.
- A clone of `@base/ubuntu-24.04` spawned with `secrets_mode: :managed` unlocks within the 90s managed-boot timeout *without* hand-copying an agent into the snapshot (once a current binary is at the configured path).

title: Live @base/deploy-node-bun has unit but no mjolnir-agent binary; mj deploy dies at 30s vsock ping
description:
The 30s number is `Mjolnir.VM.@default_await_boot_timeout` (30_000). `spawn/1` `GenServer.call`s `:await_boot` until the guest agent answers vsock. It is not a cargo/build deadline. `:managed` secrets already raise this to 90s because LUKS runs during `do_boot`. Builder/Orchestrator do not pass `:await_boot_timeout`, so every `mj deploy` build VM inherits 30s.

That timeout is a *deadline for a vsock ping*, not a slow-boot allowance. On 2026-08-27 the identikey OP deploy (`mj deploy . --name identikey`) never got that ping from `deploy-node-bun`. Raising the timeout would only wait longer.

## What actually failed

`Orchestrator` default `base_image` is `deploy-node-bun` (gge.1.10). Live image on 45.76.77.97:

- Built 2026-08-07 23:19 (stat on the subvolume).
- Has `/etc/systemd/system/mjolnir-agent.service` (`ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent`, `WantedBy=basic.target`, `Restart=on-failure`, `StartLimitBurst=3`).
- **Does not have** `/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent` (ls: No such file).
- `basic.target.wants/mjolnir-agent.service` is linked.

systemd starts the unit, exec fails, burst-limit, vsock never answers. Host log: TAP created, virtiofsd started, **never** `Guest network configured`. ~30s later `GenServer.call ... :await_boot, 30000` EXIT timeout → HTTP 500 `spawn_failed`. Same for a plain `mj spawn --base deploy-node-bun --memory 512` with no extra mounts.

Contrast, same host, same minute: `mj spawn` default `ubuntu-24.04` reached PTY-ready in ~5s. That image **has** the binary (`/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent`, dated 2026-06-23). identikey therefore built with rpc `base_image: "ubuntu-24.04"`.

## Injection is still a silent no-op (0e8 comment)

`config/prod.exs` sets `guest_agent_bin` to `/opt/mjolnir/native/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/mjolnir-agent`. That file **does not exist** on the host. `inject_guest_agent/1` only copies when the path exists; otherwise it returns `:ok` with no log. Clone of deploy-node-bun therefore still has no binary. 0e8 already named this.

## Relation to closed mjolnir-0e8

0e8 (closed 2026-08-12, 522b3b8) fixed the *builder scripts*: `scripts/lib/guest-agent.sh` `install_guest_agent` now installs binary + unit + symlink and fails the image build if any are missing. `build-deploy-base.sh` even comments that the first build of this image failed exactly this way.

The **live** `@base/deploy-node-bun` was never rebuilt after that fix. It still matches the pre-0e8 "unit only, binary supposed to be injected" shape. Script ≠ image.

Verified spawn of a *fresh* image in 0e8 used `@base/ci-test`, then deleted it. `just build-deploy-base` was never run against the live deploy image.

## What is not the bug

- Extra virtiofs `src` mount: ubuntu-24.04 with `extra_mounts` + 2048 MB **did** boot and compile identikey-server. deploy-node-bun failed *without* extra mounts too.
- Cargo duration: the build VM never started the first step.
- `serial-getty@ttyS0` 90s wait (seen on an ubuntu *service* snapshot) is a separate boot-hang; not this 30s vsock miss.

## Fix (rebuild, then make the miss noisy)

1. Rebuild `@base/deploy-node-bun` with current `scripts/build-deploy-base.sh` (post-0e8 `install_guest_agent`). Confirm the binary is in the image before cutting `mj deploy` back to this default.
2. `mj doctor` (host, no VM id): fail or warn if default deploy base has the unit and no binary, and if `:guest_agent_bin` is set to a missing path.
3. `inject_guest_agent/1`: log a warning when the configured path is missing instead of silent `:ok` (already noted on 0e8, still unfixed).

Until (1), `mj deploy` of any app that is not already a cache-hit on an older layer will 500 at detect/build spawn.
acceptance_criteria:
- `test -x /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@base/deploy-node-bun/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent` is true on the prod host.
- `mj spawn --base deploy-node-bun --memory 512` reaches state=running (guest network configured, vsock exec works) well under 30s.
- `mj deploy` of a tiny mjolnir.toml app boots a build VM from that image without `:boot_timeout`.
- `mj doctor` (or spawn logs) names a missing guest-agent binary instead of a bare `:boot_timeout` / HTTP 500 when the image or `:guest_agent_bin` is broken.

title: ADR + spec: Redis sidecar bind, AOF, AUTH
description:
Architecture node. Pins the sidecar.

## Decisions to lock
- systemd unit (blob-door pattern), not OTP Port (postgres pattern). BEAM restart must not kill Redis.
- Bind :host_api_ip:6379 only. Fail closed if dummy missing. Never 0.0.0.0.
- requirepass (or ACL user). Password in deploy secrets as REDIS_URL=redis://:pass@10.200.0.1:6379/0. Merge like Tenants.ensure, do not wipe other keys.
- Durability: appendonly yes, appendfsync everysec, dir /var/lib/mjolnir/redis. RDB as extra snapshot. everysec = up to 1s loss on crash — name it.
- INPUT 10.192.0.0/10 → 10.200.0.1:6379 (same trap as 5432/7222).
- v1 is not a hotel: one process, one password. No Redis SELECT-as-tenant. No second instance.
- Rename/ACL-deny FLUSHALL, FLUSHDB, DEBUG, CONFIG from the guest user.
- Ride just deploy / deploy.sh; restart Redis only when binary or redis.conf changed.
- First consumer: Hypersigil Medusa (sessions via connect-redis, plus cache / event-bus / locking / BullMQ if they enable those modules). Wiring medusa-config.ts is the app repo.

Capability host-redis. ADR next number (0006). Amend host-sidecars.md.

title: Guest peek/ack protocol; vsock ACK stays a hint
description:
## Why

Guest drain is destructive (agent.rs handle_messages drain). DeliverMessageAck means RAM VecDeque only. App crash between GET and process loses the only copy even after host durability.

## What

Peek-then-ack on guest HTTP inbox. ack_messages over vsock. Host tombstones @mail/<vm_id>/acked/. Depends on durable accept.

## Acceptance
- [ ] GET does not delete host mail
- [ ] Host deletes/tombstones only on application ACK
- [ ] DeliverMessageAck never removes the file

title: Mailbox durable accept: JSON-per-id + fsync-before-200
description:
## Why

The architecture node. Unify three queues (running cast, booting GenServer list, dormant pending_messages) into Mjolnir.Mailbox. 200 only after tmp+rename+fsync. Filename is message_id.

## What

openspec change add-mailbox-durable-accept (architecture, human-gate). Copy Forge.Store write path, not DormantRegistry File.write. Startup sweep of unacked mail. Delete retry_deliver_message, :restoring reject, finish_boot drain loop.

Decide: Admit at POST (4xx, Tatastu-correct) vs at delivery.

## Acceptance
- [ ] ADR + change with contract: POST body id, 200 {ok, message_id, status queued|duplicate}
- [ ] Non-200/timeout => producer retries same id
- [ ] Host crash after 200 still has the file
close_reason: Host Mailbox spool landed in act

title: Retry-safe host mailbox (durable accept + app ACK)
description:
## Why

Tatastu POSTs a turn and the laptop may close. Today POST /api/vms/:id/messages is a best-effort wakeup channel whose 200 is not durable accept, and running/booting/dormant have different semantics. Guest-only runId dedupe cannot resurrect a drop. A per-workspace front-proxy VM does not fix this (it is wake-policy, and cannot honestly 200 without host disk).

## What

Host durable mailbox: JSON-per-message under @mail/<vm_id>/<message_id>.json, Forge.Store tmp+rename+fsync before 200. Producer id is the filename. Delivery loop independent of VM state. Delete only on guest application ACK. Unify/delete the three ad-hoc queues.

Fable consult 2026-08-21; memory key mailbox-retry-safe.

## Acceptance
- [ ] 200 means the message file is fsynced; producer may forget
- [ ] Same message_id retried is a no-op (queued or tombstoned), never a second turn
- [ ] Running, booting, and dormant share one queue
- [ ] Host crash + guest crash + signal_done-during-accept do not drop an accepted message
- [ ] Vsock DeliverMessageAck never deletes mail
notes: Act landed (host spool + guest peek/ack). Fold next. 5le4.3 still open for accept-during-done integration test on KVM.

title: Prove guest PUT/GET through the door
description:
Live proof that a guest can use the door, and that B2 is still the copy that counts.

## Proofs
1. Spawn a VM from ubuntu-24.04. From inside: PUT bytes whose Blake3-base58 is H, GET H, bytes match. Re-PUT same bytes → 200, no extra B2 version. PUT under the wrong hash → 400, H not created.
2. From a second guest, GET H succeeds (door is host-wide, not per-VM).
3. Stop the door unit. Host-side HeadObject/GET of `blob/b3/H` on B2 still returns the bytes. Guest GET may 502 — that is availability, not data loss.
4. Guest has no `B2_*` in env or files. `ss` on the host still shows bind only on 10.200.0.1:7222.

Needs KVM + the live host. Tag as integration if it becomes an ExUnit case.
acceptance_criteria: From a guest: PUT then GET match; mismatch refused; re-PUT no extra B2 version. After door stop, B2 still has the object. Second guest can GET the same hash.
close_reason: Guest PUT/GET, second guest GET, reput 200, mismatch 400, B2 cat after door stop.

title: Inject blob_door_url into guests
description:
Tell each guest where the door is.

## Why
`configure_identity` already writes `/etc/mjolnir/vm.json` with `vm_id` + `api_url` (`http://10.200.0.1:4000`). Without `blob_door_url`, every guest has to guess.

## Do
- Extend vsock `configure_identity` (host protocol + guest agent) with `blob_door_url` (e.g. `http://10.200.0.1:7222`).
- Guest writes it into `/etc/mjolnir/vm.json` next to `api_url`.
- Re-inject every boot (tmpfs / identity file can lag a resume).
- Never put `B2_*` in the guest. Never put the door URL on the public gateway.
- Guest-agent change needs `just deploy --agent` before a live body sees the field.

## Use from the VM
```
h=$(python3 -c 'import hashlib,sys,base64; ...')  # or b3sum + base58
curl -sS -X PUT --data-binary @file \
  -H 'content-type: application/octet-stream' \
  "$BLOB_DOOR_URL/storage/blob/b3/$h"
curl -sS "$BLOB_DOOR_URL/storage/blob/b3/$h" -o out
```
Door hashes; mismatch → 400. Same bytes again → 200 no extra B2 version. 64 MiB RAM cap until streaming lands.

title: Deploy blob door on 10.200.0.1:7222
description:
Stand mjolnir-blob-door on the Mjolnir host so guests can reach it.

## Why
The crate and systemd unit exist. The process does not. Default bind is loopback; TAP guests cannot hit 127.0.0.1 on the host.

## Do
- Cross-build on the Linux host (`cargo build -p mjolnir-blob-door --release` in `native/`). Recrypt-core is not required; this crate is aws-sdk-s3 + blake3 + axum.
- Install `/opt/mjolnir/bin/mjolnir-blob-door` + `systemd/mjolnir-blob-door.service`.
- `/etc/mjolnir/blob-door.env`: `BLOB_DOOR_BIND=10.200.0.1:7222`, `BLOB_DOOR_ALLOW_NONLOCAL=1`, `BLOB_DOOR_BACKEND=b2`, B2 endpoint/bucket/key. Application key: read/write, **not** delete. Versioning on the bucket out of band.
- INPUT allow `10.192.0.0/10` → `10.200.0.1:7222` (UFW, same comment shape as tenant Postgres 5432). Guest TCP to the dummy is INPUT, not FORWARD.
- Bind only `:host_api_ip`. Fail closed if that address is missing. Never `0.0.0.0`, never the public NIC.
- `just` recipe: build+install+restart the unit without restarting Elixir (Elixir restart bounces every VM).
- Host `curl http://10.200.0.1:7222/health` → ok. `ss -lntp` shows 10.200.0.1:7222 only.

## Inherited
dummy-mjolnir already has 10.200.0.1/32. Do not invent a second overlay IP.

title: Blob door: deploy + guest overlay (not MinIO)
description:
Blob door remaining work. ADR 0003 + add-blob-store/api/client already folded (2026-08-17).

## Already true
- Address is Blake3, layout recrypt `blob/b3/{base58}` + optional `.obao`.
- Canonical copy is B2, ack after HeadObject/GET. No ILM, no guest snapshot as backup.
- Door crate is `native/mjolnir_blob_door` (HTTP PUT/GET/HEAD on `/storage/blob/b3/{hash}`).
- We are not doing MinIO — not v1, not a cache, not a later landing.
- Taskmaster client exists; SQLite holds hashes; `BLOB_DOOR_URL` fail-closed; no `B2_*` in the app.

## Not true yet
- Door is not installed on 45.76.77.97 (no binary, no env, nothing on :7222).
- Door default bind is `127.0.0.1:7222`. Guests cannot reach host loopback.
- Guest overlay already has `:host_api_ip` `10.200.0.1` on `dummy-mjolnir` (tenant Postgres is `10.200.0.1:5432`, UFW INPUT from `10.192.0.0/10`). Blob door is not on that address.
- Guests are not told a door URL (`/etc/mjolnir/vm.json` has `api_url` only).

## How a VM uses it (target)
Guest HTTP to `http://10.200.0.1:7222/storage/blob/b3/{hash}` (same overlay as tenant Postgres). No B2 keys in the guest. `deliver_message` is not the large-blob path (16 MiB cap). iroh-blobs is later transmit, not the archive.

## Non-goals of this epic
MinIO. iroh-blobs as archive. Encryption (add-encrypt-blobs). recrypt-server `/files`. Streaming above the door's 64 MiB RAM cap.
design: Reuse the host-sidecar-tenant overlay: bind 10.200.0.1:7222 (not 0.0.0.0, not public NIC, not lo). BLOB_DOOR_ALLOW_NONLOCAL=1 is the hatch the binary already has. INPUT TAP→7222 same shape as UFW rule for 5432. Inject blob_door_url next to api_url. Sites.Storage.Recrypt already speaks these routes — cutover is a URL, not a new door.

title: GET /api/certs 500: System.tmp_dir! under ProtectSystem=strict
description:
GET /api/certs (and therefore mj cert ls) crashes on the live host with RuntimeError: could not get a writable temporary directory.

Cause: Mjolnir.Gateway.Certs.with_tmp/2 calls System.tmp_dir!() which wants /tmp. mjolnir.service has ProtectSystem=strict and ReadWritePaths includes /tmp/mjolnir but not /tmp. The raise is uncaught, so the router never reaches its {:error, _} 500 JSON path — Bandit closes the connection with an empty body.

Discovered 2026-08-16 immediately after deploying dd345f8 (HTTP-01 cert API). Issue path uses systemd-run as uid=mjolnir to dodge the same sandbox; list() does not.

Fix options (pick one):
1. Point with_tmp at Path.join("/tmp/mjolnir", ...) or Application.get_env(:mjolnir, :socket_dir)
2. Set TMPDIR=/tmp/mjolnir in systemd/mjolnir.service Environment=
3. Parse cert metadata without writing a temp PEM (openssl -inform PEM on stdin)

Do not add /tmp to ReadWritePaths. Do not add ReadWritePaths for /var/lib/mjolnir-gateway (that restarts the BEAM and kills VMs — already called out in API.Certs).

Reproduce: ssh root@45.76.77.97 'curl -sS -D - localhost:4000/api/certs'
Journal: journalctl -u mjolnir | grep tmp_dir
