title: Per-tenant BTRFS subvolume trees + qgroup quota
description:
Pure refactor, no crypto. Immediately useful.

btrfs.ex:111 hardcodes <btrfs_root>/@snapshots/<name>. Make the tenant prefix a
PARAMETER of create_snapshot/clone_from_snapshot rather than a constant.

## Target layout

  <btrfs_root>/
  |-- @base/                       shared, plaintext, Blake3-verified (unchanged)
  |-- @tenants/<identikey_fp58>/
  |   |-- vms/<vm_uuid>/
  |   |-- snapshots/<name>/  + <name>.json  + <name>.mem/
  |   `-- data/<vm_uuid>.img       LUKS2, DEK wrapped to <identikey_fp>
  `-- @trash/                      unchanged

## Buys three things at once

1. Namespace isolation — no collisions; no enumeration leak (today the
   {:snapshot_exists, name} error tells tenant B that tenant A holds that name).
2. Quota — btrfs qgroup applies naturally per tenant subtree.
3. Replication unit — send a tenant's tree, not the host's.

## Migration

Existing flat snapshots have owner_id: nil. policy/snapshot.ex:32 already denies
those to non-localhost users, so they are already inert for tenants — adopt into
@tenants/_system/ or leave in place behind a legacy read path. Do NOT silently
reassign them to a tenant.

## Open

- Path component: identikey_fp (self-describing, breaks if binding changes) vs a
  stable internal tenant UUID?
- Quota enforcement: btrfs qgroup (kernel, hard) vs app-level accounting
  (flexible, bypassable)?

title: Identity binding: OIDC sub -> IdentiKey fingerprint
description:
Everything else in mjolnir-k8y depends on this.

owner_id today is the Keycloak `sub` — an identifier the SERVER assigns. An
IdentiKey fingerprint (sites/identikey.ex: Blake3 of the Ed25519 pubkey,
base58) is derived from a key the USER holds. Encryption-to-user-key needs the
second. Nothing connects them.

## Work

- Enrollment: at first login the user proves possession of their IdentiKey;
  server records a SIGNED `sub -> identikey_fp` binding in SecretStore.
- Keep the two identifiers doing different jobs:
    owner_id (sub)  = authz key. Cheap string compare in policy/*.ex, no crypto
                      in the hot path. NOTHING in policy/{vm,snapshot}.ex changes.
    identikey_fp    = encryption key. Every DEK-wrap and storage-path decision.
- Resolve/lookup helper both directions, cached.

## Blocked on / notes

SecretStore signature verification is STUBBED (secret_store.ex verify_envelope/2)
pending the recrypt Rust integration. A binding record we cannot verify is
security theatre — either wire verification first or make the stub loud and the
binding provisional.

## Open

Key rotation: rotating an IdentiKey requires re-wrapping every DEK. Loss/
recovery path — does offering one violate the exit test (epic sec.6)?

comments.author: Duke Jones
comments.text: STALE AS WRITTEN. ADR-001 in identikey-core: sub is a XID (hash of the inception key), not a Keycloak sub bound to a current-key fingerprint. Fingerprint-as-subject makes PQ rotation an identity break. Mjolnir as a capability-aware RP should take disclosed-mode XID as owner_id once identikey-oidc exists. Keycloak connect.identikey.io is the OIDC stand-in only. Do not implement a binding table from Keycloak sub to fingerprint as the load-bearing identity.

title: [epic] Multi-tenant Mjolnir: per-tenant encrypted snapshots, replicable across hosts
description:
Design: docs/plans/initiatives/multi-tenant-snapshots.md (2026-08-13)

Make every VM and snapshot belong to an IdentiKey-rooted account, encrypt
tenant state so the host operator cannot read it, and let a user's VM come up
on any host in the fleet.

## Already true (do not rebuild)

- owner_id end-to-end: api/router.ex:277 stamps from authenticated sub;
  vm.ex:1044 persists; authz.ex + policy/{vm,snapshot}.ex enforce owner-equality
  and filter list endpoints. mjolnir-gge.1.9 closed with 'owner_id ALREADY
  flowed correctly'.
- Snapshot owner metadata: btrfs.ex:create_snapshot/3 writes owner_id sidecar.
- policy/snapshot.ex:32 already denies legacy (owner_id: nil) to non-localhost.
- Per-VM LUKS, two modes (vm.ex:42-44): :managed (host escrows passphrase,
  re-injects on boot/wake, NOT zero-knowledge) and :persistent (passphrase held
  by remote Iroh peer, refuses dormancy). :persistent is already ~80% of
  'encrypted to the user's key'.
- SecretEscrow lives OUTSIDE btrfs_root, so btrfs subvolume snapshot never
  captures passphrases.
- IdentiKey Ed25519 + Blake3/base58 fingerprints (sites/identikey.ex);
  IdentiKey-rooted keyspace (secret_store.ex) — signature verify STUBBED.
- Biscuit capability design written (docs/plans/rbac-design.md), not built.

## The four gaps

1. @snapshots/ is a FLAT global namespace (btrfs.ex:111 hardcodes the path).
   Collisions across tenants; the {:snapshot_exists, name} error leaks
   existence; isolation is advisory JSON checked only at the API layer.
2. owner_id is a Keycloak sub (server-assigned), NOT an IdentiKey fingerprint
   (user-held). Encryption-to-user-key needs the latter. Nothing binds them.
3. Memory snapshots write PLAINTEXT guest RAM to @snapshots/<name>.mem
   (memory_snapshot.ex:98). For a LUKS-unlocked VM that includes the dm-crypt
   DEK. Silent, total bypass of the tier-3 design under multi-tenancy.
4. No node identity, placement registry, or cross-host replication.

## The encryption boundary (the one real decision)

Do NOT encrypt whole snapshots to the user's key. Ciphertext is high-entropy:
dedup and compression die, reflink cloning stops working, @base goes from 7.5G
shared to 7.5G PER TENANT — and it protects nothing, because the base OS is
public Ubuntu whose integrity matters, not its confidentiality.

Keep the three-tier model:
  Tier 1 @base       plaintext, Blake3-verified + signed  (shared reflink)
  Tier 2 virtio-fs   plaintext                            (CoW dedup)
  Tier 3 LUKS2       DEK wrapped to owner's IdentiKey     (tenant data)

'Encrypted to each user's key' = tier 3 grows to hold everything
tenant-specific. PRE (recrypt/OpenFHE BFV) wraps the DEK so the host can
re-encrypt it to a VM's ephemeral key without seeing plaintext — that is what
makes fleet placement compatible with host-opaque encryption.

## Exit test (Duke's revenue protocol)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, tested not asserted: a user holding their IdentiKey can
take a raw btrfs send stream of their tenant subtree off Mjolnir entirely and
decrypt their tier-3 volumes with no server participation.

## Order

1. Identity binding (sub -> identikey_fp)   [everything depends on it]
2. Per-tenant subvolume trees + qgroup      [pure refactor, no crypto]
3. Memory-snapshot key handling             [luksSuspend — see child]
4. DEK wrapping via recrypt PRE             [Rust integration; shares mjolnir-9bq.5]
5. Biscuit capabilities (rbac Phase 1)      [unlocks sharing]
6. btrfs send replication + placement       [multi-node payoff]

Steps 1-3 buy real isolation with no Rust integration.

Related: mjolnir-qwp (btrfs send -> B2), mjolnir-8m3 (identity remapping),
mjolnir-6fn (libcluster), mjolnir-9bq.5 (keyspace/recipients via PRE).

title: Off-box durability for BTRFS snapshots: btrfs send/receive → B2
description:
@snapshots/ (14G) and @base/ (7.5G) on 45.76.77.97 have ZERO off-box backup.
Single /dev/sda, no RAID. Disk loss = every VM checkpoint gone permanently.

## Current state (verified 2026-08-13)

Only thing leaving the box is b2:mimir-backups/forgejo (forgejo-backup.timer)
and, as of now, b2:mimir-backups/mjolnir-sites (mjolnir-sites-backup.timer,
installed this session — 10.8 MiB, rclone copy, append-only).

Unprotected:
  @snapshots/  14G  — named checkpoints (startup-central-r1, deploy-*),
                      dormant-VM snapshots. NOT rebuildable.
  @base/      7.5G  — arch, ubuntu-24.04, ci-ubuntu-24.04, buzz-agent,
                      deploy-node-bun. Rebuildable from scripts, slowly.
  @vms/             — live VM state.

## Why plain rclone is the wrong tool here

BTRFS snapshots share extents via CoW; the 14G figure double-counts shared
blocks. A file-level sync uploads full expanded size and re-uploads nightly.
Worse, it cannot reconstruct subvolume structure — restore yields a directory
tree, not a snapshot you can `mj spawn` from.

## Approach

`btrfs send -p <parent> <snap>` streams only changed extents. Snapshots are
already created read-only (send requires ro), so this runs against live VMs
with no quiescing and no pause.

Design work needed:
  1. Parent lineage tracking — an incremental chain is order-dependent; one
     missing link makes every later increment unrestorable. Need a manifest of
     which parent each stream was cut against.
  2. Periodic full re-anchor so chain depth stays bounded.
  3. Transport: `btrfs send ... | zstd | rclone rcat b2:...` vs staging to
     disk first (staging needs headroom; rcat has no resume on failure).
  4. Retention/GC policy on the B2 side.
  5. Restore drill — a backup that has never been restored is a hypothesis.
     Acceptance: restore a snapshot from B2 onto a clean host and boot it.

## Notes

- rclone remote `b2:` is native-B2 (type=b2), NOT the S3 API. recrypt-storage's
  aws_sdk_s3 backend would need a separate S3-compatible app key against B2's
  S3 endpoint. Different credential.
- hard_delete=false on the remote, so overwrites retain prior versions.
- Prior art sketched in docs/plans/initramfs-verified-boot.md (send/receive
  over ssh) and docs/plans/initiatives/mjolnir-sovereignty-vision.md
  (cross-node replication) — both future-facing, neither implemented.

title: mjolnir.toml manifest: explicit escape hatch for undetectable stacks
