title: Managed-secrets app unit never starts after a VM restart
description:
ConditionPathIsMountPoint=/secrets is evaluated when systemd reaches multi-user.target, which happens long before the HOST connects over vsock and sends inject_secrets. So on every VM reboot/resume the condition is false, systemd skips the unit, and nothing ever re-triggers it: the app stays down permanently.

This is fail-closed (no plaintext leak) but also fail-permanent. Before the condition existed the same race made the app start WITHOUT its secrets env - silently misconfigured rather than down.

Fix: after a successful mount + load_env_vars, the guest agent should ask systemd to start the app unit. The guest agent currently shells out to systemctl nowhere at all (grep: zero hits), so this is a new capability.

Acceptance: reboot a managed-secrets service VM; the app is running with its secrets env after the unlock completes, and is NOT running before it.
close_reason: Fixed in 6a6c59b; verified live on 45.76.77.97 — app restarts with secrets after reboot, and a hand-start with the volume closed is still skipped by the condition

title: Managed secrets unlock times out on RESUME but succeeds on a fresh spawn — VM 2da0e442 has never had /run/mjolnir
description:
VM 2da0e442-730c-4926-a6c7-4ff316a98e96 (the host's only secrets_mode: managed VM) fails its LUKS unlock with :timeout on every restart. Observed on the deploys of 2026-08-12 21:20:23 UTC and 2026-08-13 02:07:26 UTC. It reaches state=running and serves fine, but /run/mjolnir is never mounted, so any secret the VM expects is simply absent.

ISOLATED 2026-08-13 while verifying mjolnir-y32. A freshly spawned managed VM unlocks in about TWO SECONDS:
  POST /api/vms {secrets_mode: managed} -> booting at t+2s, running at t+4s, secrets_unlock_failed: null
Two independent fresh spawns (b963019b, eee77f62) both succeeded immediately. So the 60s bound is not too tight and cryptsetup is not slow — the RESUME path specifically hangs.

The likely difference is in maybe_unlock_secrets/2: SecretEscrow.get_or_create returns origin :created on first boot and :existing on resume. On :created we send the entries and the guest runs dd + luksFormat + mkfs. On :existing we send no entries and the guest is expected to luksOpen the snapshot-carried ciphertext volume. Only the second shape times out, which points at the guest-side open path (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/secrets.rs), not the host.

Worth checking whether that VM's volume ever existed. It has failed every restart we have logs for, so it may never have been created successfully — in which case the guest is being asked to open a volume that is not there and hangs rather than erroring.

VISIBILITY IS ALREADY GOOD: mjolnir-3v2 surfaces this as secrets_unlock_failed on GET /api/vms/:id, which is how it was caught at all. This issue is the underlying failure, not its reporting.

RELATED: nothing retries the unlock. A VM that fails it stays without secrets until someone acts. Deliberately out of scope for y32 — Health.Monitor must not retry it on a 30s tick (see the mjolnir-3v2 note on keeping the flag out of checks/overall).
acceptance_criteria: A restart of 2da0e442 completes with secrets_unlock_failed: null and /run/mjolnir mounted inside the guest.
close_reason:
Root cause was NOT cryptsetup and not the resume path in the guest. maybe_inject_guest_agent/2 skipped guest-agent injection whenever resume_mode was true, so VM 2da0e442 was still running its 2026-06-23 agent on 2026-08-13 — one that predates the inject_secrets action. The LUKS volume never existed; there was never anything to reopen.

Fixed in 225a007 (inject on resume) plus a guest-side typed error response so an unparseable request stops presenting as a 60s timeout.

VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION, deploy 2026-08-13 02:42:53 UTC:
- agent binary in the VM rootfs updated to the 02:42 build, inject_secrets present
- 02:42:59 Managed secrets created for VM 2da0e442 (escrow existing) — 5s after restart, not a 60s timeout. Says CREATED, confirming the volume never existed.
- GET /api/vms/2da0e442 secrets_unlock_failed: null
- inside the guest: /dev/mapper/mjolnir-secrets on /secrets type ext4, and /run/mjolnir/secrets.env present at mode 0600
- ZERO warnings or errors in the whole boot log; 4 VMs with unchanged iroh ids, 2 routes, both sites 200

title: CI VMs need a server-side lease so client death cannot strand them
description:
Split from mjolnir-24r, whose reproduction (2026-08-12) shows client-side teardown cannot be the only guarantee: the forgejo-runner was SIGKILLed by systemd after hanging 90s on shutdown, and a SIGKILLed process runs no deferred cleanup, so the detached-context StopVM never fired and VM 50ef47c4 leaked. SIGKILL, host crash, and OOM-kill all bypass in-process cleanup by construction.

PROPOSAL: VMs spawned by a runner carry a lease — a TTL the owner must renew (heartbeat on the existing exec traffic, or an explicit renew call). Mjolnir reaps VMs whose lease has expired and which no live job claims. Durability's Reconcile currently does the opposite for these: it faithfully resumes an orphan forever, which is correct for a user VM and wrong for a job VM whose job no longer exists.

DECISIONS NEEDED (do not implement without them): lease duration and renewal mechanism; whether the lease is a general VM property or CI-specific; how it interacts with Reconcile's resume path and with :trash retention; whether a lease expiry should trash (recoverable) or hard-delete. Trashing is almost certainly right — it is O(1) and reversible via POST /api/trash/:id/restore.

Related: mjolnir-cm2 (VM metadata tags for CI correlation) would give the ownership handle this needs.
notes: VERIFIED LIVE IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-12 after deploy — see mjolnir-24r's close reason for the full evidence. Summary: happy path fired zero reclamations (runner cleaned up its own VM); failure path reclaimed a backdated CI VM on the next 30s tick, routed to @trash (restorable), tagged for 24h retention, with all 4 production VMs untouched. Boot-time lease stamping confirmed on a real runner-spawned VM: lease present at 3600s before any exec renewal, then advanced by exec traffic.
close_reason:
Implemented in a197766. Mjolnir.CILease: VMs tagged metadata.purpose=ci carry runtime.lease_expires_at (free-form map, no schema bump); renewed by VM-scoped API activity (exec mandatory, plus GET :id and :id/health); swept on the existing Health.Monitor 30s tick and reclaimed through Mjolnir.VM.stop/1 so the rootfs goes to @trash, never a hard delete. TTL 3600s matching the runner's own timeout: 1h and exceeding the longest single exec (a cold cargo build is one 6m14s exec with no API traffic), because reaping live work is far worse than an orphan lingering. CI trash retention 24h vs 7d default, read from the sidecar reap_trash already writes.

FAIL-CLOSED THROUGHOUT: eligibility is a strict AND of ci_owned? and lease_expired?; a missing lease is never treated as expired; unknown trash metadata gets the LONGER retention; sweep is double-gated (list_by_metadata + per-record predicate) and wrapped in its own rescue.

TWO GAPS FOUND IN REVIEW AND FIXED, either of which would have made this silently useless: (1) VM.build_running_record/1 rebuilds runtime from scratch on every boot AND resume, so a renew-only lease was wiped on restart — leaving the orphan permanently unreclaimable, since eligibility fails closed on a missing lease. That is the accumulation-across-restarts the feature exists to stop. The lease is now stamped at record-build time too. (2) That also covers a VM whose runner died before it ever issued an exec, which would otherwise never have carried a lease.

15 new tests (1150 -> 1165, 0 failures), covering all 7 required cases plus stamping; the reclamation test drives a fake GenServer registered in VMRegistry to prove the stop goes through the real VM.stop contract rather than a shortcut. Verified no production VM can match either gate: all 4 have empty metadata.

NOT YET DEPLOYED — ships on the next deploy.

title: VM executor silently drops every hyphenated action input (INPUT_FETCH-DEPTH etc.)
description:
Live executor act/container/mjolnir/vm.go in identikey/forgejo-runner (branch mjolnir) writes step env as 'export K=V' lines into /.forgejo/.env.sh, skipping any key failing isValidShellVarName (vm.go:177). Action inputs are exported as INPUT_<NAME> with the name verbatim, so every hyphenated input — INPUT_FETCH-DEPTH, INPUT_PERSIST-CREDENTIALS, INPUT_INCLUDE-HIDDEN-FILES — is dropped, because bash cannot export a name containing a hyphen.

Silent: the step runs with the input simply absent. actions/checkout@v4 survives because its JS falls back to defaults for missing values. actions/upload-artifact@v4 does not: getBooleanInput on an absent include-hidden-files throws 'Input does not meet YAML 1.2 Core Schema specification' and the upload never starts. Passing the input explicitly in 'with:' does NOT help — the drop happens after act has resolved inputs.

FIX: env(1) accepts names that bash cannot export. Partition the env map — valid identifiers keep the 'export K=V' path in .env.sh (they must persist across exec calls for post-steps), and invalid ones become an 'env NAME=value ... ' prefix on the command itself. Do not simply skip them.

Blocks artifact upload (mjolnir-4bk) and will hit any action with hyphenated boolean inputs.
acceptance_criteria: A workflow step using actions/upload-artifact@v4 receives include-hidden-files and completes the upload; a step can read a hyphenated input it was passed in 'with:'.
close_reason: Fixed in identikey/forgejo-runner 9a3efce7, built and live on the server. Names bash cannot export are now passed as an 'env K=V ...' prefix on the command; exportable ones still go to .env.sh for post-step persistence. Verified: upload-artifact receives include-hidden-files and completes the upload (runs 7, 8, 9) — before the fix it threw on the absent input every time.

title: build-ci-image.sh installs no toolchain: the CI image's Rust/mise/zig were hand-added too
description:
Found while verifying mjolnir-0e8. Same disease, different organ.

scripts/build-ci-image.sh mentions rust, cargo, rustup, mise and zig ZERO times. A freshly built image has only mjolnir-agent, mjolnir-network-setup and mount-extra-fs.sh in /usr/local/bin.

The live @base/ci-ubuntu-24.04 has cargo, cargo-clippy, cargo-fmt, clippy-driver, mise, rustc, rustfmt, rustup and zig there. All of it was added out of band, exactly like the guest agent was. So the CI image remains unreproducible even after mjolnir-0e8 — rebuild it today and you get a VM that boots correctly and cannot compile anything.

VERIFIED 2026-08-11: built to @base/ci-test, spawned VM ffb5a76d. mjolnir-agent active, runner uid=1000, /workspace owned correctly — but 'cargo --version' and 'rustc --version' both exit 127, command not found.

This BLOCKS the CI plan (building mj on a Mjolnir VM via the Forgejo runner) — the runner would get a VM that cannot build Rust.

Open decisions for whoever takes it:
- rustup vs mise-managed toolchain. build-deploy-base.sh already uses mise and has solved the shim-vs-real-path problem the hard way (it links real install paths from ~/.local/share/mise/installs, because mise shims point at /mise and dangle when tested from the host). Reuse that logic rather than rediscovering it.
- Which targets. x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu at minimum; x86_64-unknown-linux-musl if the image should also build the guest agent.
- Whether zig/cargo-zigbuild belongs in the image (the Justfile uses cargo zigbuild for musl cross-builds).
- Image size: a full Rust toolchain is ~1GB+ on top of the current image.

Whatever lands should be verified the same way: build to a scratch subvolume, spawn, and assert 'cargo --version' works — the post-condition check in scripts/lib/guest-agent.sh is the pattern.
close_reason: Fixed in ea30027. scripts/lib/mise.sh installs mise into every base image (ci, deploy-base, rootfs-ubuntu-24.04, buzz-agent) and the CI image now gets rust + zig THROUGH mise instead of hand-added rustup. Three quiet failure modes handled: (1) non-login PATH — wrappers in /usr/local/bin plus a verify under 'env -i', since the old profile.d/.bashrc wiring made mise invisible to mj exec; (2) missing /proc — rustup-init exits 1 with no useful message and reshim emits shims pointing at a bare /mise, so mise_use mounts and unmounts /proc around installs; (3) mise's rust backend is rustup-based, so installs/rust/<ver> is a guest-absolute symlink to /root/.cargo/bin that find() walks straight past — mise_find_tool handles both layouts. VERIFIED: build rc=0 with both post-conditions logged; VM spawned from the never-hand-touched image ran mise 2026.8.4 / cargo 1.97.1 / zig 0.16.0 / rustup 1.29.0 from a bare exec shell; 'cargo new && cargo build' produced a working binary; 'mise use -g node@22' at runtime gave node v22.23.2. Rebuild is 2.9G vs live 3.6G with /usr/local/bin parity (rustup + zig linked so promotion is not a regression). Test VM and @base/ci-test removed; live @base/ci-ubuntu-24.04 untouched and NOT yet replaced — promotion is 'just build-ci-image'.

title: Deploy build fails in the bundler layer: cp -a of full source + bun run build kills the build VM
description:
With mjolnir-gge.1.10 (base image) and the build-VM memory fix (6f0a8d6) in, a real 'mj deploy' of startup-central now gets through detect and the INSTALL layer — bun install succeeds — and fails on the third layer:

  cp -a /mnt/deploy-src/. /app/ && bun run build
  -> {:step_failed, ..., {:vsock_unavailable, {:normal, ...}}}

:vsock_unavailable means the build VM's agent went away mid-exec (the wrapper added in mjolnir-8ie). Host had 29GB free and 171G disk, so it is inside the guest.

Two untested hypotheses, in order:
1. Memory again. That step copies the ENTIRE source — this app carries 139MB of static/ — into the VM rootfs and then runs a vite/SvelteKit build. 2048MB may still be short. Cheap to test by raising :deploy_build_memory_mb.
2. The copy itself. 139MB through virtiofs into a CoW rootfs, then a bundler over it.

To diagnose properly, capture the build VM's serial console before teardown — it is currently removed with the VM, so there is no post-mortem. That is arguably the real fix: builds fail opaquely because the only witness is deleted.

Each test cycle costs ~8 minutes (119MB upload + build), so gather evidence before the next guess.
acceptance_criteria: A real mj deploy of startup-central completes through the build stage; a failed build leaves a retrievable serial log.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-08, by the diagnostics added in 9c630c5 — first use, first answer. It is NOT memory, disk, or the bundler.

THE HEALTH MONITOR IS KILLING THE BUILD.

  00:09:45  Deploy.Builder: 2 hit / 1 miss, 1 step to run (the long cp -a 139MB + bun run build)
  00:10:27  Health.Monitor: VM 4a37b68c guest-agent unreachable over vsock but VM is TCP-live; attempting L1 vsock heal
  00:10:29  Health.heal: guest_agent_ping = {:dead, :timeout}, attempting heal
  00:10:31  Health.heal: vsock_connection = {:dead, :timeout}, attempting heal
  00:10:31  Deploy.Builder: step failed {:vsock_unavailable, {:normal, ...}}   <- SAME MILLISECOND

A long build step keeps the guest agent busy, so the health probe times out. The monitor declares the VM unreachable and heals it — and the heal is VM.rebuild_vsock_connection/1, which STOPS the Vsock.Connection process the build's own in-flight exec is blocked on. The exec's GenServer.call therefore exits :normal, which the mjolnir-8ie wrapper reports as :vsock_unavailable.

Corroboration, all consistent:
- serial console shows a completely healthy guest: mjolnir-agent.service started, basic.target reached, no errors, no shutdown — the log simply stops
- highlights == [] (no OOM, panic, segfault, ENOSPC, I/O error) — which is what redirected the investigation off the memory hypothesis
- exit is :normal, not a crash — the connection was deliberately torn down
- ONLY the long step ever fails; mise install and bun install both complete and cache (2 hit / 1 miss on the retry)
- the same pattern appears on the previous attempt's VM cc74a48d at 23:54

The build-VM memory bump in 6f0a8d6 was therefore treating a symptom. It is defensible on its own merits (build VMs should not inherit the 256/512MB service default) but it was not the fix.

FIX OPTIONS, roughly in order of preference:
1. An exec in flight means the VM is BUSY, not dead. Track in-flight execs in Mjolnir.VM state (cheap now that mjolnir-8ie moved exec off the mailbox into a Task) and have Health treat busy as alive. Fixes this for every long exec, not just deploys.
2. Never heal the vsock while a request is pending on that connection — rebuild_vsock_connection/1 should refuse, or drain first.
3. Exclude ephemeral build VMs from health monitoring entirely. Narrowest, but leaves the general bug (any long mj exec is exposed to the same heal).

Note the monitor also probes IROH on build VMs (iroh_connection = {:dead, :iroh_probe_timeout}), which they neither have nor need — more evidence that ephemeral build VMs should not be under the same health regime.
RESOLVED 2026-08-08. Root cause was mjolnir-1s9 (health monitor healing the build VM to death), found by the diagnostics in 9c630c5 on their first real failure and fixed in 3114139.

startup-central now builds and deploys end to end:
  [build] release deploy-0c12dd6c... (2 hit / 1 miss)
  [run]   booting service VM
  [done]  https://z4rdfsyg...-3000.vm.worldtree.network

The diagnostics infrastructure stays: captures land in /var/lib/mjolnir/deploy/failures/<stamp>-<vm>/ with serial.log + context.json, and a failed build now reports a cause and the guest's own kernel lines rather than a 1KB tuple. The empty-highlights result is what redirected this investigation off the memory hypothesis.

title: I5 violation: Reconcile revives a VM whose guest powered itself off — intentional exit is not final
description:
Observed end-to-end while verifying @base/buzz-agent (mjolnir-cxz) on 45.76.77.97:

  22:17:24  buzz-harness.service main process exits 1
  22:17:25  guest FailureAction=poweroff fires; host logs [vm-terminate] b97ff130 ... done
  22:17:32  host logs 'Reconcile: VM b97ff130-0720-4787-b82e-dfb34327600c resumed'

The guest deliberately ended itself and Mjolnir brought it straight back. Reconcile treats any VM record whose intent is :running but which has no live hypervisor as stranded, and rehydrates it — it cannot distinguish 'the host lost the VM' from 'the guest chose to stop'.

Why this is conformance-critical, not cosmetic: block/buzz docs/remote-agents.md I5 makes intentional termination TERMINAL. An owner !shutdown, or an inactivity reap, must not be undone by the substrate. buzz-backend-mjolnir's L3 binding (docs/L3-mjolnir-binding.md, §I5) states 'this binding ships with no revive-on-abnormal-death policy at all' and 'nothing restarts anything'. Reconcile as it stands makes that statement false for every Buzz body, and it is the single easiest way to make the provider non-conforming.

Note this is a DIFFERENT trigger from the DormantRegistry wake-on-message hazard already called out in docs/plans/initiatives/buzz-provider.md §3.6 — no relay traffic is involved, the reconciler does it on its own.

Evidence the image side is correct: /var/lib/buzz/harness-exit in the VM subvolume holds exit_reason=exited, exit_status=1, service_result=exit-code — written before poweroff, readable by the host from the stopped subvolume, and sufficient to classify intentional (exited/0) vs abnormal.

Possible shapes for the fix (design needed):
  - a per-VM 'no_revive' / lifetime-policy flag on the VM record that Reconcile honours
  - Reconcile reads harness-exit (or a generic guest-exit marker) and declines to resume on a clean intentional exit
  - the deploy/stop path flips intent to :stopped before the guest powers off, so there is nothing stranded to reconcile

Blocks the provider's I5 claim; relevant to mjolnir-a5t (graceful stop) and mjolnir-j5o (wedged-body reaping, where a force-reap must stay classified abnormal).
close_reason:
Fixed and verified end-to-end on 45.76.77.97 (commits 110cc76, 0aa8716).

Per-VM lifetime policy in spawn_config: restart_policy :always (default, unchanged) | :never. A stranded :never record is FINALIZED — intent -> :stopped, rootfs preserved — instead of resumed. In spawn_config rather than a new record field, so no schema bump and no migration. Written on the first record persisted at boot, because a crash between boot and a second write would leave a :never VM looking restartable. Parsing fails OPEN to :always everywhere: an unrecognised policy silently meaning 'never restart' would strand a fleet on a typo.

Declared, not inferred. Reconcile does not decide by reading guest state: a wedged body writes no marker, and a guest that CAN write one should not decide whether the host may restart it. When @base/buzz-agent's /var/lib/buzz/harness-exit is present it is recorded as evidence (exited/0 = intentional) — size-capped, three known keys only — and changes no decision. Keeps mjolnir-j5o's rule intact: a force-reap stays abnormal.

Owner-issued Start still works (I5 blesses it; what it forbids is the substrate deciding). VM.revive/1 stamps runtime[revive_authorized_at], honoured for exactly one resume and consumed automatically when the successful boot re-persists the record — surviving a FAILED resume so the authorization is never spent on a boot that never happened. Caught during review: without it revive was a silent no-op and :never VMs were recoverable only via forget/1, which destroys them.

API: POST /api/vms takes "restart_policy": "always"|"never" (unrecognised values rejected, not defaulted). GET /api/vms now lists :stopped records with exit evidence — their rootfs is still on disk.

Live verification: self-exit -> :stopped, not resumed, rootfs 1.6G preserved -> operator revive -> resumed once, token consumed -> second self-exit -> :stopped again. Control: a default-policy VM still logs 'Reconcile: VM ... resumed' exactly as before.

24 reconcile tests (13 new), full suite 1113 passing.

Provider action required: buzz-backend-mjolnir must spawn with restart_policy=never — the default is :always and the L3 I5 claim is false without it.

title: Fresh base images don't boot: build-ci-image.sh / build-deploy-base.sh omit BOTH the mjolnir-agent binary and its unit
description:
scripts/build-rootfs-ubuntu-24.04.sh:100-118 installs /etc/systemd/system/mjolnir-agent.service and links it into basic.target.wants. scripts/build-ci-image.sh and scripts/build-deploy-base.sh do NOT.

VM.spawn's inject_guest_agent/1 only copies the BINARY into the clone; the unit that starts it must be baked into the base image. Without it the VM boots, the guest agent never runs, and spawn fails with :boot_timeout surfaced to the API as a bare {"error":"spawn_failed"}.

The live @base/ci-ubuntu-24.04 masks this: its mjolnir-agent.service file is dated 2026-06-07, months after the image build — it was added by hand. Anyone re-running `just build-ci-image` today gets a non-booting CI image.

Found while building @base/buzz-agent (mjolnir-cxz), which hit exactly this and now installs the unit itself (scripts/build-buzz-agent-image.sh).

Fix: factor the unit install into a shared helper (or copy the block) in both scripts.

Second, smaller defect found alongside: build-deploy-base.sh's mise shim symlink loop tests \`[[ -x "$R/root/.local/share/mise/shims/$bin" ]]\` from the HOST. mise shims written inside a debootstrap chroot point at /mise (mise resolves its own path via /proc/self/exe, and /proc is not mounted), so those tests are false and the loop silently emits 'Warning: node not found ... skipping symlink' — leaving node/npm off PATH in the built image.
close_reason: Fixed in 522b3b8. scripts/lib/guest-agent.sh is now the single implementation across all four builders (ci-image, deploy-base, rootfs-ubuntu-24.04, buzz-agent): installs binary + unit + basic.target.wants symlink, then verifies all three and exits non-zero if any are missing. Fails instead of warning; ALLOW_NO_AGENT=1 opts out. Also fixed a host-side 'chown runner:runner' that aborted build-ci-image.sh under set -e before it could finish at all. The mise-shim defect in the second half of this bead was already fixed independently (build-deploy-base.sh now links real mise install paths and fails loudly). VERIFIED: fresh build to @base/ci-test exited 0 with 'Guest agent verified', used the fresh musl agent, and VM ffb5a76d spawned from that never-hand-touched image reached state=running with mjolnir-agent active. Test VM and subvolume removed; live @base/ci-ubuntu-24.04 untouched. NOTE: the image still ships no Rust toolchain — same class of hand-patch, filed as mjolnir-xx5 (P1), which blocks the CI plan.

comments.author: Duke Jones
comments.text:
Root cause is worse than first written. inject_guest_agent/1 (lib/mjolnir/vm.ex:1775) only copies the binary when :guest_agent_bin is configured AND the file exists — on 45.76.77.97 the prod path native/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/mjolnir-agent does NOT exist (`find / -name mjolnir-agent -type f` outside btrfs returns nothing), so injection is a silent no-op and the clone has no agent binary at all.

So a base image needs BOTH baked in:
  1. /usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent
  2. /etc/systemd/system/mjolnir-agent.service + basic.target.wants symlink

build-rootfs-ubuntu-24.04.sh does both (gated on AGENT_BIN). build-ci-image.sh and build-deploy-base.sh do neither. Verified by spawning from a freshly built image: boots to basic.target, mjolnir-agent.service 'starts' 3x then FAILED, /var/log capture shows '/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent: No such file or directory', spawn dies on :boot_timeout -> {"error":"spawn_failed"}.

Secondary: :guest_agent_bin pointing at a nonexistent path fails silently. Worth an explicit warn at boot, or a doctor check.

title: Back-fill owner_id on the live startup-central registry entry
description:
mjolnir-xuv added ownership to Deploy.Registry entries. Legacy entries (owner_id: null) fail closed: denied to regular users, allowed only to localhost — matching Policy.VM's treatment of nil-owner VMs.

/var/lib/mjolnir/deploy/registry/startup-central.json currently has owner_id: null. Consequences until back-filled:
- localhost ops (the Justfile's ssh-wrapped curl) work normally
- 'mj domain set/rm' and a redeploy via a BEARER TOKEN are denied with 404
- the app is hidden from GET /api/apps for non-localhost callers

The correct owner is not inferable from the box: the app's service VM (de9fe3e2) has owner_id null too, and the only real owner_id present anywhere is bfd22745-3ca8-44da-8cca-916092684262 (VM 076adf62, the zine VM) — which may or may not be the same person who owns startup-central. Needs the intended owner's user_id, then a one-line edit to the JSON (and a Registry reload or restart).

Deliberately NOT guessed: assigning an app to the wrong subject is a silent authz mistake.
acceptance_criteria: startup-central.json carries the correct owner_id; 'mj domain' via bearer token works for that owner and is refused for anyone else.
notes: DONE 2026-08-08. owner_id backfilled to bfd22745-3ca8-44da-8cca-916092684262 and verified EMPIRICALLY rather than assumed: 'mj domain ls' over Duke's real bearer token lists the app (so the subject matches), and with a different owner set it returns 'No apps deployed.' while 'mj domain set' is refused with a 404 that does not leak existence. The subsequent redeploy preserved owner_id through the cutover.

title: VM GenServer still blocks its mailbox on inline vsock calls (health probes, terminal, reconfigure)
description:
Follow-on from mjolnir-8ie. The PERMANENT wedge is fixed — exec now runs off the GenServer — but several other handle_call clauses still perform vsock round-trips INLINE, so an unresponsive guest blocks the mailbox for the duration of each:

  - {:probe_iroh_status, timeout}  (VM.iroh_status, from Health.IrohConnection)
  - :reconfigure_iroh, :reconfigure_network
  - :rebuild_vsock_connection      (from Health.VsockConnection)
  - the terminal_* family          (terminal_open/read/send/send_and_read/close)

These are BOUNDED (vsock_request defaults to 10s), so the block is transient rather than permanent, but it is enough to make a health check on a severed-vsock VM report a false 'vm_unreachable' to any concurrent caller: four probes at up to ~10s each is up to ~40s of mailbox blocking per tick. Observed exactly that on 2026-08-07 — GET /api/vms/:id returned 'running' and GET /api/vms/:id/health returned vm_unreachable moments later, on the same VM.

probe_iroh_status was additionally DISCARDING its timeout argument (), so Health.IrohConnection's 3s bound silently became vsock_request's 10s default. Fixed.

The general fix is to give these the same treatment as exec: hand the round-trip to a Task and GenServer.reply from there. Care needed for the ones that MUTATE state (rebuild_vsock_connection, reconfigure_*) — those cannot simply move off-process, and probably want a 'work in progress' marker in state plus a reply when the task reports back.
acceptance_criteria: A VM whose guest agent is unreachable answers status/get/health promptly and consistently while probes are in flight; no caller observes a false :unreachable.
notes:
POST-DEPLOY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-12 21:19 UTC — the fix is live and its own acceptance holds (no handle_call blocks the mailbox on a vsock round-trip; 26 tests). But I predicted it would eliminate the false 'unreachable' seen on deploys, and IT DID NOT. That symptom has a different cause and is now filed as mjolnir-y32.

Measured timeline on the deploy of this very fix:
  21:19:35 restart -> 21:19:53 'GenServer unreachable (call timed out)' -> 21:20:23 'Managed secrets unlock failed: :timeout' -> 21:20:23 resumed.

The blocking is in the BOOT path, not a handle_call: do_boot runs inside handle_continue(:boot), and maybe_unlock_secrets/2 uses a 60s vsock bound (justified — LUKS create can exceed 10s). Health.Monitor's call times out against that and renders the VM unreachable. Recording it here so nobody later reads this issue as having fixed the deploy-time symptom.
close_reason:
Fixed in ab2c141. All remaining vsock round-trips are off the VM mailbox. Read-only clauses (terminal_open/read/send/list/close, probe_iroh_status, authorize_inject_peer) use the spawn-and-reply pattern exec established.

CORRECTION TO THIS ISSUE: it grouped reconfigure_iroh and reconfigure_network with the Tier 2 state mutators. They are not — both returned {:reply, reply, state} with state untouched (verified against the pre-change code), so they moved with the simple pattern. Only rebuild_vsock_connection genuinely writes state; it spawns a worker and folds the result in from handle_info, so vsock_conn is still written only by the owning process, and callers arriving mid-rebuild queue instead of racing a second rebuild.

FOUND IN REVIEW AND FIXED: that waiter queue had no exit path if the worker never reported. try/catch converts ordinary failures into a result, so only an uncatchable kill reaches it — but the waiter list would then stay non-empty forever and every later rebuild would join a queue that can never drain, permanently wedging the very recovery path this change protects. The worker's monitor ref is now retained and a DOWN fails the waiters; two tests cover it, including that a stale DOWN after the normal result does not double-reply.

24 tests in test/mjolnir/vm_mailbox_nonblocking_test.exs prove handle_call returns {:noreply, _} immediately against a wedged dependency, the caller still gets its reply, and a concurrent cheap :status call resolves right after a slow probe is handed off — the direct analog of the false vm_unreachable. Suite 1165 -> 1195, 0 failures.

NOT YET DEPLOYED.

title: Gateway: a custom_domain whose apex is missing from :gateway_apexes fails SILENTLY
description:
Caused a ~10 minute outage of startupcentral.build on 2026-08-07 (18:18:31-18:28:14).

Mechanism: Gateway.RouteReconciler only emits a [[route]] for an app whose custom_domain apex appears in :gateway_apexes. If the apex is absent, the reconciler emits NOTHING — no warning, no error — and the gateway answers the bare apex with 400 'Empty subdomain'. Nothing in the chain that produced the broken state reports a problem: the app is registered in Deploy.Registry with a custom_domain, apps.toml regenerates 'successfully', and the gateway logs a config.loaded with a lower route_count than before.

Trigger in this instance: startupcentral.build was added to :gateway_apexes at RUNTIME via Application.put_env on 2026-07-20 and never persisted. A comment in /etc/mjolnir/gateway.toml even said 'persist in config/config.exs before restart'. It was not, so the apex existed only in the running BEAM; the next restart regenerated apps.toml without the route.

Fixed for this domain two ways (config/config.exs :gateway_apexes, and MJOLNIR_GATEWAY_APEXES in /etc/mjolnir/env). The CLASS of bug is still open.

Wanted:
- RouteReconciler logs a loud warning (ideally an EventBus event) when a Deploy.Registry app has a custom_domain whose apex is not configured — naming the app and the apex.
- Consider deriving the apex from the custom_domain automatically when it is unambiguous, rather than requiring two places to agree.
- A startup self-check that every registered custom_domain resolves to an emitted route, so the failure surfaces at boot instead of on the next customer request.
acceptance_criteria: Registering an app with a custom_domain whose apex is not in :gateway_apexes produces a clear warning naming the app and apex; a regression test covers it.
close_reason: Fixed: RouteReconciler warning now names app+domain+needed apex+configured apexes; GET /api/apps exposes apex_registered so a dropped route is visible beyond logs. Tests cover both directions.

title: B0: self-hosted Buzz relay on Mjolnir (provider demo target)
description:
One Buzz relay running on Mjolnir, self-hosted, as the demo/dev target for the provider.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT LATER: block/buzz#2663 (2026-08-05 correction) establishes that Block-HOSTED communities refuse the provider-deployed identity class (desktop-minted key + NIP-OA auth_tag) from datacenter origins with 'restricted: not a relay member'. Affects every provider (ssh/gce/hetzner/crabbox), not just ours. So a self-hosted relay is the ONLY target where buzz-backend-mjolnir fully works — it is the demo environment, not a later product.

Scope: Buzz docker compose bundle (Postgres/Redis/MinIO/Caddy) in a Mjolnir VM, behind the Mjolnir gateway with a domain. NOT the hosted product (that is mjolnir-80q, which adds egress guarantee + billing).

Blocks the P1 demo: 'agent boots in a VM, answers a mention in a channel'.

title: VMGENID — kernel CONFIG_VMGENID + ACPI device in Cloud Hypervisor
description:
The correct, non-racy fix for snapshot entropy reuse (mjolnir-3y6.5). An ACPI device holds a 128-bit generation ID; the hypervisor changes it on restore; Linux drivers/virt/vmgenid.c (5.18+) sees the change and reseeds the CRNG IN THE KERNEL before userspace is scheduled. No userspace reseed can provide that ordering.

Two pieces, verified missing 2026-08-07:
1. Guest kernel — no vmgenid/VM_GEN_COUNTER symbols in /var/lib/mjolnir/vmlinux-ch. Enable CONFIG_VMGENID. Cheap: we already build a custom PVH kernel.
2. Cloud Hypervisor v50.0.0 — no VMGENID strings; not implemented. Needs the ACPI device added. Upstream contribution or a patched build. This is the bigger half.

Until both land, mjolnir-3y6.5's interim reseed carries an unavoidable race between the guest agent and userspace on resume.
acceptance_criteria: A restored VM reseeds its CRNG without guest-agent involvement; two VMs forked from one snapshot diverge immediately with no host-side reachability gate needed.
notes: Re-checked against CH v53.0 after the mjolnir-3y6.15 upgrade: still ZERO vmgenid/VM_GEN_COUNTER strings. Upstream has not added the ACPI device, so the entropy-reuse hazard (mjolnir-3y6.5) is NOT fixed by the upgrade and the CH half of this remains real work. The kernel half (CONFIG_VMGENID in our PVH build) is still cheap and independent.

title: Policy coverage test failing: 4 endpoints have no policy enforcement
description:
Mjolnir.Policy.CoverageTest (test/mjolnir/policy/coverage_test.exs:35) fails on main. Endpoints without policy enforcement:
  POST /api/deploy
  PUT /api/apps/:app/domain
  DELETE /api/apps/:app/domain
  GET /api/apps

Pre-existing on main as of 2026-08-07 — confirmed by stashing unrelated work and re-running. Introduced with the deploy/sites/domain surface (commits f862174, bfefab0). The suite is otherwise green (1011 tests, this is the only failure), so it is masking any NEW coverage regression.
acceptance_criteria: mix test passes with zero failures; each of the four endpoints either enforces a policy or is deliberately whitelisted with a comment saying why.
notes: DUPLICATE of mjolnir-xuv (filed 2026-07-21), which describes the identical four endpoints with better analysis — it identifies the multi-tenancy authz hole, not just the red test. Closing this one; track it at mjolnir-xuv.

title: mj connect / Iroh PTY path needs the same shared-session support as the vsock path
description:
The vsock PtyOpen path now takes an optional tmux session name, so GET /api/vms/:id/pty?session=<name> gives several clients one shared terminal. The Iroh path does NOT: iroh.rs spawns DEFAULT_SHELL unconditionally because the session name would have to ride on the Hello frame, which is a versioned wire protocol shared with the mj client (native/mjolnir_client).

Until this lands, 'mj connect' and the browser/gateway PTY diverge: the same VM gives you a shared terminal over WebSocket and a private shell over Iroh. Needs a Hello frame field plus a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump on both ends.
acceptance_criteria: mj connect --session <name> lands in the same tmux session as the WebSocket PTY with the same name. Version mismatch between old client and new agent degrades to a private shell rather than erroring.
close_reason: ALPN-negotiated session handshake landed in 990d900 and is deployed. Verified end to end on VM 600a005c: mj connect --p2p --session vtest and the WebSocket PTY on the same name both land in ONE tmux session (capture-pane shows both markers in a single shared pane, tmux list-sessions shows exactly one). No fallback message => mjolnir-shell/2 negotiated. Old pre-change mj binary against the new agent degrades to a private shell with no error, satisfying the version-mismatch criterion. Follow-ups filed: WS path stdin injection, and a pre-existing exit-code bug (mjolnir-lmx).

title: API + CLI surface for freeze/thaw
description:
Expose memory snapshot as a distinct, heavier operation rather than silently changing what mj snapshot create does. Filesystem snapshot stays as-is; memory snapshot is the strictly more capable sibling and the caller picks.

Surface: mj snapshot create <id> <name> --memory (or mj freeze/mj thaw), plus the corresponding API params. Snapshot metadata and mj snapshot show must make it obvious which kind a snapshot is — restoring a fs-only snapshot expecting a live process is a bad surprise.
acceptance_criteria: mj snapshot show distinguishes fs-only from memory snapshots. Existing fs-snapshot behaviour is unchanged for existing callers.
notes:
CONSTRAINT for the API/CLI surface, from ef4a525: freezing is a ONE-WAY PARK, not a checkpoint. vm.snapshot is terminal for any virtio-fs VM — the source wedges on its first post-snapshot filesystem I/O while CH still reports Running.

So 'mj freeze <id>' must be presented as parking the VM (it stops), NOT as taking a checkpoint of a VM that keeps serving. The CLI should say so at the point of use, and the API should tear the source VMM + virtiofsd down as part of the freeze rather than leaving a Running-but-wedged VM for Health.Monitor to try to heal.

'mj snapshot create' (filesystem-only) stays the non-disruptive option and does resume cleanly — the two verbs need clearly different words in help text, because 'snapshot' and 'freeze' otherwise sound interchangeable and one of them stops your VM.

comments.author: Duke Jones
comments.text: When this lands the API/CLI freeze path, pass secrets_mode (and vsock) through to MemorySnapshot.freeze. A :managed/:persistent VM without that is refused (k8y.3). After thaw, reopen secrets via inject_secrets or Secrets.Quiesce.resume before publishing reachability — same gate as Entropy.reseed.

comments.author: d0rje
comments.text: STEER probe comment

comments.author: d0rje
comments.text:
STEER 2026-09-03 (standard). User accepted all three recommended forks. `bd update --design/--notes` failed (events.id has no default in embedded Dolt); this comment is the residue `change` should read.

## Decided
- verbs: mj freeze / mj thaw; mj snapshot create stays filesystem-only (user)
- identity: named park, same VM id on thaw (user)
  mj freeze <id> <name> tears the source down and writes a kind=memory snapshot. mj thaw <name> restores that same VM id. 409 if the id is live. Forks are mjolnir-8m3.
- restore paths: only explicit thaw this node (user)
  mj spawn --snapshot <memory-name> refuses and points at thaw. handle_done / DormantRegistry / mj message stay filesystem mailbox park.

## [AUTO]
- HTTP: POST /api/vms/:id/freeze {name}; POST /api/snapshots/:name/thaw. Do not extend POST /api/vms/:id/snapshots.
- GET snapshot list/show include kind filesystem|memory (acceptance).
- Scopes: reuse snapshots:create (freeze), vms:spawn + snapshots:read (thaw). No new scope.
- Freeze API tears down source VMM + virtiofsd; CLI says parked/stopped at point of use.
- Pass secrets_mode + vsock into freeze; refuse managed/persistent without wipe (k8y.3). After thaw: reseed, reopen secrets, then publish reachability.
- No extra interactive confirm. --json like other commands. MCP freeze/thaw tools out of scope this node.
- 8m3 (fork new ids) and mailbox-mid-thought freeze are later; this surface must not imply they work.

## Feeds change
Operator surface is two new verbs over the existing MemorySnapshot engine. Freeze is a named one-way park of that VM, not a checkpoint and not a clone. Snapshot create/list/show stay; show gains kind so memory vs filesystem is obvious. Thaw is name-addressed and returns the original id. Spawn and mailbox do not grow a memory-restore path in this node.

title: vsock reconnect handshake after restore
description:
HAZARD 4. The guest agent holds a live vsock connection in restored RAM and believes it is connected; the host-side Mjolnir.Vsock.Connection GenServer for the old VM is gone. CID is stable (derived from the VM UUID) but both ends must renegotiate.

Needs an explicit post-restore handshake, plus a guest-agent path that detects a dead peer and re-listens rather than hanging forever on a stale fd.
acceptance_criteria: A restored VM answers exec and ping over vsock without manual intervention; guest agent recovers from a peer that vanished mid-connection.
notes: Upstream CH v52.0 (#7958) resets vsock connections on snapshot restore, which covers the RESTORE half of this. NOT the whole story: mjolnir-8ie was reproduced during the mjolnir-3y6.1 spike showing the vsock also dies on a long PAUSE ALONE, with no restore involved, and the guest agent never re-establishes. Keep this bead for the pause case and the guest-agent side.
close_reason:
Closing as NOT THE PROBLEM, with evidence. The hazard as written — 'the guest agent holds a live vsock connection in restored RAM and believes it is connected; both ends must renegotiate' — does not occur. Measured on 45.76.77.97 with a host-side vsock client speaking Mjolnir's wire protocol:

- pause 15s + resume, then a FRESH connection: PONG. No renegotiation needed.
- freeze + kill VMM + thaw into a fresh VMM, then a FRESH connection: PONG at t+3s, t+8s, t+15s, t+25s. A thawed VM answers ping over vsock with no manual intervention, which is this bead's acceptance criterion.

CH v52's #7958 (vsock connections reset on restore) genuinely covers the restore half, as this bead's own note suspected. The guest agent's accept loop spawns per connection (vsock.rs:505) and logs-and-continues on accept errors, so it does not wedge.

The bead's note kept this open for 'the pause case' from mjolnir-8ie. That is real but it is NOT a vsock problem: see ef4a525. vm.snapshot is TERMINAL for any virtio-fs VM — after pause->snapshot->resume the guest blocks on its first filesystem I/O (vcpu0 in kvm_vcpu_block, _fs0 in ep_poll) and everything stalls behind it. vsock going dark is a SYMPTOM of the guest being wedged, not a connection that needs renegotiating. A plain long pause with no snapshot is completely fine.

So there is nothing to build here. What the epic actually needed was the contract correction in ef4a525 (freeze is a one-way park) — reopen only if a thawed VM is ever observed failing to answer vsock.

title: Restore orchestration — virtiofsd + TAP + fresh VMM ordering
description:
HAZARDS 2 and 5. Restore cannot happen into a booted VM — it needs a fresh cloud-hypervisor process started WITHOUT --vm-config.

Required ordering: (1) rootfs subvolume present at the pinned generation, (2) virtiofsd started on the SAME socket path recorded in the snapshot — CH reconnects to vhost-user, it does not respawn the daemon, (3) TAP device recreated and up with the matching MAC/IP before restore (Mjolnir.Network allocation is hash-deterministic from the VM id, which helps), (4) fresh VMM, (5) vm.restore, (6) vm.resume.

If virtiofsd is not listening, restore fails or the guest wedges on first I/O.
acceptance_criteria: Restore path in Mjolnir.VM brings up virtiofsd and TAP before the VMM, and fails loudly with a specific error if either is missing.
notes:
CORRECTION to this bead's close reason. It said forking N VMs from one memory image 'needs per-thaw config rewriting and a CID reallocation whose interaction with the vsock device state in state.json is unproven'. The unproven half is now proven: CH v53 restores cleanly from a rewritten config.json carrying a different virtiofsd socket path AND a different vsock CID, with the marker process continuing at the same PID. Reflinking the RAM image is free (0.00s, zero additional bytes).

The refusal that ships is still correct — nothing today rewrites the config, so two concurrent thaws would still collide on one virtiofsd. But the COST ESTIMATE was wrong: forking is cheap, and the remaining work is network identity and guest identity, not storage. See mjolnir-8m3.
close_reason:
Done in 2dada84, proven end-to-end on 45.76.77.97 through the real Elixir code: pre-freeze counter=7 pid=761, post-thaw counter 11->14->17->20 with pid=761 UNCHANGED and zero i8042/VM-reset events.

Acceptance ('brings up virtiofsd and TAP before the VMM, and fails loudly with a specific error if either is missing') met. Verified refusals on the live host: {:virtiofsd_socket_in_use, path}, {:memory_snapshot_not_found, name}, {:snapshot_not_readonly, name}, {:snapshot_replaced, name, 208321, 208325}. Plus {:backend_socket_not_listening, path, timeout}, {:tap_name_mismatch, ...}, {:tap_mac_mismatch, ...}, {:tap_setup_failed, ...} covered by tests.

KEY FINDING — config.json is the authority and must be READ, not derived. CH records ABSOLUTE socket paths and the vsock CID verbatim, so a thaw cannot put backends where a new VM would normally go. What makes it work is decoupling shared-dir from socket path: virtiofsd serves the fresh pinned CLONE on the socket path the snapshot recorded. TAP must be recreated for the SOURCE vm id (metadata.source_vm_id), because MAC/IP are hash-derived and the guest holds the old ones in RAM.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND ONLY BY RUNNING IT (all fixed):
1. The Generation pin broke on its own first legitimate use — cloning FROM a read-only snapshot advances its Generation (root item now lists the clone), so thaw #2 falsely refused. Pin is now gen_at_creation + readonly flag. See mjolnir-3y6.3.
2. The connect-and-close liveness probe was DESTRUCTIVE: virtiofsd serves one client and exits on disconnect, so the probe killed the daemon. In preflight it would have aimed at a RUNNING PRODUCTION VM's socket. Readiness is now a stat; ownership comes from the process table via --socket-path.
3. A failed thaw left its clone behind, making the retry fail with an unrelated btrfs_snapshot_failed.

NOT SUPPORTED, refused rather than half-working: forking N VMs from one memory image. Two thaws want the same virtiofsd socket and same vsock CID (both in config.json); the second would attach to the first VM's virtiofsd — one daemon, two guests. Needs per-thaw config rewriting + CID reallocation vs the vsock device state in state.json.

REMAINING for the epic: thaw returns a running-but-unreachable VM. Adoption into the VM GenServer/StateStore/Health and the reseed-then-publish gate is mjolnir-3y6.10 (API+CLI surface); mjolnir-3y6.6 (vsock reconnect) is likely needed for the adopted VM to be exec-able.

title: Mjolnir.CloudHypervisor.Client — add snapshot_vm/2 and restore_vm/2
description: PUT /api/v1/vm.snapshot {destination_url} and PUT /api/v1/vm.restore {source_url, prefault}. Mirror the existing put/2 helpers in lib/mjolnir/cloud_hypervisor/client.ex. Extend the Mjolnir.Hypervisor behaviour with snapshot_instance/2 + restore_instance/2 so the abstraction does not leak CH specifics.
acceptance_criteria: Both endpoints callable against a live CH socket; behaviour callbacks added; unit tests with a stubbed socket.
close_reason: Client.snapshot_vm/3 and restore_vm/3 landed in b92eb91. Both take a 600s ceiling (guest RAM is written uncompressed, so the call scales with VM size) against the 30s default now applied to every other CH call. Every request carries --max-time: a wedged vhost-user handshake hangs vm.restore forever (how CH v50 failed — vmm thread parked in unix_stream_data_wait) and an unbounded curl there takes the calling GenServer with it. curl exit 28 surfaces as {:timeout, path, secs}, distinct from {:curl_failed, ...}, because a timed-out restore leaves a half-restored VMM to kill while a curl failure usually means the socket was never there.

title: Upstream: fix block/buzz#4730 (remote agent presence)
description:
Provider-backed agents render a hardcoded <PresenceDot status="online" /> gated only on isActive, so remote liveness derives from backend_agent_id rather than relay presence — violating Buzz's own invariant I3. Diagnosed to file and line in the issue.

Small fix, in the desktop, on exactly the code path we care about. DO THIS BEFORE ANNOUNCING ANYTHING — it establishes us as a contributor rather than a vendor with a press release.
notes:
Submitted as block/buzz#5138 (2026-08-06): https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/5138
Branch dukedorje:fix/remote-agent-presence-liveness. DCO check passes, mergeable.
Remaining CI appears to need maintainer approval (first-time contributor).
Local gates all green: 4488 desktop tests pass/0 fail, tsc clean, pnpm check clean.
Keep OPEN until merged — the plan gates announcing the provider on this landing.

title: Community data egress guarantee for hosted Buzz
description:
Buzz has no inter-relay replication and no export path: a tenant leaves with their npub and none of their history. Hosting it unchanged inherits that failure and fails the exit test.

Deliver: signed, complete community export (event log + blobs + manifest), plus a VERIFIED restore into a bare self-hosted Buzz relay from the export alone with no help from us. Untested egress is not egress.

This is a LAUNCH REQUIREMENT for the hosted product, not a follow-on. It is also the differentiator — every other Buzz host is on K8s+RDS and structurally cannot offer it.

Also needs the B2 backup path (see b2-backup-infra memory: Sites/VM data is not yet backed up).

title: Secret injection path for Buzz agent keys + negative test
description:
deploy payload -> Mjolnir.SecretStore -> vsock injection at guest boot -> harness process env. Mostly exists; needs wiring plus the test that pins the property.

This is our headline advantage over the Kubernetes binding, where the spec states plainly: 'that key rests as a Secret: anyone the cluster trusts to read secrets in that namespace can read it.'

MUST include the negative test: assert the nsec appears in NO host-side artifact — not the VM record, not any API response, not logs, not the syslog stream. The claim is the product; an untested claim is a liability.
close_reason: SecretStore + vsock inject_identity; negative test pins nsec off host artifacts (ab24433)

title: Graceful stop with harness drain (Buzz I3 staleness bound)
description:
Stop path: vsock shutdown signal -> wait for harness drain -> then stop hypervisor. Grace window >= the harness's full graceful-shutdown path.

The relay's presence TTL is 180s. A hypervisor kill that races the drain converts a clean stop into an abnormal one and burns the entire window. This makes the force-kill timeout a conformance-relevant constant, not a tuning knob.

title: Build @base/buzz-agent rootfs image
description:
Base BTRFS subvolume carrying buzz-acp plus ACP agents (goose/codex/claude-code). Add to just build-ci-image alongside the CI rootfs.

Requirement from the L3 binding: the harness must run as the guest's signal-receiving process so that harness exit terminates the VM (required by invariant I5).

Open: which agents baked in vs fetched at boot (image size vs cold start).
close_reason:
Built, spawn-verified, and harness wiring proven end-to-end on 45.76.77.97 (commit 807d57b).

Deliverables: scripts/build-buzz-agent-image.sh + `just build-buzz-agent-image` (@base/buzz-agent, 1.6 GB).

Open question resolved — everything baked, nothing fetched at boot. sprig is one multi-call binary (buzz-acp = buzz-agent = buzz = rg = tree = the git-nostr helpers), extracted from the digest-pinned ghcr image the Kubernetes binding also pins, so both bodies run identical harness bytes. goose 1.45.0 + claude-agent-acp + codex-acp on pinned node 20.20.2 baked behind WITH_GOOSE / WITH_NPM_AGENTS; /etc/buzz-agent-image.json records the resulting harness set for discover_harnesses.

I5 requirement satisfied and demonstrated: injected /run/mjolnir/buzz.env -> buzz-harness.path fired -> buzz-acp ran as the unit's main process -> rejected an invalid nsec, exit 1 -> /var/lib/buzz/harness-exit recorded exit_reason=exited exit_status=1 service_result=exit-code -> FailureAction=poweroff -> host logged [vm-terminate].

Gotcha worth keeping: SuccessAction=/FailureAction= are systemd.unit(5) options. In [Service] systemd reports SuccessAction=none and a clean harness exit leaves the body running.

Filed from this work: mjolnir-0e8 (fresh CI/deploy images don't boot — no agent binary, no unit) and mjolnir-yhr (Reconcile revives an intentionally-exited VM; blocks the I5 claim, parented to mjolnir-e70).

title: Extend VM metadata with generation counter + metadata filtering (Buzz I4)
description:
Extends mjolnir-cm2 beyond CI correlation. The Buzz provider's reconciliation loop (invariant I4: at most one live instance per agent key per scope) needs three substrate primitives Mjolnir lacks:

1. VM metadata map (String=>String), persisted in StateStore, queryable via GET /vms filter
2. Monotonic generation counter per VM record, bumped on every mutation
3. Conditional delete (If-Match: <generation>) -> 409 on mismatch

(3) is NOT optional. Without compare-and-delete fencing the destructive rows of the reconciliation loop cannot be implemented conformingly. Interim behavior is to REFUSE them, per the spec's own rule that a provider which cannot positively identify an object as its own output does not repair around it, it reports it.

BLOCKING for the provider's full reconciliation. P1 of the provider ships degraded (create-or-no-op, no destructive repair) until this lands.
close_reason: Closed

title: Buzz provider & hosted Buzz-on-Mjolnir
description:
Ship buzz-backend-mjolnir (free OSS provider deploying Buzz agents into Mjolnir microVMs), hosted Buzz-on-Mjolnir (paid, differentiated by a real data-egress guarantee), and recrypt encryption for Buzz media.

Thesis: two costs Block's remote-agent spec names as honest — the agent key resting as a readable K8s Secret, and the body's filesystem state being mortal — are properties of containers, not of remote agents. A microVM on BTRFS has neither.

Spec of record: block/buzz@main:docs/remote-agents.md (protocol_version 1, invariants I1-I5, conformance L1/L2/L3).
Plan: docs/plans/initiatives/buzz-provider.md
Report: docs/research/buzz-comparative-analysis.md
Provider repo: ~/work/IdentiKey/buzz-backend-mjolnir
notes: Folded mjolnir-1pe 2026-08-17 into openspec/specs/buzz-local-client/spec.md (nsec is opaque SecretStore blob, vsock inject_identity, negative host-artifact test). add-buzz-local-runtime stays PENDING (facade, crate, @base/dev, mjolnir-gti). Guest agent still needs just deploy --agent for a live buzz.env write.

title: Health roll-up reports vsock/agent failure when only L2 guest_network is dead
description: Mjolnir.Health.check/2 rolls any dead check up to :dead, then corroborated_overall downgrades to :agent_unreachable when TCP-live. This discards WHICH check failed. Live report: guest_agent_ping :ok, vsock_connection :ok, iroh_connection :ok, guest_network {:dead, :egress_blocked} -> overall :agent_unreachable, and Monitor logs 'guest-agent unreachable over vsock'. That message is false when the L0 vsock ping passed, and it cost a full debugging session chasing a nonexistent vsock bug (1004 false warnings since 07:33 on 2026-07-21). Fix: only report :agent_unreachable when the L0/L1 vsock checks actually failed; otherwise report the failing check by name.
close_reason: Both already fixed in 1f0a480 (2026-07-21) but never closed. Verified independently today: lib/mjolnir/health/guest_network.ex requires a default route then probes egress with whichever of curl/wget/ping exists, reporting :degraded (not :dead) when no tool is present; lib/mjolnir/health.ex defines @agent_channel_checks and only downgrades to :agent_unreachable when the vsock-path checks themselves failed, keeping the failing check visible by name. Regression coverage in test/mjolnir/health/corroboration_test.exs; 34 health tests green. Stale moduledoc describing the old ping probe corrected in 987ec4d.

title: Health.GuestNetwork probes with ping, absent from ubuntu-24.04 base image
description: GuestNetwork.probe/1 runs 'ping -c1 -W2 1.1.1.1' inside the guest, but iputils-ping is not installed in the ubuntu-24.04 base image (base switched Arch->Ubuntu in 82f3a37). Guest returns 'sh: 1: ping: not found' -> probe maps non-zero to NOPING -> {:dead, :egress_blocked}. Verified guest egress is actually healthy: https://1.1.1.1 returns 301 and DNS resolves. Fix: use a TCP-based egress check (the probe already cannot distinguish 'binary missing' from 'packet dropped'), and/or install iputils-ping in the base image.
close_reason: Both already fixed in 1f0a480 (2026-07-21) but never closed. Verified independently today: lib/mjolnir/health/guest_network.ex requires a default route then probes egress with whichever of curl/wget/ping exists, reporting :degraded (not :dead) when no tool is present; lib/mjolnir/health.ex defines @agent_channel_checks and only downgrades to :agent_unreachable when the vsock-path checks themselves failed, keeping the failing check visible by name. Regression coverage in test/mjolnir/health/corroboration_test.exs; 34 health tests green. Stale moduledoc describing the old ping probe corrected in 987ec4d.

title: Deploy build base image: node+bun+mise preinstalled (ci-style) so builds skip the ~30s toolchain install
description: The first deploy installed nodejs (apt) + bun (curl|bash) inside the build VM every time (~30s+, and the bun installer fails 'HOME: unbound variable' unless HOME=/root is exported). A prebaked base image (like ci-ubuntu-24.04 + bun) makes builds start from a warm toolchain, matching Detector's node@20/bun assumption.
design: Extend the CI image build (scripts/build-ci-image.sh pattern) to produce a 'deploy-node-bun' base with mise + node@20 + bun on PATH and HOME sane. Deploy.Builder spawns from it; install/build layers then key on lockfile/source hash over the warm base.
acceptance_criteria: A SvelteKit/adapter-node build on the deploy base needs no apt/bun install step; first-layer boot has node+bun ready.
notes:
DONE (script) — scripts/build-deploy-base.sh added + merged to main (commit e4ae76e). Builds a 'deploy-node-bun' BTRFS base (mise + node@20 + bun, HOME=/root, shims symlinked to /usr/local/bin so bare 'sh -c' vsock exec resolves them). shellcheck-clean; NOT yet run on the server (needs root+Linux debootstrap) and NOT yet wired in. WAVE-2 WIRING (lib/, do in the /api/deploy or a Builder task): Deploy.Builder.build/3 takes :base_image (defaults to base_layer_id -> falls through to VM.spawn default 'ubuntu-24.04'); the deploy-lane caller (Deploy.Supervisor) must pass base_image/base_layer_id 'deploy-node-bun' or the new image is never used. Detector already emits 'mise install' as step 1 -> becomes a fast no-op on this base if the app pins node@20.
BLOCKING LIVE DEPLOYS as of 2026-08-07. The wiring half DID land — Deploy.Orchestrator now defaults to base_image 'deploy-node-bun' (asserted in orchestrator_test.exs:91) — but the image was never built on the server, so the halves are out of sync and every real deploy dies at the first build VM:

  Deploy.Builder: 0 hit / 3 miss; resume from %{base_image: "deploy-node-bun", ...}
  btrfs subvolume snapshot /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@base/deploy-node-bun ...
  [error] VM 5f8ac188 failed to boot: {:btrfs_snapshot_failed, 1, "ERROR: Could not statfs: No such file or directory"}

/var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@base/ currently holds only: arch, buzz-agent, ci-ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04.

Unblock with:
  ssh root@45.76.77.97 'cd /opt/mjolnir && sudo bash scripts/build-deploy-base.sh /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@base/deploy-node-bun'

Note the script has never actually been executed anywhere, so expect first-run friction. Until it exists, mj deploy cannot complete and mjolnir-gge.12.1's live acceptance step stays blocked.
BUILT AND WORKING 2026-08-07. @base/deploy-node-bun now exists and boots. Three defects found on first execution, all fixed (commits e6f5a61, and the toolchain fix before it):

1. The symlink step looked for mise's SHIMS, which are symlinks to /mise — a path in neither the rootfs nor the host, so they dangle both ways. Every lookup missed and /usr/local/bin was left empty. Now discovers the real installs/ paths (which must be discovered, not constructed: mise resolves node@20 -> 20.20.2, bun@latest -> 1.3.14), and a miss is a hard error rather than a Warning lost in 1300 lines of debootstrap output.

2. Symlinks are wrong even against the real paths: npm/npx are shell scripts deriving their prefix from $0, so a symlink at /usr/local/bin/npm makes npm look for /usr/local/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js. Replaced with exec wrappers, uniformly.

3. mjolnir-agent.service was never installed, so the VM booted but never pinged over vsock -> :boot_timeout. NOTE build-ci-image.sh has the SAME gap; @base/ci-ubuntu-24.04 and @base/ubuntu-24.04 have the unit only because someone added it out of band. Worth fixing there too.

ACCEPTANCE MET: a VM spawned with base_image 'deploy-node-bun' boots, and a bare vsock exec (no login shell, no PATH setup) resolves node v20.20.2, npm 10.8.2, bun 1.3.14, which bun -> /usr/local/bin/bun. A real deploy now gets through detect and the install layer (bun install succeeds).

title: VM.spawn: plumb owner_id + extra_mounts (both silently ignored today) — unblocks owned build VMs + virtio-fs source ingest
description: Found during the first real deploy (startup-central, 2026-07-19): passing owner_id or extra_mounts to Mjolnir.VM.spawn via rpc is SILENTLY IGNORED (they're in @config_key_allowlist but not plumbed to the boot path). Consequences: (1) rpc-spawned build VMs have owner=nil, so the owner-scoped /api/vms/:id/exec 404s -> can't use 'mj exec' (the reliable vsock channel); had to fall back to serial-console VM.exec which is UNRELIABLE for multi-line/long build commands. (2) extra_mounts is ignored, so the virtio-fs source-share ingest doesn't work; had to copy source into the rootfs subvolume host-side as a hack.
design: Plumb owner_id and extra_mounts through VM.spawn -> child_spec -> boot config -> Cloud Hypervisor (extra virtiofsd via VirtioFS.start_many; guest mounts by tag). With owner_id honored, build VMs are owned -> mj exec (vsock, handles multi-line/long) works. With extra_mounts honored, the Builder can mount the app source read-only instead of copying into the rootfs. Add tests.
acceptance_criteria: VM.spawn(%{owner_id: X, extra_mounts: [%{tag,shared_dir}]}) produces a VM owned by X with the share mounted; mj exec works on it.
notes: LANDED IN CODE (main, commit 25fef62). Finding: owner_id ALREADY flowed correctly (init/1 sets it; HTTP + internal callers go through it) — added regression tests, not a fix. extra_mounts WAS dropped: build_config/1 never copied :extra_mounts into state.config (VirtioFS.start_many was already correct) -> one-line fix. Guest-side mount is caller's responsibility on a plain base (mount -t virtiofs <tag> <path>). 16 unit tests; extra-virtiofsd startup itself is server/KVM-only.

title: mj domain set/rm/ls + /api/domains — merge-aware custom_domain update + trigger reconcile
description: No CLI/API exists to manage app domains today (only hand-edited gateway.toml). Add 'mj domain set <app> <fqdn>', 'mj domain rm <app>', 'mj domain ls' backed by a new HTTP API, since there is currently no /api/deploy or /api/domains surface at all (router.ex has nothing).
design: API: PUT /api/apps/<app>/domain {fqdn}, DELETE, GET list. Server: merge-aware Registry update (Registry.put appears to REPLACE the Entry from attrs, so read-modify-write to avoid wiping service_vm_id/url/port), set custom_domain+port, then RouteReconciler.trigger(). ls joins registry + live VMs to show app -> fqdn -> backend(guest_ip:port) -> cert status. Composes with 'mj deploy --domain <fqdn>' (gge.1.7).
acceptance_criteria: mj domain set makes the reconciler emit an apps.toml route within a debounce window; mj domain ls shows the mapping; mj domain rm removes the route on next reconcile.
notes: ADD from migration findings: (1) 'mj domain unset <app>' reverse path — clear custom_domain (merge-aware), reconcile (route auto-drops since desired_specs filter fails), optionally prune [[domain]]/[[cert]]. (2) Idempotency/validation — BEFORE setting custom_domain, assert the apex is actually configured (in :gateway_apexes AND has a [[domain]]); otherwise the reconciler silently logs :no_apex and emits NO route (a quiet failure). The CLI must surface this as a hard error, not a silent no-op. (3) render_and_reload() is synchronous (returns the routes) vs trigger() debounced — the API should confirm the route landed in apps.toml before returning success.

title: mj domain — reconciler-driven custom-domain management for deployed apps
description:
Give deployed apps a first-class custom domain via the CLI, driven by the route reconciler so it survives redeploys. Today (proven manually with startupcentral.build, 2026-07-20): routes are set by hand-editing /etc/mjolnir/gateway.toml + SIGHUP; the mj CLI has NO route/domain/app-deploy commands and there is no HTTP API for it. The reconciler machinery (Gateway.Routes/RouteReconciler unions Deploy.Registry.custom_domain + :gateway_extra_domains -> apps.toml, re-derives backend from vm_id on every deploy/VM event) is fully built but nothing populates custom_domain and the apex must be pre-registered in :gateway_apexes.

## Context
Grounded in the startup-central first-customer deploy to mjolnir (2026-07-19/20). startupcentral.build is currently a hand-written gateway.toml [[route]] (pinned to the service VM's guest IP -> breaks on next redeploy); this epic replaces that pattern.
design: End state: 'mj domain set <app> <fqdn>' persists custom_domain on the registry (merge-aware), ensures the apex is registered (gateway_apexes + a [[domain]] + cert in gateway config), and triggers a reconcile. Backend re-derivation is already free from the reconciler. Three sub-problems: (1) persist custom_domain incl. across redeploys, (2) dynamic apex registration without an orchestrator restart, (3) per-domain cert provisioning (ACME if the Cloudflare token covers the zone, else install a provided Cloudflare Origin CA cert via [[cert]]).
acceptance_criteria: mj domain set <app> <fqdn> makes the app serve at <fqdn> with TLS; a subsequent redeploy (new service VM/IP) keeps serving at <fqdn> with NO manual gateway edits; mj domain ls shows app->fqdn->backend->cert; mj domain rm removes it.
notes: STATUS 2026-07-20: startupcentral.build MIGRATED to the reconciler path live (zero downtime) — proves the architecture. But it exposed two live fragilities that this epic must close: (A) redeploy wipes custom_domain [12.1, now P0] and (B) orchestrator restart drops the runtime-only apex [12.3]. Until both ship, startupcentral.build's route survives only as long as there's no app redeploy AND no orchestrator restart (apex held via runtime put_env; route reconciler-managed). config.exs:76 gateway_apexes still lists only the original 3 apexes.

title: Example-app test harness — a fixture app per major deploy feature, driven end-to-end
description: Build a suite of small committed example applications, each exercising one major deploy feature, plus a harness that runs 'mj deploy' against each and asserts the live behavior (URL serves, feature works, redeploy caches, rollback restores). Fixture matrix: (1) hello-sveltekit — stateless adapter-node, the P0 path; (2) bun + native dep (better-sqlite3 w/ trustedDependencies) — validates lifecycle-script handling on target; (3) stateful-sqlite — writes rows across deploys; proves release-dir mode + shared state survives redeploy (gge.7); (4) migrations — drizzle app whose deploy runs a migration, incl. a deliberately failing migration asserting the release aborts and the old version keeps serving; (5) secrets — app that serves an env var injected via secrets_mode: :managed, asserting it survives VM reboot; (6) custom-domain — registry-driven gateway route; (7) later: Procfile/generic-node/python per gge.2. Each fixture doubles as living documentation of what the platform supports. Extends gge.1.8's ExUnit :integration infra; server-gated.

title: DB migrations as a first-class deploy phase — auto-run, never SSH-in-manually
description:
Migrations are where 'automatic feel' lives or dies: if you have to SSH in and run db:migrate by hand, the deploy layer has failed. Add a migrate phase to the deploy pipeline: an optional manifest key (e.g. [deploy] migrate = "bun run db:migrate" in mjolnir.toml, or detected from drizzle/prisma/rails conventions later) that runs against the app's PERSISTENT database after files are in place and before the release goes live (before the symlink flip in release-dir mode / before cutover in fresh-VM mode). Failure aborts the release — the previous release keeps serving, and the error surfaces as an app failure, not a platform one.

Ordering subtleties to design: migrations run in the RUN environment (the stateful VM, where the real db lives), not the build VM — build layers must never touch state (also keeps them cacheable + secret-free per the initiative doc's hard rule). Pair with the pre-deploy btrfs snapshot from gge.7 so a bad migration is state-rollbackable, not just code-rollbackable. Zine's flow (drizzle: bun run db:generate committed, bun run db:migrate applied at deploy) is the reference case.

title: Design: stateful-app deploy model — Capistrano-style releases on a persistent VM
description:
The fresh-VM-per-deploy cutover (Deploy.Runtime P0) wipes on-VM state — a stateful app like Zine keeps its SQLite db (subscribers, send ledger) on the rootfs, so every deploy would destroy it. But statefulness is one of Mjolnir's differentiators: VMs persist, and btrfs snapshots make that persistence cheap and rollbackable. Design a second deploy mode that embraces it.

Proposed model (Capistrano-style, per Duke): the app VM is long-lived; a deploy places the new build into a timestamped release dir (/app/releases/<ts>) and atomically re-points a 'current' symlink; the unit's WorkingDirectory follows the symlink. Rollback = re-point the symlink to the previous release (instant, no rebuild). Transport-agnostic: tar upload, git pull, scp — anything that gets files into the release dir works. Durable state (sqlite db, uploads) lives OUTSIDE releases (e.g. /app/shared) and is linked in, Capistrano-style.

Decide: (1) how this composes with the layer-cache Builder — build in the ephemeral build VM as today, then sync the built artifact into the stateful VM's release dir (build stays cached/reproducible; run VM keeps identity+state)? (2) per-app mode selection: stateless apps keep fresh-VM cutover (immutable, blue/green-ish), stateful apps get release-dir mode — detector/manifest chooses. (3) btrfs snapshot of the app VM pre-deploy as the state-level rollback complement to the symlink flip. (4) health gating before the flip (relates gge.5).
notes: Design direction (discussed 2026-07-01): Capistrano's pointer-flip survives; its two failures (no env reproducibility, shared/-dir-by-convention) are both solved by Mjolnir primitives — layer-cache builder supplies reproducible envs; a NESTED btrfs subvolume for /data is structurally excluded from rootfs snapshots (snapshots aren't recursive), making the durable-state contract filesystem-enforced instead of conventional. Core tension: code rolls back, data rolls forward — keep the axes separately addressable; never auto-revert data. Recommended model: long-lived VM; releases/<ts> + current symlink flip + unit restart (fast path, no reboot); rootfs snapshot pre-flip (safety net, reboot to revert, /data rides through); /data subvolume snapshot pre-migration (restore is manual + operator-confirmed — it discards writes). Migrations run between placement and flip; failure aborts, old release keeps serving; expand/contract as documented contract. SQLite: wal_checkpoint before data snapshots for clean copies. Blue-green = the STATELESS mode (fresh-VM cutover via gateway flip already is it); for local-SQLite apps it's theater (one writer). Steal health-gating for the stateful flip. DEFAULT = stateful — misclassification is asymmetric: stateless-treated-as-stateful accumulates a stale /data; stateful-treated-as-stateless loses the db. Manifest opts into stateless.

Aligns with deploy epic gge.4 Forge-over-vsock direction.

title: vm.ex: :managed mode plumbing, boot unlock, dormancy, escrow lifecycle
description: Parse :managed (router.ex + vm.ex). maybe_unlock_secrets step in do_boot: first boot=gen+escrow+init, wake=read escrow+open. Allow :managed dormancy at vm.ex:836 (keep :persistent refusal). Delete escrow on kill but NOT on handle_done. Protocol.inject_secrets_request helper.

title: Guest agent: vsock inject_secrets action (host-side LUKS delivery)
description: protocol.rs: VsockRequest::InjectSecrets{id,passphrase,init_size_mb?,entries?} + response. vsock.rs dispatch arm calling secrets::{try_claim_injection,init_secrets_volume|open_secrets_volume,load_env_vars,set_env_vars}. Reuses LUKS engine; no Iroh. Builds on server only.
