title: Mjolnir.SecretEscrow — per-VM passphrase escrow off the data volume
description: New module: put/get/delete(vm_id, passphrase) as 0600 atomic files under :secret_escrow_dir (default /var/lib/mjolnir/escrow, OUTSIDE @vms/@snapshots). gen_passphrase/0 (32 random bytes base64). Unit-testable on Mac.
close_reason: Mjolnir.SecretEscrow implemented; 7 unit tests pass on macOS

title: Managed (host-escrowed) secrets mode — dormancy-capable LUKS secrets
description: Add secrets_mode=:managed: host generates a per-VM LUKS passphrase, escrows it on the host OFF the BTRFS data volume (/var/lib/mjolnir/escrow/<vm_id>, 0600), and re-injects it over vsock on boot AND on dormancy wake. Unlike :persistent (passphrase held by a remote Iroh peer, host-blind, refuses dormancy), :managed lets the host autonomously unlock secrets on wake-on-message — enabling scale-to-zero for VMs with secrets. Trade: no host-compromise resistance (accepted for now). Host escrows only the passphrase; the .env content rides inside the snapshotted (ciphertext) LUKS blob, so wake = re-open existing volume.
close_reason: Managed (host-escrowed) secrets mode complete + server-verified end-to-end. Commits 42e16aa (docs) + 938f711 (impl).

title: snapshot of running VM wedges guest + drops it from mj list; revive can't recover
description:
mj snapshot create on a RUNNING VM reports success but (1) can leave the guest wedged (CH pause/resume; sshd/app/Iroh hang while CH vm.info=Running), (2) makes the VM vanish from mj list/info/url, and (3) mj revive reports success but no-ops. Caused ~11min prod outage; only host-root 'curl ... vm.reboot' recovered it.

ROOT CAUSE (code-grounded):
- do_snapshot/3 (lib/mjolnir/vm.ex:1883) does sync->pause->btrfs snapshot->resume but NEVER verifies the guest recovered after resume. Returns success whenever BTRFS.create_snapshot is ok.
- VM.list/0 (vm.ex:189) drops any VM whose GenServer.call(:get_state, 5000) times out (catch :exit -> nil; reject nil). The VM is NOT de-registered — its GenServer mailbox is blocked behind a synchronous vsock call into the wedged guest (likely a Health.Monitor heal). The 5002ms log line is this exact timeout.
- revive/1 (vm.ex:264) only flips StateStore intent=:running. Reconcile.run (reconcile.ex:77,106) skips VMs with a live registry entry. The wedged VM is still registered -> revive is a guaranteed no-op for this failure mode.
- No CH reboot wrapper exists: client.ex has pause/resume/shutdown/delete/info/resize but no reboot_vm; no reboot_instance behaviour callback; no mj reboot/restart command.

FIX PLAN:
1. do_snapshot health-verify: post-resume guest ping; on failure attempt vm.reboot+re-ping; report degraded/error loudly instead of 'created successfully'.
2. list/0 (and info/url): on :get_state timeout include the VM marked degraded/unreachable rather than omitting it.
3. Add reboot plumbing: Client.reboot_vm (PUT /api/v1/vm.reboot) -> reboot_instance callback -> VM.reboot/1 -> POST /api/vms/:id/reboot -> mj reboot/restart.
4. revive/1: detect alive-but-wedged (live GenServer + unreachable guest agent) and reboot+re-attach instead of no-op.
5. Fix ~5s GET /api/vms stall: stop guest-blocking heals from running inside the VM GenServer mailbox / bound+parallelize liveness probes so :get_state is never starved.
notes:
VERIFIED END-TO-END on deployed server (2026-06-26, restart 03:15:58 UTC, incl. 19af2a8):
- spawn -> exec ok
- snapshot create -> success; post-snapshot exec ok (vsock conn rebuild)
- mj reboot -> 'guest healthy, control plane re-attached'; exec after reboot ok with uptime 'up 0 min' (proves clean restart from preserved rootfs, NOT destroyed); VM stays running
- mj revive on healthy live VM -> ok no-op, VM still responsive
- list shows VMs correctly throughout; prod VM 076adf62 untouched
All core fixes confirmed working in production. Reboot race fixed by the terminate-cleanup hardening. Closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Builder executor — boot resume_from, exec+snapshot each layer, teardown (injectable-ops, macOS-unit-tested)
description: The VM/BTRFS execution half of Deploy.Builder, sibling to the pure planner (gge.1.4.1). Mjolnir.Deploy.Builder.build/3 takes base_layer_id + ordered steps (each with precomputed input_hash), derives existing layers from BTRFS snapshots, calls Plan.compute, then: full cache hit -> no VM; else boot one ephemeral VM from resume_from (base image when resume==base, else deploy-<key> snapshot), exec each steps_to_run command via VM.exec and snapshot the result to its content-addressed key, always tear the VM down. Drives VM/BTRFS through an injectable ops seam so the boot->exec->snapshot->teardown choreography is unit-tested on macOS with fakes; real captures (VM.spawn/exec/snapshot/stop, BTRFS.list_snapshots) are server-gated. exec surfaces non-zero exits as {:error,{:exit_code,..}}, so failed build steps abort + teardown.
notes: DONE (macOS half). lib/mjolnir/deploy/builder.ex + test (6 tests, deploy suite 91/0). build/3: list snapshots -> Plan.compute -> full-hit short-circuit (no VM) | else boot ONE ephemeral VM from resume_from (base_image when resume==base, else deploy-<key> snapshot), exec+snapshot each steps_to_run on the live VM (snapshot quiesces+resumes), ALWAYS teardown via try/after. Effects behind injectable ops map (default = VM.spawn/exec/snapshot/stop + BTRFS.list_snapshots); fakes record call order in tests. Layer id <-> 'deploy-'<>key translation owned here; planner stays name-agnostic. exec non-zero exit -> {:error,{:exit_code,..}} aborts build. REMAINING: server integration test (real KVM+BTRFS) tracked on parent gge.1.4.
close_reason: Closed

title: Forgejo runner leaks VMs: teardown StopVM uses cancelled job context, DELETE fails on cancel/timeout/shutdown
description: ROOT CAUSE of the leaked CI VMs (see cdz). native/forgejo-runner/pkg/mjolnir/executor.go VMEnvironment.Remove() issued the StopVM DELETE /api/vms/:id on the inherited job context. act runs Remove/Close via Finally(), so on a cancelled job, a timed-out job, or a runner restart (shutdown force-cancels in-progress jobs with shutdown_timeout=0s — confirmed in journalctl), the ctx is already cancelled and net/http fails the DELETE immediately with 'context canceled'. The VM is never destroyed; Mjolnir durability (r84) then resurrects the orphaned :running record on every restart, so owner=localhost CI VMs accumulate (found 16 live leaked on root@45.76.77.97, 2026-06-24). Normal completions clean up fine (live ctx), so it is a slow leak.
design: Detach teardown from the job context: context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60s) for the StopVM DELETE so cleanup always reaches the API even when the inherited ctx is dead. Mjolnir client carries its own base-URL/auth (localhost bypass), so dropping inherited ctx values is safe. Fixes both Remove() and Close() (Close calls Remove).
acceptance_criteria: A cancelled or timed-out CI job still results in its VM being destroyed (mj list / localhost /api/vms returns to baseline); runner restart during a job does not leak the job's VM.
notes:
REOPENED BY EVIDENCE 2026-08-12: the runner-restart path is NOT fixed. The 725f802 detached-context fix addresses Remove() being CALLED with a dead ctx; it cannot help when Remove() never runs at all.

REPRODUCED deliberately (identikey/mjolnir run 10, VM 50ef47c4-f26e-4e01-aa89-09e628810530, base ci-ubuntu-24.04, owner localhost). Exact journal sequence:

  15:57:48  runner: received shutdown signal
  15:57:48  shutdown_timeout=0s -> 'forcing the jobs to shutdown'
  15:57:48  [poller] shutdown begin, 1 tasks currently running
  15:57:48  [mjolnir-exec] ERROR: Post http://127.0.0.1:4000/api/vms/50ef47c4.../exec: context canceled
  (90s gap — the runner never exits)
  15:59:18  systemd: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing. SIGKILL, status=9/KILL

TWO DEFECTS, the first causing the second:
1. The runner HANGS on shutdown. It does not exit after force-cancelling jobs; it sits until systemd's TimeoutStopSec (90s, the default — the unit sets no override) and is SIGKILLed. A SIGKILLed process runs no deferred cleanup, so the 60s detached-context StopVM never fires.
2. The VM therefore leaks. 8 minutes later 50ef47c4 was still :running with the repo checked out and no build process — a pure orphan. Durability then resumes it across restarts, which is precisely how 16 leaked VMs accumulated on 2026-06-24.

So the acceptance criterion 'runner restart during a job does not leak the job's VM' FAILS. The normal-completion path remains fine (run 9 completed and its VM was destroyed).

DIRECTION (needs a decision, not filed as fixed): fixing the hang alone is not enough — SIGKILL, a host crash, or an OOM kill all bypass in-process cleanup by construction. Client-side teardown cannot be the only guarantee. The robust fix is server-side: give CI-spawned VMs a lease/TTL that Mjolnir reaps when the owning runner stops renewing, so no client death can strand a VM. Fixing the shutdown hang (and/or setting TimeoutStopSec) is worth doing as defence in depth, not as the answer.
close_reason:
Closed by the server-side lease (mjolnir-urp, deployed 2026-08-12). The original client-side fix (725f802, detached context for StopVM) handles a cancelled job whose process still lives, but I reproduced its limit today: systemd SIGKILLed the runner after it hung 90s on shutdown, and a SIGKILLed process runs no deferred cleanup at all, so no client-side change could ever have covered it. The guarantee is now server-side and independent of the client's survival.

PROVEN LIVE IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-12, both paths:

HAPPY PATH (run 16, clean completion): the runner tore its own VM down, VM count returned to baseline 4, and ZERO CILease reclamations fired — the lease correctly stayed a backstop rather than the primary mechanism.

FAILURE PATH (deliberate): spawned a throwaway VM tagged purpose=ci, backdated its lease_expires_at by 120s, and the real production Health.Monitor sweep reclaimed it on the next tick:
  [warning] CILease: reclaiming CI VM 3f048573-... (metadata=%{"purpose" => "ci", "repo" => "lease-proof", "run_id" => "manual-24r"}), lease expired 123s ago
Its rootfs went to @trash (restorable=true via POST /api/trash/:id/restore), NOT hard-deleted, and the sidecar carries purpose=ci so it reaps at 24h rather than 7 days. All 4 production VMs were untouched throughout — they carry empty metadata and cannot match either gate.

BOUND, stated honestly: reclamation is not instant. An abandoned VM is reclaimed within the 60-minute lease TTL (chosen to match the runner's own timeout: 1h and to exceed the longest single exec — a cold cargo build is ONE 6m14s exec with no API traffic, so a shorter TTL would reap live jobs). If instant reclamation is ever wanted, the runner should send an explicit release on job end and the lease becomes a pure backstop; filed nowhere yet, mentioned in mjolnir-urp.

title: Builder cache-decision planner (pure, macOS-verifiable) — step chain + existing layers → resume point + steps to run
description: The pure core of Deploy.Builder, extractable and unit-testable with no VM. Given a base layer id, an ordered list of build steps (each with a precomputed input_hash), and the set of already-existing layer ids, compute: the chained cache_key per layer (via Mjolnir.Deploy.CacheKey.compute, chaining parent→child), which layers are cache HITS vs MISSES, the deepest contiguous cached prefix (resume_from), the steps that still need to run, and the final release_layer_id. Key property to lock in tests: because keys chain on the parent layer id, the hit set is ALWAYS a contiguous prefix — a downstream key can never spuriously hit once an ancestor changed. The VM/BTRFS execution half of gge.1.4 (boot resume_from, run steps via VM.exec, snapshot each) stays open and server-gated.
notes: Pure function over data; caller precomputes input_hash with CacheKey.hash_file/hash_tree (keeps FS access out of the planner). Defines the data shape the server-side executor will consume.
close_reason: Mjolnir.Deploy.Builder.Plan implemented: pure cache-decision planner (chained keys, structural contiguous-prefix hit invariant, resume_from/steps_to_run/release_layer_id). 9 tests incl. the downstream-key-must-not-hit case. VM/BTRFS execution half of gge.1.4 stays open + server-gated.

title: Deploy.Builder — run ordered build plan in ephemeral VM, snapshot + cache each layer
description: The frame of the deploy layer. Given a build plan: boot an ephemeral VM from the base (or parent layer on cache hit = reflink clone + skip), run each step via Mjolnir.VM.exec, snapshot the result via VM.snapshot/Mjolnir.BTRFS, content-address it with the cache-key module. Cache hit → reflink clone + advance; miss → boot parent, run step, snapshot. Discard the ephemeral build VM; promote the final layer as the release. Ephemeral-build-then-promote.
notes: INTEGRATION VERIFIED on server (45.76.77.97) 2026-06-25 via live-node rpc scenario (synthetic marker steps). Evidence: build1_cold={0 hit,3 miss,3 built}; build2_noop={3 hit,0 miss,0 built} + log 'full cache hit (3 layers)' = NO VM booted; build3_tail={2 hit,1 miss,1 built}, log 'resume from %{snapshot: deploy-84c1..}, 1 step to run' = reflink-resumed from L2; release_same_1_2=true; release_changed_3=true; booted release files={l1,l2,v2} (cached L1/L2 carried forward, only tail reran). All 4 deploy-* snapshots cleaned up. Committed test: test/mjolnir/deploy/builder_integration_test.exs (:integration, ExUnit form). NOTE: server MIX_ENV=test btrfs infra (@base-test/@vms-test symlinks) is dangling, so the ExUnit form needs a populated isolated btrfs root to run; live-rpc-in-prod-node was used instead. gge.1.4 acceptance MET.
close_reason: Closed

title: Deploy layer cache-key module — hash(parent_layer_id + step_cmd + input_hash)
description: Pure content-addressing for the snapshot layer cache. cache_key(parent_layer_id, step_command, input_hash). 'npm ci'-class steps key on the lockfile hash; 'build'-class steps key on the source-tree hash (respecting .gitignore/.dockerignore). Deterministic, stable across runs. This is the 'get cache-key correctness right early' piece the design doc flags as subtly-wrong-until-battle-tested.
notes: macOS-VERIFIABLE: pure hashing, exhaustive mix tests (same inputs→same key; any input change→new key; ordering matters). No VM.
close_reason: Mjolnir.Deploy.CacheKey implemented: SHA256(SHA256(parent)‖SHA256(cmd)‖SHA256(input)), fixed-width inner digests defeat boundary collisions; hash_file/hash_tree (sorted, exclusion-aware). 30 tests green.

title: Deploy.Detector (P0: SvelteKit/adapter-node only) — dir → fixed build plan, PM from lockfile
description: Minimal hardcoded detector for the P0 slice: assume a SvelteKit/adapter-node app, detect the package manager FROM THE LOCKFILE (bun.lock→bun, pnpm-lock.yaml→pnpm, package-lock.json→npm; default npm), and emit a fixed build plan struct {runtime: node@20 via mise, steps: [mise install, <pm> install, <pm> run build], start: node build/index.js, port: 3000}. Pure function over a directory listing — no VM, no network.
notes: macOS-VERIFIABLE: pure file inspection, full mix test coverage with fixture dirs. This is the seam that generalizes in gge.2 (P1).
close_reason: Mjolnir.Deploy.Detector + BuildPlan struct implemented; lockfile-based PM detection (bun>pnpm>yarn>npm). macOS unit tests green.

title: P0 — Prove the wow: hardcoded SvelteKit path, snapshot-layer builder + cache, mj deploy → URL
description: First vertical slice. Hardcode the SvelteKit/adapter-node path (no general detection yet). Build the snapshot-layer Builder: run an ordered build plan in an ephemeral VM, snapshot+content-address each step, reflink-clone on cache hit. Boot the release snapshot as a service VM and return the gateway HTTPS URL. No manifest, no rollback. Goal: FEEL the instant rebuild (L1/L2 cache hit, only L3 reruns on a one-line change).
design: Cache key = hash(parent_layer_id + step_command + relevant_input_hash); npm ci keys on package-lock.json, build keys on source tree hash. Ephemeral-build-then-promote. Get cache-key correctness right early — it's the subtly-wrong-until-battle-tested part.
acceptance_criteria: mj deploy in a SvelteKit/adapter-node repo returns a live HTTPS URL; a no-op re-deploy is a full cache hit; a one-line src change reruns only the final layer.
notes: FIELD-VALIDATED end-to-end 2026-07-19/20: startup-central (SvelteKit/adapter-node/bun) built via Builder-equivalent steps in a microVM -> release snapshot startup-central-r1 -> Runtime.start service VM (256MB) -> live at ticket URL, then custom apex startupcentral.build. Confirms the pipeline design. Remaining glue to close gge.1: /api/deploy (gge.1.6), mj deploy client (gge.1.7), + the new ingest/owner_id and base-image gaps. Secrets: managed mode times out Runtime.start's 30s await_boot (LUKS boot too slow) -> used a systemd EnvironmentFile drop-in instead (see gge.10).

title: mj deploy — Heroku-style 'git push and it's live' app deploy layer (snapshot-layer PaaS)
description: Implement the 'mj deploy' layer specified in docs/plans/initiatives/mjolnir-deploy.md. In an app dir, 'mj deploy' should — zero-config for the common case — build the app inside a microVM, snapshot every build step (BTRFS reflink layer cache) so rebuilds are instant, boot the result as a supervised service, and return a live HTTPS URL. Builds on Forge (run-state reconciliation, NOT the chassis), Sites, gateway, mise, and the VM snapshot/dormancy machinery. The frame is a NEW snapshot-layer builder; Forge is a component. Child tasks track the doc's phasing P0–P3 plus the parallel recrypt track.
design: Two-phase model (load-bearing): BUILD is imperative/ordered/non-idempotent → snapshot-layer builder (each step → content-addressed BTRFS snapshot, cache key = hash(parent_layer + step_cmd + input_hash)); RUN-STATE is declarative/convergent → Forge resources (systemd_unit/file/user) reconciled inside the guest over vsock exec. New modules: Mjolnir.Deploy.Supervisor {Detector, Builder, Runtime, Registry}, POST /api/deploy, 'mj deploy' client subcommand (distinct from existing 'mj server deploy' which runs scripts/deploy.sh).
notes: No code exists yet as of 2026-06-24. Design doc at docs/plans/initiatives/mjolnir-deploy.md (commits 6ecab5f, 9d74b8e, 56ec216). Decided: tar-the-cwd source ingest (front door) + first-class private-repo deploy-key pull; qgroup-metered layer GC with two GC classes; secrets re-inject on wake + render-to-tmpfs now, recrypt-to-VM-key as end-state. Resist scope gravity into a general PaaS — the zero-config moment is the product, not feature count.

title: StartupReconcile blocks API availability proportional to VM count
description: During server verification of mjolnir-r84: with 18 stranded :running records, the blocking StartupReconcile child resumes all VMs synchronously (~3s each) BEFORE Bandit/the HTTP API starts, so the public API was unreachable for ~60s after restart (connection refused). Make reconcile non-blocking (or parallelize resumes, or start the API before reconcile) so API availability is independent of stranded-VM count. Found while verifying the durability epic on root@45.76.77.97.
design: Two levers, both applied: (1) StartupReconcile child changed from blocking Mjolnir.Startup.run to a concurrent {Task,:start_link,...} so the supervisor reaches Bandit immediately — ordering still holds since Cleanup sweep + registries are earlier siblings; (2) Reconcile.run/0 resumes via Task.async_stream with :reconcile_max_concurrency (default 4, timeout :infinity) instead of serial Enum.each; (3) execute/1 wraps resume in try/catch so an await_boot exit can't abort the async_stream batch. Stranded VMs already show state=recovering in /api/vms; Health.Monitor 30s tick is the safety net.
close_reason: Implemented in 845a1a3 (branch fix/s8h-reconcile-nonblocking): reconcile off the blocking boot path + bounded-parallel resumes. 613 unit tests pass. Full server-restart-with-stranded-VMs verification rides the pending r84 KVM integration run.

title: Classify transient boot failures and route fresh-spawn recovery through Reconcile
description: Transient virtiofsd/CH start failures (ENOMEM/EMFILE/EAGAIN/addr-in-use) are treated like permanent ones. On a transient FRESH-spawn boot failure, persist a :running StateStore record and preserve the rootfs (don't trash) so Health.Monitor+Reconcile retries it. Finding 4.
close_reason: transient_boot_error?/1 classifier; fresh-spawn transient boot failures now preserve rootfs + persist :running record so Reconcile retries instead of trashing.

title: Cleanup orphan sweep must fail SAFE (preserve on unknown lookup)
description: cleanup.ex safe_state_lookup returns :not_found (=>delete) when StateStore lookup raises, and the sweep enumerates @vms treating every dir as a candidate. Make it return :unknown=>preserve, skip reserved dot-dirs (.trash), and soft-delete (trash) genuine orphans. Finding 3.
close_reason: safe_state_lookup returns :unknown=>preserve (was :not_found=>delete); reserved dot-dir skip; genuine orphans soft-deleted via trash.

title: Publish flow must auto-register identity (HEAD rejected with :identity_not_registered)
description:
Live e2e on 45.76.77.97 (rpc Publisher.publish): snapshot accept + chunk upload + serve all work, but HEAD update 500s with :identity_not_registered. SecretStore.verify_signed_record requires a previously-stored 'identity/pubkey' bootstrap record (self-authenticating: fingerprint(embedded pubkey)==fp, no signature). Publisher.publish and mix mjolnir.publish never deposit it, so first-time publish fails — breaks the whole newcomer UX.

VERIFIED FIX SHAPE: registering the identity inline (SecretStore.put(fp, 'identity/pubkey', %{pubkey: base64(ed25519_public)})) then publishing → full roundtrip 200 + body_matches:true.

TODO: (1) add HTTP route to deposit the self-authenticating identity record, e.g. PUT /api/sites/:fp/identity; (2) Publisher.publish PUTs it (idempotent) before post_snapshot/post_head; (3) test. Then redeploy + re-run e2e via mix mjolnir.publish (no manual register).
notes: FIX COMMITTED 77e9fa7 (not yet deployed). Added PUT /api/sites/:fp/identity + Publisher.publish auto-registers (idempotent) before snapshot. Router tests cover register-unblocks-HEAD + fingerprint-mismatch-400. Full suite 608/0. NEEDS REDEPLOY to take effect on server, then re-run live e2e via the CLk (no manual register): mix mjolnir.publish should succeed first-try. NOTE: live test left an orphaned test site + registered identity on server under a random fp (harmless, tiny; GC later).
close_reason: Deployed (40160ce) + LIVE-VERIFIED on 45.76.77.97: first-time publish with fresh IdentiKey and NO manual registration → {:ok, seq 1, snapshot 2Mco...}; serve 200, body_matches:true. Auto-register (PUT /:fp/identity) works end-to-end.

title: Storage seam: Sites.Store → recrypt-storage (NIF vs sidecar spike + impl)
description:
Replace the STUBBED local Elixir chunk store (Mjolnir.Sites.Store, lib/mjolnir/sites/store.ex — verify_bao! is stubbed) with calls into recrypt-storage, which already implements content-addressed put/get WITH Bao outboards (put_with_outboard/get_with_outboard) and is e2e-tested against Minio.

## Why
The hardest stub (Bao outboard content-addressing) is already done and tested in Rust. Reimplementing it in Elixir is wasted effort and a second crypto implementation to keep correct.

## Spike first (the real decision)
Prove Sites.Store can round-trip ONE chunk (put_with_outboard then get_with_outboard, verifying hash) through recrypt-storage. Decide integration shape:
- NIF (rustler) — in-process, fastest, but couples BEAM to OpenFHE/aws-sdk build.
- Sidecar (recrypt-server HTTP, already exists) — looser coupling, network hop, separate process to supervise.
Recommend trying sidecar first (recrypt-server already runs an HTTP API) unless latency demands a NIF.

## Acceptance
- Sites.Store.put/get delegate to recrypt-storage (no stubbed verify).
- Bao verification is real (bytes failing hash never land).
- Round-trip test passes against a local backend.
- Decision (NIF vs sidecar) recorded in the issue + design doc.
notes: DEPLOYABILITY: prod compile exit 0; full mix test 600/0; Sites.Supervisor boots safe (default backend = Sites.Storage.Local, recrypt backend only if MJOLNIR_RECRYPT_STORAGE_URL set). SERVER RUNBOOK to go live: (1) in recrypt repo, add 4 content-addressed chunk routes to recrypt-server that round-trip a PRECOMPUTED outboard: PUT/GET /storage/blob/b3/{hash} and {hash}.obao (1:1 with put/get_with_outboard); current POST /files is multisig-gated, hashes server-side, stores empty outboard. (2) build+run recrypt-server on 45.76.77.97. (3) export MJOLNIR_RECRYPT_STORAGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7222. (4) validate: mix test test/mjolnir/sites/storage/recrypt_test.exs --include recrypt_storage.

comments.author: Duke Jones
comments.text: Live wiring no longer waits on recrypt-server /files. The blob door (mjolnir-u8v7) already speaks PUT/GET /storage/blob/b3/{hash} and .obao — the contract Sites.Storage.Recrypt expects. Cutover is mjolnir-u8v7.4 once the door is up. Do not grow recrypt-server /files as a second door.

title: Complete IdentiKey Sites: real publish path (storage→crypto→keyspace→transport→CLI)
description:
Make IdentiKey Sites actually work end-to-end so a user can: get an Iroh address, sign content with their IdentiKey, and publish static assets publicly / to recipients / to a keyspace — with everything durably backed by Backblaze B2.

## Why
Sites is a carefully-shaped scaffold with stubbed security-critical guts (Bao verify, manifest/HEAD signing, decrypt, Iroh bind all STUBBED). The design (docs/plans/initiatives/identikey-sites.md) is sound and the hard crypto already exists in ~/work/IdentiKey/recrypt. The work is integration, not invention.

## Layering (confirmed against both repos)
- Storage / 'Vault' = recrypt-storage crate (local.rs/s3.rs, aws_sdk_s3, outboard-aware, e2e-tested vs Minio). B2 = same code, B2 endpoint.
- Keyspace / recipients = identikey-storage-auth crate (keyspace.rs, capability.rs, grant.rs) + recrypt-core PRE (post-quantum).
- Serving / naming / provenance = Mjolnir.Sites (Iroh endpoint, HEAD pointer, OpenTimestamps, gateway).

## Product principle (drives the CLI child)
Common case must require ZERO special vocabulary: 'mjolnir publish ./dist' is public-by-default and returns a URL. Verifiability is a property you GET, not a feature you invoke. Recipients/keyspace are progressive-disclosure flags. No Norse codenames in the user surface; module stays Mjolnir.Sites internally.

## B2 invariant
Every published chunk + manifest must eventually land in Backblaze B2 (durable offsite). Local FS/BTRFS is the hot tier; B2 is the durable backing via recrypt-storage's S3 backend (endpoint_url + force_path_style, same as its minio() ctor).

## Out of critical path
OpenTimestamps (anchoring) and BTRFS-send replication stay deferred — not required for publish+serve.

## Related (do not duplicate)
mjolnir-89y (PG backfill), mjolnir-fn4 (HeadIndex hot serve), mjolnir-3ku (vault package mirror).
notes: LIVE STATUS (2026-06-23): Public-mode publish fully working in prod. Deploy clean (iroh 1.0 guest-agent rebuild OK, NRestarts=0, Bandit bound after 17-VM reconcile ~68s). E2E verified: signing (.3), Local storage (.1), serve/decrypt, and auto-register (.7) all green live. DONE: .2 (B2 scripts, install pending), .3, .6, .7. REMAINING (server-side): .1 go-live (4 recrypt-server chunk routes for recrypt/B2 backend — Local backend works today), .4 host Iroh bind (note: iroh now 1.0), .5 keyspace/recipient modes. Orphaned tiny test sites left in @sites under random fps (e2e/e2e2) — GC later.

title: VM cannot reach host Forgejo (localhost:3000 unreachable from VM)
description: UPDATED: Multi-step itself works fine (confirmed run 15/18 both succeeded with 2+ steps). The actual issue is VM→host networking: Forgejo listens on 127.0.0.1:3000 which is unreachable from inside the VM. Steps that call the Forgejo API (package upload, action checkout) fail because the VM's localhost is itself, not the host. Fix options: (1) Make Forgejo also listen on the TAP bridge IP or 0.0.0.0, (2) Add a host-IP env var injected into VMs, (3) Use the public IP (45.76.77.97) in FORGEJO_SERVER_URL config. Also: actions/checkout needs network to clone — must ensure VM has outbound connectivity to the host. Additionally update CI image to include: mjolnir-agent service, mjolnir-network-setup script (both were missing from the debootstrap build).
close_reason: Fixed: VM→host networking via dummy interface (10.255.255.1) + UFW allow from 10.0.0.0/8. Forgejo bound to 0.0.0.0. Multi-step was never broken — the failures were network connectivity and missing Node.js action support.

title: Proper Git fork of forgejo-runner (replace Python patches)
description: Replace the brittle Python-patch-on-clone approach with a proper Git fork. Maintain github.com/identikey/forgejo-runner as a real fork with our changes as 3 commits on a branch: (1) add pkg/mjolnir/ Container impl, (2) wire into act/runner/run_context.go (IsMjolnirEnv, startMjolnirEnvironment), (3) add SchemeMjolnir to labels.go. Rebase on upstream tags for upgrades. Delete: scripts/patch-runner.py, scripts/patch-runner-labels.py, native/forgejo-runner/cmd/ stub, native/forgejo-runner/act-inlined/ duplicate. Keep only pkg/mjolnir/executor.go + client.go as canonical. Update deploy.sh to git pull the fork instead of clone+patch.
close_reason: Fork at mimir.worldtree.network/identikey/forgejo-runner, mjolnir branch with 2 clean commits. deploy.sh updated to clone fork instead of patch. Python scripts and duplicate files deleted.

title: Fix syslog vsock transport: route through guest agent channel 2
description: The guest-side syslog-vsock-forwarder.sh uses socat VSOCK-CONNECT:2:5001 (direct vsock connection to host port 5001), but the host-side Syslog.Listener receives data on vsock protocol channel 2 (the multiplexed binary channel within Mjolnir.Vsock.Connection). There is no raw vsock listener on port 5001 — the guest forwarder will get connection refused. Fix: add a syslog forwarding mode to the Rust guest agent (native/mjolnir_guest_agent) that reads from /dev/log and sends lines over vsock channel 2 using the existing wire protocol. Update scripts/ci-image/syslog-vsock.service to start the guest agent in syslog-forwarder mode instead of socat. Remove the socat-based forwarder script.
close_reason: Guest agent now binds /dev/log and forwards syslog on vsock channel 2. Socat forwarder removed.

title: Add hypervisor selection config — :cloud_hypervisor or :none
description: New config key (likely under :mjolnir, :hypervisor) selecting the backend. When :none, skip /dev/kvm validation, skip Cloud Hypervisor REST socket setup, skip BTRFS reflink checks. Allows the app to boot on hosts without virtualization. Document in config/runtime.exs and docs/hardware-requirements.md §7.
acceptance_criteria: App starts on a host with no /dev/kvm when hypervisor: :none is set. App still starts normally with hypervisor: :cloud_hypervisor on a KVM host.

title: Mjolnir.Worker.Port — supervise OS process via OTP Port
description: New Worker implementation managing a Linux process as an OTP Port. Lifecycle: spawn (start command, attach Port, monitor exit), get_status (running/exited/crashed + exit_code), stop (graceful SIGTERM with timeout then SIGKILL). Config per-worker: command, args, env, cwd, restart strategy. Integrate with existing DynamicSupervisor. Structured logging with metadata worker_type=:port, worker_id, os_pid.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for spawn/normal-exit/crash/restart. Manual test: long-running echo loop, kill -9 it, verify restart.

title: Define Mjolnir.Worker behaviour
description: Introduce a behaviour module abstracting 'a thing Mjolnir supervises.' Callbacks: spawn(args), get_status(ref), stop(ref), exec(ref, cmd) (optional), snapshot(ref) (optional). Both microVM workers and Port workers will implement this. Foundation for the OTP-only profile — without this, CloudHypervisor assumptions leak through the lifecycle code in lib/mjolnir/vm/*.
acceptance_criteria: Behaviour module compiles. @callback definitions documented. No existing implementations changed yet.

title: OTP-only deployment profile — supervise host processes without Cloud Hypervisor
description: Enable Mjolnir to deploy in environments where the full hypervisor profile is impossible (containerized GPU rentals — RunPod, Vast.ai, Modal — and other no-KVM environments). Introduce a Mjolnir.Worker behaviour with two implementations: CloudHypervisor (existing microVM path, refactored) and Port (new — supervises an OS process via OTP Port). Preserve the orchestration semantics that matter (supervised lifecycle, structured failure recovery, Iroh-tunneled HTTP API, unified control plane) while giving up the microVM isolation that isn't achievable in tenant containers. First consumer: a GPU inference workload (vLLM serving Qwen 3.5) on a RunPod pod, controlled via the same Mjolnir API surface that fronts the bare-metal node at 45.76.77.97. Defined in docs/hardware-requirements.md §7 (currently forward-looking — this epic implements it).

title: forge: adopt the Mjolnir host (fix 2026-05-11 audit drift)

Also added sysctl ip_forward and mjolnir-gateway.service. ReadWritePaths updated for ufw/sysctl write access.

description: Elixir: Diff property test (every matrix cell), Declarations loader unit tests, SystemdUnit canonical-encoding stability test, Host GenServer reconcile-loop test with stubbed transport, API integration test (full plan→apply cycle against a sandbox host root). title: forge: Rust CLI (plan/apply/adopt/diff/fzf)
description: Extend Rust CLI with 'mjolnir forge' subcommand tree. New src/forge/ module: mod.rs, api.rs (HTTP via reqwest reusing SSH-tunnel pattern from connect.rs), plan.rs, apply.rs, adopt.rs, diff.rs, fzf.rs. Commands: plan, apply [--only K] [--resource X], diff <res>, adopt [--fzf], ignore <res>, probe, hosts, events. Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 drift, 2 errors.
design: fzf is opt-in via --fzf or stdout.is_terminal() && which::which("fzf").is_ok(). ~80 LOC fzf wrapper streams tab-separated rows to fzf's stdin. CLI never knows what SQLite is; it renders responses from /api/forge/*.
acceptance_criteria: 'mjolnir forge plan' prints colored status table. 'mjolnir forge apply' converges :new/:drifted/:missing/:prune; returns 1 on drift, 2 on errors. 'mjolnir forge adopt --fzf' lets user pick from unmanaged list (fzf if on PATH, dialoguer::Select fallback).

Subcommands verified: 'mjolnir forge plan --host H', 'forge apply --host H [--yes --all-safe --resource KIND/ID]', 'forge state', 'forge hosts list', 'forge hosts add HOST [--transport ssh]'. title: forge: HTTP API (/api/forge/*)
description: Mount Mjolnir.Forge.API under Mjolnir.API.Router. Endpoints: GET /state (filterable host/kind/status), GET /plan (force re-observe + return diff), POST /apply ({resources, dry_run}), GET /diff/:host/:kind/:id, POST /adopt, POST /ignore, GET /events, GET /hosts, POST /hosts. CBOR by default, ?fmt=json for human inspection. Localhost auth bypass like VM endpoints.
design: CBOR via :cbor hex package. SSE events stream (/events/stream) is a v1 ticket. All bodies negotiate via Accept; SSE frames are JSON for text/event-stream compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: curl localhost:4000/api/forge/state?fmt=json returns valid JSON with the resource table. POST /api/forge/apply with dry_run=true returns per-resource intended actions without mutating disk. Authorization works the same as /api/vm/* (localhost bypass via SSH tunnel).

CBOR deferred to v1; JSON only for v0. Compiles + boots cleanly. Forge.API.diff/adopt/ignore/events deferred to v1 (TUI-driven endpoints).

title: forge: Host GenServer + reconcile loop
description: Mjolnir.Forge.Host (GenServer, one per managed host, started under Mjolnir.Forge.HostSupervisor as :transient). State: host id, transport (:local|:ssh), interval_ms, auto_apply. handle_info(:reconcile) → observe_all → Diff.compute → Repo upsert → EventBus broadcast → optionally apply_safe_actions for :new/:drifted/:missing/:prune. Default interval 60s.
design: apply_safe_actions/2 explicitly excludes :conflict and :unmanaged — those always require human ack. Local transport uses File.read!/System.cmd directly; SSH transport is a v1 ticket. Host worker is :transient — one crashing host doesn't take out the rest (mirrors VMSupervisor).
acceptance_criteria: Starting a Host with transport=:local for 'self' against a declarations file containing one systemd_unit produces a Repo row with status=:new (if absent on disk) or :converged (if matches). :conflict and :unmanaged are NEVER auto-applied.
close_reason: Landed: Mjolnir.Forge.Host GenServer with plan/1 and apply/2. Uses :transient restart under HostSupervisor (DynamicSupervisor). Auto-apply defaults false per blast-radius decision (mjolnir-3il). :conflict and :unmanaged never auto-resolved. SSH transport stubbed (returns :ssh_transport_not_implemented_yet) — deferred to mjolnir-jl1.

Supports systemd_unit/2 macro for v0 (other kinds added with their tickets).
design: Open question per doc: forge/declarations/ vs config/. Going with forge/declarations/<host>.exs for now — keeps unit-file content diffable as separate files referenced via File.read! from declarations. Decision flagged separately.
acceptance_criteria: A forge/declarations/<host>.exs with two systemd_unit blocks evaluates to a list of 2 declared resources retrievable via Mjolnir.Forge.Declarations.for_host("<host>"). Editing the file triggers a reload event on the EventBus.

File-watching is a v1 ticket.

title: forge: Diff engine (three-way compute)
description: Mjolnir.Forge.Diff.compute/3 takes (declared, owned, observed) maps keyed by {kind, id} and returns a list of {kind, id, status, declared_hash, owned_hash, observed_hash} per the design's 8-row matrix. Statuses: converged, drifted, missing, new, prune, conflict, unmanaged, plus the (cleared-ownership) tombstone row.
design: Pure function — no I/O, no DB. Takes hashes (or content + hash). Caller upserts results into Repo. This is the load-bearing piece of the design; keep it side-effect-free so it's trivially testable.
acceptance_criteria: Property test: every (declared,owned,observed) cell of {present,absent} × {present,absent} × {present,differs,absent} maps to the documented status. Unit test: a 3-resource declared set + a 1-resource owned set + a 5-resource observed set produces correct row classifications.
close_reason: Landed: Mjolnir.Forge.Diff.compute/3 — pure function over the 8-row matrix. Auto-adopt-on-exact-match implemented (decision per mjolnir-f7e). 11 unit tests cover every matrix cell + content propagation + multi-key fanout. 0 failures.

title: forge: Resource behaviour + SystemdUnit impl
description: Define Mjolnir.Forge.Resource behaviour (kind/0, id/1, canonical/1, observe_path/1, probe/2, apply/2, delete/2). Implement Mjolnir.Forge.Resource.SystemdUnit using {:file, /etc/systemd/system/<id>} observe, with apply = cp + systemctl daemon-reload + enable, delete = systemctl disable + rm. Canonical encoding uses :cbor with deterministic key ordering (RFC 8949 §4.2.1).
design: File-backed observe is preferred (cheap, uniform). Behaviour shape produces {:present, content} | :missing | {:error, _} from observe_one/3 regardless of path — diff engine doesn't branch on file vs probe.
acceptance_criteria: SystemdUnit can observe an existing unit file, produce a stable canonical CBOR encoding (same input → same bytes → same blake3 hash across runs), apply a new unit, and delete it. Behaviour callbacks documented.
notes: ~180 LOC for behaviour + SystemdUnit. New kinds in later tickets reuse this shape.
close_reason: Landed: Mjolnir.Forge.Resource behaviour with observe/3 dispatcher (file-backed vs probe) + Mjolnir.Forge.Resource.SystemdUnit (writes /etc/systemd/system/<id>, daemon-reload + enable + restart on apply, disable+rm on delete; v0 file-backed only). Canonical encoding via Mjolnir.Forge.Canonical (sorted-key JSON + SHA-256, no new deps).

title: forge: Supervisor + Repo + Ecto migrations
description: Mjolnir.Forge.Supervisor (one_for_one) under Mjolnir.Supervisor with: Mjolnir.Forge.Repo (Ecto + ecto_sqlite3, pool_size: 1, WAL mode), migrations for resources/events/host_meta schemas, SQLite at /var/lib/mjolnir/forge/state.db. Indexes on (host), (host,status), unique (host,kind,resource_id).

acceptance_criteria: App boots with Forge supervision tree. Repo migrates cleanly. Inserting/selecting a resources row via Repo works in iex. Survives BEAM restart (WAL recovery).

Following codebase convention — Forge.Store mirrors StateStore pattern at /var/lib/mjolnir/forge/state/<host>/<kind>_<id>.json. Canonical encoding: Jason with sorted keys. Hash: :crypto.hash(:sha256, ...) — no :cbor or :b3 dep needed.

title: Forge: host config reconciler (umbrella)
description: Mjolnir.Forge is a declarative host config reconciler with three-way diff (declared/owned/observed), ownership tracking for prune, file+probe observe strategies, CBOR-over-HTTP API, Rust CLI, and (later) ratatui TUI. Design in docs/plans/host-reconcile.md (2026-05-12). v0 fixes the four drift items found in the 2026-05-11 host audit.
design: Three-way diff matrix is the entire state machine. Hash everything (blake3+canonical CBOR), materialize content only for diff display. Reconciler is server-side BEAM; Rust CLI is thin HTTP client over SSH-tunneled localhost — same pattern as 'mjolnir vm-spawn'. Apply is idempotent destroy-then-create. Ownership distinguishes prune from leave-alone — without it, removal is impossible.
acceptance_criteria: v0: 'mjolnir forge plan/apply/adopt --fzf' works against self host for systemd_unit kind. v1: full kind set + TUI + SSE + second (SSH) host. v2: on-host agent, HA controllers, web UI.

title: serial-getty@ttyS0 holds ubuntu snapshot boots for 90s
description:
ubuntu-24.04 (and deploy-node-bun) enable `serial-getty@ttyS0` with autologin. A *fresh* `mj spawn` of ubuntu-24.04 reached PTY-ready in ~5s.

Identikey 2026-08-27: after Builder snapshot of a running ubuntu build VM, Runtime.start of that snapshot hung in the guest serial log:

  Job dev-ttyS0.device/start running (42s / 1min 30s)
  … up through 1min 2s …

Managed-secrets unlock then failed `:timeout` (~60s) even though Iroh identity had already logged. Masking the getty on the snapshot (`ln -sfn /dev/null /etc/systemd/system/serial-getty@ttyS0.service`) was part of making the next Runtime.start work (together with copying a current agent).

`build-rootfs-ubuntu-24.04.sh` and `build-deploy-base.sh` both enable this getty. MicroVMs should not block boot on a serial device CH may not attach the same way on snapshot-spawn vs base-spawn.

Separate from bhcr (missing agent binary). Do not treat this as the 30s vsock miss.
acceptance_criteria:
- A service VM spawned from a release snapshot of `ubuntu-24.04` (Builder quiesce-snapshot after build steps) does not spend ~90s in `Job dev-ttyS0.device/start`.
- Either the image masks `serial-getty@ttyS0` for microVM boots, or CH always presents ttyS0 before systemd waits, or await/secrets timeouts are not racing this hang.
- identikey had to `ln -sfn /dev/null …/serial-getty@ttyS0.service` on the release snapshot by hand; that must not be a per-app step.

title: spawn_failed / :boot_timeout does not name a vsock agent miss
description:
`VM.spawn` waits `@default_await_boot_timeout` (30s) for the guest agent vsock ping. On timeout the identikey deploy saw: HTTP 500, client `unexpected EOF` / `spawn request failed`, server `GenServer.call ... :await_boot, 30000` EXIT.

`scripts/lib/guest-agent.sh` already documents this exact operator experience: image boots, nobody answers vsock, API returns a bare spawn_failed with no message naming the cause.

The 30s is a ping deadline. When it fires, say so. Distinguished from LUKS/managed 90s timeout and from a later `secrets_unlock_failed`.
acceptance_criteria:
- When `:await_boot` times out because the guest never answered vsock, the API error (and orchestrator NDJSON `error`) names that: guest agent never pinged, not a bare `:boot_timeout` / HTTP 500 `spawn_failed`.
- Builder/Orchestrator progress line for a deploy build-VM miss includes the base image name.
- Serial/journal already have TAP+virtiofsd; the caller-visible error must be enough to look at the image agent, not at cargo.

title: mj doctor does not check guest-agent binary on base images or guest_agent_bin path
description:
`Mjolnir.Health.Host.check/0` covers kvm, vsock, NAT, btrfs, socket/state dirs. It does not look at base images or `:guest_agent_bin`.

Identikey 2026-08-27: `mj doctor` reported Host ok (kvm, vsock, NAT, btrfs) while `@base/deploy-node-bun` had the agent *unit* and no binary, and the configured inject path did not exist. Every `mj deploy` then 500'd at spawn. The operator-facing health check said the host was fine.

This is the diagnostic half of bhcr/hjnz. Do not auto-heal by rewriting a base image; refuse-to-fix and name the rebuild (`just build-deploy-base` / `install_guest_agent`) and the missing inject path.
acceptance_criteria:
- `mj doctor` (host, no VM id) fails or warns if the default deploy base (`deploy-node-bun`) has `mjolnir-agent.service` wanted and no `/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent`.
- Same for `ubuntu-24.04` if the binary is missing.
- Warns if `:guest_agent_bin` is set to a path that does not exist, or is nil in prod.
- The finding names the image and the missing path; it does not only say `:boot_timeout`.

title: nod-biscuit-runtime: host mint/verify Biscuits
description:
# mjolnir-axsb.1.3: host mints/verifies Biscuits and real Blake3

**Goal.** Elixir can mint an Ed25519-rooted Biscuit, verify it (and reject a tampered/widened one), and compute auth-challenge §5 fingerprints plus salted secret commitments with **real** Blake3. No HTTP.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `KeyPair::new()` mint → `Biscuit::from(bytes, root.public())` succeeds; `to_vec` round-trips.
- [ ] Append `check if holder($fp), $fp == "<fp>"` via `append(block!(...))`; authorizer with matching `holder("<fp>")` + `allow if right(...)` succeeds; missing holder fact fails.
- [ ] Tampered authority bytes fail `Biscuit::from`.
- [ ] `blake3_hash(<<>>)` equals official empty vector `AF1349B9F5F9A1A6A0404DEA36DCC9499BCB25C9ADC112B7CC9A93CAE41F3262` (today skipped in `test/mjolnir/sites/crypto_test.exs:13-24`).
- [ ] Holder fp of an Ed25519 pubkey equals `identikey_auth::ClassicalPublicKey::fingerprint()` on the same 32 bytes — not `IdentiKey.fingerprint/1`.
- [ ] Commitment `Blake3("mjolnir/secret-commit/v1" || salt || secret)` is 32 bytes; unsalted `Blake3(secret)` is not used.
- [ ] No `/api/secrets/*` routes. Existing SecretStore directory names unchanged.

## Contract
biscuit-auth **6.0.0** (docs.rs, 2026-06-06). Verified usage:

```rust
use biscuit_auth::{KeyPair, Biscuit, macros::*};
let root = KeyPair::new();
let tok = biscuit!(r#"right("github-pat-ci", "redeem");"#).build(&root)?;
let bytes = tok.to_vec()?;
let t = Biscuit::from(&bytes, root.public())?;
let t2 = t.append(block!(r#"check if holder($fp), $fp == "FP";"#))?;
authorizer!(r#"holder("FP"); allow if right("github-pat-ci", "redeem");"#)
  .build(&t2)?.authorize()?;
```

Blake3 already in-tree (`native/mjolnir_blob_door/src/lib.rs:32-34`):

```rust
pub fn blake3_bytes(data: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] { *blake3::hash(data).as_bytes() }
```

Holder fingerprint — `identikey-protocol` `crates/identikey-auth/src/key.rs:50-53`:

```rust
pub fn fingerprint(&self) -> Fingerprint {
    Fingerprint(*blake3::hash(&self.to_value().to_bytes()).as_bytes())
}
// to_value = dCBOR map {"alg": tstr, "key": bstr}  (key.rs:38-44)
```

Do **not** add hex `:blake3` (rustler 0.30/0.37 broken — `mix.exs:78-82`). New workspace crate under `native/` using `blake3 = "1"` + `biscuit-auth = "6"`. Rustler-from-that-crate or an Erlang Port is the BEAM face (tokenator stays in-process from the guest).

## Inherited
- `Sites.Crypto.blake3_hash/1` is SHA-256 — Recrypt 400s if you pretend otherwise (`docs/LEARNINGS.md` 2026-08-19; `crypto.ex:24-29`).
- Envelope `put/3` JSON-only — Gordian deferred (`secret_store.ex:599-602`).
- Guest-agent `cargo check` fails on macOS (tokio-vsock). This crate must not depend on vsock.
- `just deploy` restarts Elixir / kills VMs (tokenator-in-beam). Fine for this node; don’t add a just verb.
- Do not fold unimplemented HTTP SHALLs into living specs (2026-08-16).

## Out of scope
- `POST /api/secrets/redeem` + Auth fourth branch — `mjolnir-axsb.1.4`
- Deposit/mint CLI — `mjolnir-axsb.1.5`
- Third-party Identikey hop blocks — `mjolnir-axsb.1.6`
- Gordian envelopes — deferred
- Migrating existing Sites keyspace names off the SHA-256 stub
- JWT replacement / rbac Phase 1 VM-exec biscuits
- Protocol file fold (`update-identikey-capability` act) — separate, docs-only
acceptance_criteria: mint/verify biscuit round-trip; holder check fail-closed; tamper fails; real Blake3 empty vector; fp matches identikey-auth not IdentiKey.fingerprint/1; salted commitment; no HTTP; no Sites keyspace rename

title: E: Papyrus sends to mailbox (retry-safe, laptop may close)

title: D: Memory snapshots
description:
Memory snapshots. Checkpoint RAM + process tree, not just BTRFS. Today restore is filesystem-only (docs/actor-persistence.md); processes restart.

Acceptance (when intended): `mj snapshot create` captures memory; restore resumes execution, not just disk.

Touches Cloud Hypervisor snapshot/restore, virtio-fs coherence, mailbox delivery across a restored body.

Soft successor of C (density rehearsal may prove disk-only is enough, or not). Not a hard blocker.

Do not act. Run `intend --extract-from` this id when activating.

description:
CI boot-fat / restore-thin from a prepared filesystem snapshot. Prepare the FS like a Docker layer, snapshot, maybe compact, boot the build at large memory, snapshot the result, restore agents at small memory.

Acceptance (when intended): A Forgejo/Mjolnir CI job boots a prepared snapshot at high memory, produces a snapshot, a subsequent agent VM restores that snapshot at small memory with the toolchain already there.

Papyrus does not own this. Memory snapshots (D) are a later fidelity if disk-only restore is the bottleneck.

title: Deterministic agency — unexpanded intentions
description:
Unexpanded intentions from the 2026-08-26 hammer / deterministic-agency talk. Not an intend DAG. Not parked.

Plugin: `intend` always splits. There is no capture-only verb. These epics sit until a human throws one at `intend --extract-from <id>`.

Dossier (gathering): ~/work/IdentiKey/Papyrus/docs/notes/2026-08-26-ultimate-hammer.md
Philosophy: docs/philosophy/deterministic-agency.md
Protocol: identikey-protocol docs/standards/identikey-capability-v1.md (Biscuit; landed 2026-08-26)

If a neural network is a universal function approximator, Mjolnir is the deterministic portion of the AI agent's agency.

| | Intention | Lands | Why separate |
|---|---|---|---|
| B | Delegate permissions as signed Biscuit tokens; first UI in Papyrus | Papyrus UI + Mjolnir mint/accept + protocol (format landed) | Unblocks agents that are not the owner with all scopes |
| A | Small named roster in Papyrus (personality + skills + connections), each in a Mjolnir VM | Papyrus Terminal / shell | The product to use; depends on B if those agents should not all be root |
| C | CI boot-fat / restore-thin from a prepared snapshot | Mjolnir / Forgejo runner | Density rehearsal |
| D | Memory snapshots | Mjolnir architecture | After C proves filesystem-only restore is the bottleneck |
| E | Papyrus sends to the existing mailbox (close laptop, turn still lands) | Papyrus client of ADR 0006 | Do not re-intend the spool |

Pick order: B → A, then C, then D if C proves the need, E as a send-to-mailbox client.

title: Cross-host replication: per-tenant btrfs send + placement registry
description:
The multi-node payoff: bring a user's VM up on any host in the fleet.

## Pieces

- Transport: btrfs send -p per TENANT subtree (not per host). Mechanics,
  parent-lineage tracking and restore-drill acceptance live in mjolnir-qwp.
  Snapshots are already created read-only where it matters, which send requires.
- Placement registry: {tenant, snapshot} -> [nodes], plus which node currently
  RUNS a given VM. Nothing in the tree models this today; Reconcile and
  StateStore are single-host.
- Identity remapping on restore: new CID, TAP, IP, possibly a new Iroh node key.
  SAME problem as mjolnir-8m3 (fork N VMs from one memory snapshot) — solve once,
  use twice.
- Clustering: libcluster + :pg — tracked as mjolnir-6fn.

## Depends on

Per-tenant subvolume trees (sibling child) — the tenant subtree is the unit of
replication, so that refactor comes first.

## Interaction with memory snapshots

.mem directories must not be replicated until the luksSuspend child lands, or
replication exports the DEK across hosts.

title: Biscuit capability tokens (rbac-design Phase 1) — dual-mode with JWT
description:
Owner-equality cannot express sharing. policy/vm.ex authorizes via strict
owner_id equality with NO delegation mechanism — sharing a VM today means
sharing OIDC credentials, operator intervention, or a zero-auth Iroh ticket.

Full design already written: docs/plans/rbac-design.md. Phase 1 is explicitly
non-breaking — Biscuit alongside existing JWT, nothing removed.

## Phase 1 scope (from the design)

- biscuit-auth Rustler NIF on the Elixir host
- Ed25519 keypair at server startup
- Mint root Biscuit at VM spawn, return as a new response field
- Mjolnir.API.Auth accepts `Authorization: Bearer biscuit:<b64>`
- Policy layer gains authorize(action, %{capability: biscuit}, resource)
  evaluating Datalog instead of owner_id
- mj client stores the Biscuit alongside VM metadata

## Under multi-tenancy

Snapshot sharing becomes 'hand someone an attenuated token' rather than 'ask the
operator'. But note the two-step problem: a Biscuit grants ACCESS, while the
recipient still cannot DECRYPT tier 3 without a PRE re-encryption key. Decide
whether that is acceptable UX or needs a single verb.

Open (carried from rbac-design.md, sharper now): root capability bound to the
server key or the owner key? Server-key binding means the OPERATOR can mint any
tenant's capability — which is a different security posture once tenants are
mutually distrusting.

title: Wrap the LUKS DEK to the owner's IdentiKey via recrypt PRE
description:
Makes secrets_mode :persistent genuinely user-sovereign, and makes fleet-wide
placement compatible with host-opaque encryption.

## Today

:persistent takes a PASSPHRASE from a remote Iroh peer. Host never holds it —
good — but it requires the user's peer reachable at boot, which is fatal for
'bring my VM up on any host, now'.

## Target

DEK encrypted under the user's IdentiKey public key. At spawn the host applies a
re-encryption key rk(A->B) to transform it into something the VM's EPHEMERAL key
can decrypt — without the host ever seeing the plaintext DEK or either private
key. (initramfs-verified-boot.md Layer 2; OpenFHE BFV in ~/work/IdentiKey/recrypt.)

This is the difference between 'user must be online to boot on node 3' and
'user pre-authorized node 3'.

## Notes

- Shares the recrypt Rust integration with mjolnir-9bq.5 (Sites keyspace/
  recipients). Sequence them together.
- Host sees BFV lattice ciphertexts (~5-10KB opaque). rk(A->B) permits only that
  one directional transform; it cannot decrypt.
- Depends on the identity-binding child (need identikey_fp per tenant).
- Once this lands, encrypting @snapshots/<name>.mem to the owner's key becomes
  available as defence-in-depth for the memory-snapshot child.

title: Fork N VMs from one memory snapshot — proven cheap, needs identity remapping
description:
SUPERSEDES the pessimistic claim in mjolnir-3y6.4's close reason and commit 2dada84, which said forking needed 'a CID reallocation whose interaction with the vsock device state in state.json is unproven'. It is now proven to work.

MEASURED ON 45.76.77.97 (CH v53):
- Restored a VM from a REWRITTEN config.json — different virtiofsd socket path AND different vsock CID (78123401 -> 78123402) — while state.json still described the original devices. RESTORE=204, RESUME=204, marker process continued 1 -> 7 -> 10 -> 13 at the SAME pid 761, zero i8042/VM-reset events.
- Reflinking the 512MB memory image: 0.00s and ZERO additional bytes. btrfs 'Data used' read 25.38GiB before and after three reflinked copies. (du reports the apparent 2.0G because it cannot see cross-file extent sharing; btrfs filesystem df is authoritative.)
- The btrfs volume is mounted compress=zstd:3, so a 512MB RAM image occupies ~119MB even unshared.

WHY THE CID REWRITE IS SAFE FOR US: the guest agent binds VMADDR_CID_ANY (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/vsock.rs:184,466) so it never depends on its own CID, and the host reaches it over the per-VM unix socket rather than by CID. The CID is effectively just a host-unique number.

SO A FORK IS THREE FREE CoW OPERATIONS PLUS A JSON REWRITE:
1. rootfs: btrfs subvolume snapshot from the pinned RO snapshot (already implemented in MemorySnapshot.prepare_thaw/2)
2. RAM: cp --reflink=always memory-ranges into a per-fork dir
3. identity: rewrite fs[].socket, vsock.socket, vsock.cid in that dir's config.json

STILL UNRESOLVED, and the actual work:
- NETWORK. The probe had no net device. MAC is GUEST-VISIBLE and lives in the restored guest's RAM, so rewriting it breaks the guest's stack. Two options: (a) CH's restore already accepts net_fds=<net_id:fd> for exactly this remapping (confirmed in the v53 binary's --restore help, with RestoreMissingRequiredNetId / RestoreNetFdCountMismatch error variants) — hand each fork a fresh TAP fd while keeping the MAC; or (b) put each fork in its own network namespace so identical TAP name/MAC/IP do not collide and the guest's in-RAM beliefs stay TRUE. (b) is more elegant and needs veth+NAT per netns.
- GUEST IDENTITY. hostname, machine-id, SSH host keys and the iroh key are identical across forks — both on the cloned rootfs and in RAM. Needs a post-thaw re-identity step in the guest agent.
- ENTROPY. mjolnir-3y6.5. Forking is the case that makes CRNG cloning severe rather than mild: N forks share a random stream.

MOUNT-NAMESPACE ALTERNATIVE worth noting: bind-mounting a per-fork socket over the path config.json names would avoid rewriting config.json for virtiofs at all. Probably not worth it given the rewrite is proven to work, but it is the same trick as (b) for the network.
acceptance_criteria: N VMs restored concurrently from one memory snapshot, each with its own rootfs clone, its own reflinked RAM image, its own virtiofsd socket and vsock CID, AND its own working network via net_fds. Each fork reports a distinct machine-id/hostname/iroh node id, and a key-generation probe returns a different value from every fork (mjolnir-3y6.5). No fork's traffic reaches another's TAP.
notes:
DECISION 2026-08-14 (Duke): go with net_fds, NOT a network namespace per fork.

Rationale: net_fds keeps the one-VM-one-TAP model the rest of Mjolnir already assumes (Mjolnir.Network allocates TAP/MAC/IP hash-deterministically per vm_id; Gateway.Routes and the reconciler all read that model). A netns-per-fork would fork the networking architecture for EVERY VM in order to serve a feature only forks need, and would add veth+NAT plumbing to a path that currently has none.

Accepted cost of net_fds: each fork keeps the frozen guest's MAC, because the MAC is guest-visible and lives in restored RAM. So forks are distinguishable by IP/TAP but not by MAC. That is fine on separate TAPs (no shared L2 segment, and the host routes /32 per guest IP) but it does mean MAC can never be used as a fork identity, and two forks must never share a bridge. Worth a comment where the TAP is created.

Deferred, not rejected: the netns approach remains the better answer IF we ever want forks to be byte-identical down to the IP — the 'fork a live VM at a decision point and have both believe they are the same machine' case. Revisit then; nothing in the net_fds path forecloses it.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: net_fds needs the TAP fd passed to CH over the API socket (SCM_RIGHTS), not a path in JSON. Mjolnir.CloudHypervisor.Client currently shells out to curl, which cannot pass an fd. That is the one real piece of new plumbing this needs — either a small Unix-socket client that can sendmsg with SCM_RIGHTS, or launching CH with the tap already opened. Scope this before estimating.
IMPORTANT for the fork framing (from ef4a525): 'fork a live VM at a decision point' does NOT leave the original running. vm.snapshot is terminal for any virtio-fs VM, so freezing to get the memory image parks the source.

Forking N ways therefore costs N+1 thaws: one to replace the original, N for the forks. That does not change the mechanism or the cost (each thaw is a free CoW clone + reflink + config rewrite) but it does change the story — a fork is 'park and re-launch N ways', not 'the original continues and you get N copies'. Worth saying plainly wherever this is described.
