title: Gateway routes render before VMs finish resuming — every deploy drops a customer route for a few seconds
description:
On the deploy of 2026-08-13 02:59:59 UTC, 7 seconds after restart:

  03:00:06 [warning] Gateway.Routes: skipping startupcentral.build — VM 67490a98 is not running/local; no route emitted
  03:00:06 [warning] Gateway.Routes: this render REMOVES 1 existing route(s): startupcentral.build — customer traffic to those hosts will 400 until they come back

The state recovered on its own — the route count is back to 2 and https://startupcentral.build/ returns 200 — but for the seconds between that render and the next one, the gateway was serving one fewer route and real traffic to that host would have 400'd.

CAUSE: a restart tears down and resumes every VM (Cleanup kills, Reconcile resumes). The route render runs while resume is still in flight, sees a VM that is not yet :running, and treats 'not running right now' as 'should not have a route'. Absence-during-boot is being read as intent.

WHY IT IS SMALL BUT NOT NOTHING: it happens on EVERY deploy, and it is invisible unless you read the log — the end state looks perfect. It is also strictly worse for a slow-resuming VM: a VM that takes a minute to come back is a minute of 400s.

FIX DIRECTIONS:
1. Never REMOVE a route for a VM that is merely booting/resuming. A route should be dropped when the VM is gone (no StateStore record, or intent :failed/:stopped), not when it is between states. The warning already distinguishes 'not running/local' — that predicate is the bug, not the reporting.
2. Or defer the first render until Reconcile reports its resume pass complete, so the boot-time render never runs against a half-resumed world.

Direction 1 is preferable: it is correct even outside the deploy window.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: the second warning line — naming the removal and its consequence — is why this was caught at all. It came from the mjolnir-1pk work. Without it the deploy log would have looked clean.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy produces no route REMOVES warning, and the route file never loses a route for a VM that is merely resuming.
close_reason: Fixed in 9d16183. The predicate was the bug: 'not running right now' was being read as 'should not have a route'. The reachable set now includes :booting VMs plus StateStore records of intent :running — a VM mid-resume usually has NO GenServer at all (Reconcile has not reached it), which is the case the incident actually hit. Routes drop only when the VM is gone (no record, or intent :failed/:stopped/:dormant). Took direction 1 over deferring the first render because it is correct outside the deploy window too. Tests drive render_and_reload/1 without passing :running_vm_ids so they exercise the real default resolution; verified they fail for the right reason — reverting the predicate fails exactly the 2 resuming-VM tests while the 3 'genuinely gone' tests still pass, so the widening did not just make removal impossible.

title: A booting VM reports 'unreachable' — Health.Monitor probes it while handle_continue(:boot) holds the mailbox
description:
MEASURED ON THE DEPLOY OF mjolnir-75d, 2026-08-12 21:19 UTC. That fix moved every vsock round-trip out of handle_call, and the false 'unreachable' STILL happened — because this symptom never came from a handle_call. It comes from the boot sequence itself.

Timeline, VM 2da0e442 (the host's only secrets_mode: managed VM), single boot:
  21:19:35  mjolnir restarts
  21:19:53  [warning] Health.Monitor: VM 2da0e442 GenServer unreachable (call timed out); skipping probe this tick
  21:20:23  [error]   Managed secrets unlock failed: :timeout
  21:20:23  [info]    Reconcile: VM 2da0e442 resumed

do_boot runs inside handle_continue(:boot), and maybe_unlock_secrets/2 does a vsock_request with a 60_000ms bound (justified: LUKS create — dd + argon2id format + mkfs — genuinely can exceed 10s). While that runs the mailbox cannot answer anything, so Health.Monitor's GenServer.call times out and the VM is rendered state=unreachable with null ip/iroh in GET /api/vms. Observed on three consecutive deploys; the VM was healthy every time and settled once boot finished.

The alarming part is WHEN it happens: during a deploy, which is exactly when an operator is watching to see whether their VMs survived. Same family as mjolnir-nf6 — a probe that cannot reach something reports failure instead of reporting that it learned nothing.

TWO DIRECTIONS, both worth considering:
1. Don't call a booting VM unreachable. The monitor cannot ask the GenServer for its state (that is the blocked call), but the StateStore record is readable without touching the process — a VM whose record is present and whose GenServer is merely busy should surface as :booting/:busy, never as a state that reads like failure.
2. Question the 60s inline unlock. mjolnir-3v2 now records the outcome durably, so the unlock no longer has to be inline-and-synchronous to be observable; boot could proceed and the unlock report asynchronously. That also removes a full minute from this VM's every restart.

NOT a regression in mjolnir-75d — that fix is correct and its own acceptance (no handle_call holds the mailbox on a vsock round-trip) is met and tested. This is the remaining, differently-caused instance.
design:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-08-12 (Duke: 'making it async, that seems right').

CONFIRMED: nothing is lost by deferring. init/1 returns {:ok, state, {:continue, :boot}}, so start_child returns the pid BEFORE handle_continue(:boot) runs — POST /api/vms has already answered while the VM boots. The 60s unlock was never inside an HTTP/TCP window, only inside the process window. That is why the symptom is state=unreachable and not a slow API call. Messages arriving during boot are already buffered via state.message_queue and drained after do_boot.

HAZARD, do not skip: maybe_unlock_secrets runs INSIDE do_boot before state: :running is set, so today ':running' implies 'secrets mounted'. deploy/orchestrator.ex:352 spawns the service VM with secrets_mode: :managed and the app sources /run/mjolnir/secrets.env (guest_agent/src/secrets.rs:26). A fire-and-forget unlock lets a deploy race into starting an app with an empty env — trading a false alarm for a real silent failure, the exact family mjolnir-3v2/nf6 exist to close.

WHAT WILL NOT WORK: a second {:continue, :unlock} or a selective receive. Both leave messages in the mailbox unanswered, so Health.Monitor still times out. The work must leave the process.

SHAPE:
1. do_boot runs to vsock-ready, persists state :booting, returns {:noreply, state} — mailbox live
2. spawn_monitor performs the 60s vsock round-trip, sends {:unlock_result, ...} home
3. handle_info({:unlock_result, ...}) stamps secrets_unlock_failure and THEN transitions to :running

This preserves ':running implies secrets mounted' and resolves direction 1 for free — the VM reports :booting because the process genuinely answers. Reuses the spawn_monitor + reply-later pattern mjolnir-75d established for handle_call; this is the one blocking path 75d did not cover, which is exactly why 75d did not move this symptom.

AUDIT BEFORE MERGE: handle_boot_failure, the message_queue drain, and persist_running_state all assume boot is finished when handle_continue(:boot) returns. Also needs a :DOWN clause so a crashed unlock process does not strand the VM in :booting forever (same wedge class as the vsock_rebuild_ref guard added in 75d).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12, commit c5fb4c0. Boot is now two-phase; start_secrets_unlock/1 hands the unlock to a monitored worker and finish_boot/2 is the single place a VM becomes :running.

FOUND DURING THE AUDIT, and it would have broken every managed spawn: handle_call(:await_boot, from, %{state: :booting}) stored the caller in a boot_waiter key and NOTHING ever replied to it. That was harmless only because the inline boot never opened the mailbox, so await_boot always landed on the :running clause after handle_continue returned — the :booting clause was unreachable. Deferring the unlock makes it live. boot_waiter is now a real defstruct field and finish_boot/2 replies to it. Without that, spawn/1 would have hung to its 90s managed timeout every time.

ALSO SHIPPED: Health gained a :booting verdict beside :busy (corroborated_overall + heal + Monitor dispatch), because the L1 heal stops the very Vsock.Connection the unlock is using — the mjolnir-1s9 shape with a different cause. mj doctor now paints busy/booting as states instead of rendering both as a bare '?'.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the unlock is still not retried. A failed unlock records secrets_unlock_failure (mjolnir-3v2) and the VM boots without /run/mjolnir. Auto-retry belongs in its own issue — Health.Monitor must not retry it on a 30s tick, which is why 3v2 kept the flag out of checks/overall.

17 new tests: test/mjolnir/vm_secrets_unlock_test.exs (8, covering all three terminations plus the await_boot reply and double-transition guards) and test/mjolnir/health/booting_vm_test.exs (9).
close_reason: Deployed and verified in production 2026-08-13 02:06 UTC. Zero 'GenServer unreachable' this boot (one on the previous deploy, same VM, same point). Positively confirmed with a fresh managed spawn: the VM answered GET /api/vms with state=booting at t+2s, where the same call used to time out. All 4 VMs returned with identical iroh node ids, 2 routes, both sites 200, exactly 1 warning/error in the whole boot log (the pre-existing unlock timeout, now filed as mjolnir-azm).

title: A failed managed-secrets unlock leaves no trace in the VM's state
description:
Observed on the full deploy 2026-08-12 18:55. VM 2da0e442 (secrets_mode: managed) logged:

  [error] Managed secrets unlock failed: :timeout
  [info]  Reconcile: VM 2da0e442-730c-4926-a6c7-4ff316a98e96 resumed

and came up reporting state=running like any healthy VM. Inside the guest, /run/mjolnir does not exist and lsblk shows no crypt device — the unlock genuinely did not happen, and anything on that VM depending on its secrets will fail later for reasons that look nothing like the cause.

The log-and-continue at lib/mjolnir/vm.ex:1675-1680 is DELIBERATE and defensible; its comment says a transient cryptsetup hiccup should not wedge a whole boot. That is not what this issue asks to change. The defect is that after continuing, the failure becomes INVISIBLE: nothing in the StateStore record, GET /api/vms, mj info, or mj doctor says this VM is running without its secrets. The only witness is one log line that scrolls away.

Third instance of the same class today, after mjolnir-1pk (a route dropped in silence) and mjolnir-nf6 (a probe reporting the wrong component). A degraded VM that presents as healthy is worse than one that presents as failed.

FIX: record the outcome where it is observable — a flag in the record's runtime map (free-form, no schema bump; precedent resume_failures), surfaced in the API response and in mj doctor, so a VM running without its secrets is visibly degraded and can be healed or re-unlocked deliberately.

NOTE this VM may have no secrets provisioned at all (no host-side secret material found for it, spawn_config has owner_id null and metadata {}), so the timeout may be 'waiting for something that was never there' rather than a cryptsetup failure. Worth determining which — if a managed VM can be spawned with no secrets to unlock, that is its own bug.
notes: Correction: the separate finding referenced in the close reason was filed as mjolnir-tct (a managed-secrets VM spawnable with no owner and no provisioned secrets), not mjolnir-tkd — that id was a typo and does not exist.
close_reason:
Fixed in ea1631c. The failed unlock's outcome is carried on the VM struct and stamped into the record's runtime map (keys secrets_unlock_failed/_error/_failed_at, present only on failure), surfaced by GET /api/vms/:id, GET /api/vms/:id/health, POST /heal, and 'mj doctor <id>'. The log-and-continue at the unlock site is unchanged — that was deliberate and correct; the defect was the silence after it.

Stamped INSIDE build_running_record, not written from a side path: that function rebuilds runtime from scratch on every boot and resume, which is the same trap that would have made the CI lease vanish on restart (see memory build-running-record-wipes-runtime). A test rebuilds the record twice — once with the failure set, once without — to pin that the value comes from the struct at boot rather than a prior persisted record.

DELIBERATELY NOT :degraded. Nothing re-attempts the LUKS unlock, so folding it into checks/overall would hand Health.Monitor's 30s tick a condition it retries forever and can never fix — mjolnir-1s9 in miniature. Informational only; the roll-up (roll_up/1, corroborated_overall/3-4) is untouched, and the report reuses a VM struct already in scope so it adds no GenServer.call (no regression against mjolnir-75d).

CORRECTS THIS ISSUE'S HYPOTHESIS: I suspected the VM had no secrets provisioned and the unlock was waiting for something that never existed. Not so — SecretEscrow.get_or_create/1 synthesizes a fresh passphrase when no escrow file exists and proceeds, so escrow state cannot cause this. The literal :timeout is a gen_tcp read timeout on the 60s vsock round-trip, i.e. the guest-side cryptsetup/vsock channel hung or was not ready. Separate finding filed as mjolnir-tkd.

1195 -> 1205 tests, 0 failures; 40 client tests pass. NOT YET DEPLOYED.

title: Boot race: a guest syslog line lands on the vsock JSON control channel and fails the spawn
description:
Observed live on root@45.76.77.97, CI run 14 (2026-08-12 16:57), which failed with 'vm spawn 500: {"error":"spawn_failed"}'. Server side:

  VM e9937d1d-471e-4730-b17b-1939bb90cee0 failed to boot: %Jason.DecodeError{position: 0, token: nil,
    data: "<30>Aug 12 16:57:15 dbus-daemon[776]: [system] Successfully activated service 'org.freedesktop.systemd1'\n"}

An RFC 3164 syslog line was fed to the JSON decoder that reads the guest agent's control-channel replies. Channel 0 is JSON control and channel 2 is syslog (Mjolnir.Vsock.Protocol multiplexes on a 1-byte channel id), so either a channel-2 frame is being routed to the channel-0 reader, or unframed early-boot output reaches the control reader before framing is established. The payload — dbus activating systemd1 — is exactly the noisy window right after the guest's /dev/log appears.

INTERMITTENT, and it costs a whole CI job when it hits: the boot fails, the VM is torn down, and the run reports spawn_failed with no hint that the cause was log noise. Run 13 succeeded and two hand-issued spawns of the SAME base image immediately afterwards both succeeded, so it is a race, not a regression. NOT caused by the metadata change landing at the same time — verified by spawning ci-ubuntu-24.04 with and without metadata, both fine.

INVESTIGATE: whether Syslog.Listener can deliver to the control reader before the agent's first ping; whether the decoder should skip/---log--- a non-JSON frame instead of failing the boot outright. Failing a whole spawn because a log line arrived is disproportionate — an unparseable control frame should at worst be dropped with a warning.
close_reason:
Fixed in ae4f512 (reader) + ab2c141 (the two vm.ex call sites). ROOT CAUSE: every accepted vsock connection makes the guest agent rebind /dev/log and start draining it onto channel 2 (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/vsock.rs run_vsock_listener -> syslog.rs). On a fresh guest that backlog can reach the wire before the channel-0 reply. vm.ex's vsock_request/3 and try_ping_agent/1 read the next frame and decoded it while DISCARDING the channel byte, so syslog text went to Jason.decode and killed the spawn. Explains the intermittency (pure race) and why it was confined to boot: the persistent Vsock.Connection used afterwards demultiplexes channels correctly and was never at risk. No host-side mis-dispatch and no guest-side wrong-channel write — the guest tags syslog correctly.

FIX: Protocol.read_json_response/2 reads within one deadline, skips non-channel-0 frames and undecodable channel-0 frames with a bounded warning, and keeps reading. Failing an entire VM spawn — in CI a whole job — because a log line arrived is disproportionate regardless of cause. Health.GuestAgentPing had the identical bug independently and now shares the reader. Also fixed a socket leak in try_ping_agent: the old with-chain closed the socket only on the success path.

Regression test replays the exact dbus line from the incident on channel 2 ahead of a pong on channel 0. 1195 tests, 0 failures. NOT YET DEPLOYED.

title: Cleanup.clean_orphan_taps is host-global — a test BEAM can delete production VMs' TAPs
description:
Blocks the 'scope check' half of mjolnir-gge.1.8 (run :integration tests as ExUnit on the server).

Mjolnir.Cleanup.sweep is scoped by config almost everywhere: find_orphan_hypervisors filters ps output by socket_dir (test /tmp/mjolnir-test vs prod /tmp/mjolnir), clean_stale_sockets reads socket_dir, and clean_stale_vms lists Path.join(btrfs_root, "@vms") (test /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs-test vs prod .../btrfs). A second BEAM in MIX_ENV=test therefore leaves prod hypervisors, sockets and rootfs subvolumes alone.

clean_orphan_taps/0 (lib/mjolnir/cleanup.ex:112) takes NO config. It shells 'ip -o link show', matches ANY interface named mj-* in 'state DOWN', and 'ip link del's it. TAP devices are host-global, so a test BEAM's startup sweep would delete a PRODUCTION VM's TAP if that TAP were DOWN at that instant — cutting the VM's networking (recoverable via heal/reconfigure, but a live disruption).

Right now all 4 prod TAPs are UP, so the window is closed by luck, not design. It opens whenever a VM is mid-boot (TAP created, not yet UP) or wedged — i.e. exactly when someone is likely to be running tests to debug it.

FIX (needs a small naming decision): scope TAP ownership by config, e.g. a :tap_prefix defaulting to 'mj-' with test using 'mjt-', threaded through both Mjolnir.Network's TAP creation and clean_orphan_taps, so each BEAM only ever reaps interfaces it could have created.

RELATED, opposite direction (lower severity, same root): prod's socket_dir filter is a SUBSTRING match, and '/tmp/mjolnir-test/x.sock' contains '/tmp/mjolnir' — so a PROD restart would kill TEST VMs' hypervisors. Anchoring the match would fix both.
acceptance_criteria: A MIX_ENV=test BEAM's startup sweep provably cannot delete a TAP belonging to a VM it did not create, verified with a prod-named TAP in state DOWN present during a test sweep.
close_reason: Fixed in 406b53c. TAP names now take :tap_prefix (default 'mj-', test 'mjt-') via Network.tap_prefix/0, and Cleanup.clean_orphan_taps only reaps interfaces matching its own prefix — so a MIX_ENV=test BEAM can no longer delete a production VM's TAP. Production sets no prefix, so its names and behaviour are unchanged. A guard test asserts non-containment in BOTH directions and fails specifically on 'mj-test-', the plausible-but-wrong name that still contains 'mj-'. 1144 tests green. Unblocks mjolnir-gge.1.8's scope check.

title: mj spawn prints the ticket, not the VM id you need next
description:
Non-JSON 'mj spawn' output ends with the connection ticket and never prints the VM UUID. But every follow-up verb — mj exec/kill/info/snapshot — takes the UUID, so the natural next step requires a second round trip through 'mj list', and picking a VM out of that list by position is exactly how you kill the wrong one (I did, 2026-08-12; recovered via POST /api/trash/:id/restore).

FIX: print the VM id prominently in the human-readable spawn output alongside the ticket, e.g. 'VM <uuid>' before the ticket line. Cheap, and it removes the list-and-guess step entirely.

Consider also: 'mj kill' could refuse a bare prefix that matches more than one VM, and echo the target's base_image/created_at before destroying it.
close_reason: Fixed in a124ae0. mj spawn now prints the VM id up front; mj kill echoes id + base image/snapshot + boot time before the DELETE (no prompt — that would break scripting and kill --all). Both on stderr so stdout still carries only the ticket. Prefix matching does not exist in the CLI (resolve_vm_id requires a full UUID or exact ticket), so task 3 was moot. Also corrected a 'unix timestamp' label to 'unix ms' — boot_time is System.system_time(:millisecond). 40 client tests pass.

title: Delete the stale native/forgejo-runner mirror — it is never built
description:
mjolnir-400 replaced the patch-on-clone approach with a real fork (identikey/forgejo-runner, branch mjolnir) and its close reason claims duplicate files were deleted, but native/forgejo-runner/ survived. It is dead weight and actively harmful:

- The live executor is act/container/mjolnir/vm.go in the fork (498 lines). The in-repo copy is pkg/mjolnir/executor.go (340 lines) in a different package path. They have diverged; deploy.sh --runner clones and builds the FORK and never reads this directory.
- I diagnosed an executor bug against the in-repo copy today (mjolnir-7c4) and got the mechanism wrong because of it. That is the concrete cost.
- 'just build-runner' runs 'cd native/forgejo-runner && go build ./...', compiling dead code and proving nothing about what ships.
- README.md documents the superseded manual-patch workflow, including a patches/ file that deploy.sh no longer applies.

Delete the directory (7 files, 48K), drop the build-runner recipe, and fix the stale path references in CLAUDE.md and docs/roadmap.md. The architecture notes worth keeping (label mapping, VM lifecycle per job) are already in CLAUDE.md.
acceptance_criteria: native/forgejo-runner/ is gone; no recipe or doc points at it; nothing in the repo or deploy path references it; mix test still passes.
close_reason: native/forgejo-runner/ deleted in 0696e4d (934 lines, 7 files). Justfile build-runner recipe removed; CLAUDE.md and docs/roadmap.md now point at identikey/forgejo-runner. Verified no dangling references remain and 'just --list' parses.

title: Forgejo VM executor silently ignores working-directory on run steps
description:
ROOT CAUSE (corrected 2026-08-12): the live executor is act/container/mjolnir/vm.go in the SEPARATE repo identikey/forgejo-runner (branch 'mjolnir', built at /opt/forgejo-runner-build). The copy in this repo at native/forgejo-runner/pkg/mjolnir/executor.go is a stale mirror and is NOT what runs — see mjolnir-400.

VMEnvironment.Exec builds a script containing:

    cd <workdir> || cd "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}" 2>/dev/null || true

act passes a RELATIVE workdir for 'working-directory: native'. The guest agent runs the script from /, so 'cd native' fails, and the '|| cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE' fallback then silently lands the step in the repo root. The trailing '|| true' means even a total failure to cd cannot fail the step.

FIX: resolve a relative workdir against GITHUB_WORKSPACE before cd-ing (cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && cd <workdir>), and drop the '|| true' so an impossible workdir fails loudly instead of running the command somewhere unintended. The fallback is only correct for an EMPTY workdir, which Exec already handles above.

CONFIRMED on identikey/mjolnir run 3 (commit 30c427f): a step with 'working-directory: native' printed pwd = /workspace/src/identikey/mjolnir. Diagnostic step retained in .forgejo/workflows/build-client.yml (continue-on-error) so a fix is confirmable from any green run's log.
acceptance_criteria: A step with 'working-directory: native' executes in <workspace>/native, and a relative working-directory that does not exist fails the step loudly rather than running in the parent.
notes: CONFIRMED on identikey/mjolnir run 3 (commit 30c427f), 2026-08-12. A step with 'working-directory: native' printed pwd = /workspace/src/identikey/mjolnir — the repo root, not native/. So act/the executor discards the relative workdir and falls through to the repo root; no error is raised, which is why run 1's cargo failure was the first symptom. Diagnostic step is retained in .forgejo/workflows/build-client.yml (continue-on-error) so a fix can be confirmed by reading any green run's log.
close_reason: Fixed in identikey/forgejo-runner 9a3efce7, live. Relative workdirs are joined to GITHUB_WORKSPACE before the cd. Verified on run 8: a step with 'working-directory: .forgejo' printed pwd = /workspace/src/identikey/mjolnir/.forgejo (previously the repo root). build-client.yml now uses working-directory throughout and the explicit 'cd native &&' workarounds are gone. NOTE: the '|| cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE || true' fallback was deliberately LEFT IN so workflows in other repos relying on its leniency do not start failing; making a bad workdir fail loudly is still desirable and unfiled.

title: mj has no --base flag; base images unreachable from the CLI
description: mj spawn only offers --snapshot, which resolves in @snapshots/. Base images live in @base/ and are only selectable via the raw API base_image field (what the Forgejo runner uses). So spawning a CI VM by hand requires ssh + curl through the localhost bypass. Add 'mj spawn --base <name>' and 'mj bases' to list @base/.
close_reason: 'mj spawn --base <name>' shipped in d28f8cf, mutually exclusive with --snapshot (enforced by clap and re-checked in cmd_spawn). Verified live: spawned from ci-ubuntu-24.04 and the guest reported cargo 1.97.1 + zig 0.16.0. The 'mj bases' listing half is split out as mjolnir-8vo — it needs a server endpoint that does not exist; no route enumerates @base/.

title: Forgejo CI: build mj client in a Mjolnir VM
description: Mjolnir builds its own client. Repo identikey/mjolnir mirrored to Forgejo (mimir.worldtree.network), workflow .forgejo/workflows/build-client.yml on the ci-ubuntu-24.04 base image (rust+zig via mise). Proves the reproducible CI image end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: A push to main runs the workflow to green: cargo test -p mjolnir-protocol -p mjolnir-client passes and target/release/mjolnir --version runs inside the VM.
close_reason: Green end to end: run 3 on commit 30c427f built mj in a ci-ubuntu-24.04 VM — 49 tests pass, release binary sha256 53e03ec3e25e716eab61a4e0b1826e71fc8c645f3a64b49923b2a3e8ebc140dd. Job VM was destroyed on completion (no leak). Follow-ups: mjolnir-4bk artifacts, mjolnir-7c4 working-directory, mjolnir-5xn cargo cache.

title: pty:connect-scoped service token (fold into the auth/Keycloak migration)
description:
DRIVER: xibu's browser terminals. The plan is to swap ttyd's child command from local tmux to 'mj connect <vmid> --session <name>', which needs pty:connect on xibu. Today the ONLY credential granting pty:connect is a full JWT from 'mj login' — so shipping terminals means putting an unscoped control-plane credential (spawn/destroy any VM) on a box with dev agents committing ~40x/day and several ports bound 0.0.0.0. Duke: 'we don't want control-plane unscoped access on the zany xibu world.'

WANT: a scoped service token conferring pty:connect (and probably terminal:* for the terminal_* family) and nothing else.

The pattern already exists and should be copied, not invented — Mjolnir.Sites.Token + TokenStore: opaque 'mjsk_<id>_<secret>' credential, bound to one IdentiKey fingerprint, conferring exactly Token.scope() ('sites:publish'), checked FIRST in Mjolnir.API.Auth so presenting a scoped credential can never be silently upgraded to full scope by connecting from loopback. That last property is the important one to preserve.

SEQUENCING (Duke, 2026-08-11): the login stack is about to migrate off the old Keycloak issuer, and scoped tokens should ride along with that rather than being built twice. Do NOT start this standalone — settle the new issuer's token model first, then land pty scoping inside it.

Related: mjolnir-98o (localhost bypass grants full admin by peer IP) is the same scope-granularity problem from the other direction; whatever token model lands should close both.

title: terminal_* family has zero test coverage; send_and_read sentinel logic is the risk
description:
The whole terminal_* surface — 6 HTTP endpoints, 6 MCP tools, 6 vsock request types, 8 response types — has no automated test anywhere. Only Elixir test file matching 'terminal' is sites/token_test.exs (false positive). All 7 tmux.rs tests cover attach_argv, which is the PTY helper, not this family.

tmux::send_and_read is the intricate part and should be tested first. It appends a sentinel 'echo __MJOLNIR_DONE_<uuid>_$?__', polls capture_pane every 250ms, and picks the sentinel with rfind, distinguishing the resolved line (digits) from the echoed command line (literal $?).

Concrete cases worth covering:
- Sentinel discrimination: a command whose own output contains the echoed-vs-resolved shapes must not end the wait early.
- Concurrency: two send_and_read calls on the SAME session must not interleave sentinels. There is a per-session mutex (tmux.rs:85 SESSION_LOCKS) but it is per agent PROCESS — it does not serialise against a human typing in the same pane over a PTY, which is the whole premise of shared sessions.
- Timeout: returns timed_out:true, exit_code:None, but leaves the command RUNNING. Its sentinel lands in the pane later. Verify a subsequent call keyed by a different uuid does not match the stale sentinel.
- Output truncation: capture_pane is called with 1000 scrollback lines; a command emitting more silently truncates. Assert the truncation is at least visible.
- Minimum latency: the 250ms sleep runs BEFORE the first capture, so even an instant command costs 250ms.

Tests likely need a real tmux, so tag :integration and run on the server.
close_reason: Coverage added in dd362fe: 4 passing tests over send_and_read (250ms poll floor; timeout leaving the command alive while a later call with a different id ignores the stale sentinel; concurrent in-process calls not interleaving; capture_pane's 1000-line truncation made visible), plus a 5th #[ignore]d test documenting a real bug found in the process (mjolnir-xrv). Verified independently on root@45.76.77.97 with tmux 3.4: 22 passed / 1 ignored, run twice with identical results and no leftover mjtest-* sessions. Production code untouched. The cross-process concurrency gap (SESSION_LOCKS is per agent process, so it cannot serialise against a human typing in the same shared pane) is deliberately documented rather than tested — closing it is a design change, not coverage.

title: WebSocket PTY path still injects the tmux command into stdin
description:
connect.rs run_pty_loop (both cfg variants, ~lines 400/470) types 'tmux new-session -A -s <name>' into the shell for the WebSocket/gateway path, even though the vsock PtyOpen request already carries a native 'session' field that the guest agent honours (vsock.rs:862).

Consequence: the WS path spawns a private outer shell and attaches tmux inside it. Detaching (Ctrl-B d) drops you back into that orphan outer shell instead of closing the connection, and the attach command lands in scrollback.

Fix: have the WS/gateway path pass the session name through to PtyOpen and drop the stdin injection, mirroring what mjolnir-690 just did for Iroh. The injection should remain ONLY as the v1-agent fallback in connect_to_vm.

Found while verifying mjolnir-690 end to end.
close_reason: Fixed in 58976b3. Client now sends ?session= on the PTY WebSocket URL (percent-encoded) and both cfg variants of run_pty_loop lost the stdin injection entirely. Verified on VM 771823a2: $TMUX set inside the WS session, Ctrl-B d exits 0 with no orphan outer shell (previously hung until timeout), capture-pane shows WS + Iroh markers in one shared pane with zero 'tmux new-session' residue, invalid name refused with 400 before any shell opens. Injection survives only as the v1-agent fallback in connect_to_vm, where no other channel exists.

title: Guard: schema bumps must extend @readable_schema_versions
description:
When the StateStore record schema next moves (v2 -> v3), the OLD version must be added to @readable_schema_versions in lib/mjolnir/state_store/record.ex, or every existing record on the server is quarantined on the next deploy.

Nothing currently enforces this — it is a comment and a convention. Consider a test that asserts @readable_schema_versions contains schema_version() and at least schema_version()-1, so dropping support becomes a deliberate, visible edit rather than an omission.

The forward direction (newer file, older binary) is now safe by construction: unknown versions are left in place and reported via StateStore.unreadable/0 + mj doctor (commit 579b7d2). This issue is only about the backward direction.

Context: docs/vm-metadata-and-generations.md
close_reason: Guard test added in 48390ac. Asserts @readable_schema_versions contains schema_version() and schema_version()-1 (skipping the impossible predecessor when version is 1). Proven to fire: dropping v1 produces a failure message naming the dropped version, what happens to existing records, and the two legitimate responses. Verified reverted, mix test green.

title: Harden the localhost auth bypass: don't key full admin scope on peer IP of a shared port
description:
Split out of mjolnir-fia, which is closed because its concrete exposure is mitigated (the gateway proxies the API to 10.255.255.1:4000, not loopback, and returns 401 without a token — verified from the public internet 2026-08-07).

The residual design smell: Mjolnir.API.Auth.localhost_bypass?/1 grants ALL scopes to any peer whose remote_ip is loopback, on the SAME port that serves everyone else. That makes the security boundary a one-line config mistake away — anything that ever proxies to 127.0.0.1:4000 (a future nginx, an SSH tunnel, a sidecar) silently becomes unauthenticated full admin. The Justfile's Sites recipes already rely on exactly that shape via ssh-wrapped curl.

Better: a dedicated unix socket (or a loopback-only listener on a separate port) that carries the bypass, so the privilege comes from which door you knocked on rather than from a header-derived IP on a shared door.
acceptance_criteria: The localhost bypass is reachable only via a distinct listener/socket; binding or proxying the public API port to loopback cannot grant admin scope.

title: Integration test: DELETE /api/vms/:id If-Match fencing
description:
The compare-and-delete fence is covered at the StateStore layer (delete_if_match/2, 4 tests) but the HTTP path is not: DELETE /api/vms/:id runs authorize_vm first, which requires a live VM GenServer, so the 409 generation_conflict branch cannot be reached from a unit test.

Add an :integration-tagged test that spawns a real VM, reads its generation, mutates the record, and asserts DELETE with a stale If-Match returns 409 and does NOT stop the VM. Also cover: matching If-Match deletes; malformed If-Match is 400; absent header is unconditional.

From mjolnir-oux.

title: Storage: compression + retention for memory ranges
description:
A btrfs snapshot is ~free (CoW). A memory snapshot of a 2GB VM is 2GB on disk, every time. Without compression and retention a busy host fills up.

Put memory ranges on a zstd-compressed btrfs subvolume and define a retention policy. This changes the economics of 'snapshot everything' — memory and filesystem snapshots are complementary, not substitutes, and callers should choose deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: Memory snapshot storage is compressed; retention policy documented and enforced; mj storage reports memory-snapshot usage separately from CoW usage.
notes:
Measured during the spike: memory-ranges is written UNCOMPRESSED at exactly mem_size — a 1GiB VM produced a 1073741824-byte file, and the snapshot dir totalled 1.1G. Confirms the cost concern. CH v52's memory_restore_mode (userfaultfd lazy paging) addresses restore LATENCY but not on-disk SIZE; compression and retention are still needed.
CH v53 does expose memory_restore_mode + userfaultfd (confirmed in the binary), so lazy demand-paging on restore is available to use — that addresses restore LATENCY. On-disk SIZE is still uncompressed full-RAM per snapshot, so compression + retention remain this bead's actual scope.
Useful datum from the mjolnir-8m3 fork probe: the btrfs volume at /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs is ALREADY mounted compress=zstd:3, so memory-ranges is transparently compressed today — a 512MB RAM image occupied ~119MB on disk (~4.3x). So the 'compression' half of this bead is largely already in place at the mount level; what is actually missing is RETENTION. Also relevant: reflinked copies of a memory image cost zero additional bytes, so forks/backups of the same snapshot are free.

title: Post-restore health must probe Iroh reachability
description:
HAZARD 7. The guest's Iroh node has live QUIC connections in restored RAM that are now dead. The node ID is stable so tickets survive, but the failure mode is nasty: the VM reports healthy while nothing can actually reach it.

Post-restore health must probe Iroh reachability, not just guest-agent ping. Relates to the existing health monitor work.
acceptance_criteria: A restored VM whose Iroh node has not re-established is reported unhealthy rather than running.

title: Clock resync on resume
description:
HAZARD 6. The guest wakes believing it is snapshot-time. Certificate validity windows, agent timeouts, cron, and log timestamps all skew by the freeze duration — which for a parked agent VM could be days.

Needs a KVM-clock adjust or a guest-agent time-sync step on resume, executed before userspace continues.
acceptance_criteria: A VM frozen for over an hour reports correct wall-clock time immediately on resume, before any userspace process observes the old time.
notes: Likely fixed upstream by CH v52.0 (#7932): 'The KVM clock is now restored before vCPUs are resumed.' Re-verify after mjolnir-3y6.15 rather than implementing a guest-agent time-sync; this may reduce to a verification task.

title: recrypt encryption for Buzz Blossom media
description:
Buzz has no E2E encryption by design: 'server-managed encryption covers every channel, every DM, every event — eDiscovery works on everything.' Recrypt dissolves that tradeoff instead of picking a side: relay holds ciphertext + per-viewer recryption keys, recrypts the wrapped KEM key per read, never touches DEM bulk ciphertext, revocation atomic. Compliance access becomes a signed revocable capability grant to an auditor npub instead of standing plaintext.

SEQUENCING: Blossom blobs FIRST, not DMs. The relay runs permission-aware Postgres FTS over message content; encrypting message bodies collides head-on with search, which is exactly why Block punted. Blossom media has no FTS dependency and is the same shape as IdentiKey Sites' chunk+manifest layer.

Phase 1 blobs -> Phase 2 canvases -> Phase 3 DMs (requires an encrypted-search design first; do not promise before then).

Open: which recrypt license path permits Apache-2.0-side integration.

title: Wedged-body reaping for Buzz agents (closes spec's I5 boundary)
description:
Buzz spec I5 boundary (a): a process too wedged to run its own reaper cannot reap itself; the spec punts to 'a namespace-level TTL policy, out of scope'.

Mjolnir.Health probes the guest agent over vsock from OUTSIDE the guest, so a wedged VM is reapable without in-guest cooperation. Strictly better than a TTL: a TTL also kills healthy long-lived agents (the inactivity_seconds:0 case the spec explicitly blesses); a liveness probe kills only the wedged.

WARNING: classify a force-reap as an ABNORMAL death, never intentional. Getting this backwards corrupts the intent/accident distinction that makes indefinite agents safe under I5.

Offer the substrate-neutral phrasing upstream for spec v2.

title: Snapshot-resume for Buzz agent VMs
description:
On stop: btrfs subvolume snapshot of the agent rootfs, tagged with agent pubkey + management markers. On create: clone from snapshot if present, else from @base/buzz-agent. Retention per pubkey; GC under the same marker+generation fence.

This is the differentiator — it defeats the spec's conceded cost that 'the body's state is mortal... unless the substrate supplies persistence'.

CRITICAL: do NOT wire DormantRegistry wake-on-message to relay traffic. I5 forbids automatic revival of an intentional exit. Snapshot-resume is an optimization of the CREATE path under an owner-initiated Start, never a second trigger. This is the single easiest way to make the provider non-conforming, and it is tempting precisely because the machinery already exists.

title: mj domain set/rm: support Sites alias target via --keypair-file
description: Teach mj domain set (and rm) to bind custom domains to IdentiKey Sites: with --keypair-file, treat the positional as a site name, sign an AliasRecord client-side, and PUT/DELETE /api/sites/:fp/:site/aliases/:fqdn. App path unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Gateway re-issues ACME on every SIGHUP reload instead of using the cached cert -> Let's Encrypt duplicate-cert rate-limit churn
description: Observed 2026-07-19/20: several gateway config reloads (SIGHUP) for a new [[cert]]/[[domain]] each triggered a fresh ACME issuance attempt for the PINNED worldtree SAN set, hitting Let's Encrypt's 'too many certificates (5) for this exact set of identifiers in 168h' duplicate-cert rate limit ('retry after 2026-07-21'). Harmless (existing worldtree cert valid to October; zine+startupcentral.build use [[cert]] files not ACME), but it's self-inflicted churn that could block a REAL renewal if it coincided.
design: acme.rs already has load_or_issue/2 (acme.rs:141-155) that returns the cached cert when remaining > renew_before and only issues otherwise. The SIGHUP reload path appears to call issue() (or bypass the cache) instead of load_or_issue — route reload through the cache-aware path so a valid, non-near-expiry cert is REUSED, not re-requested. Confirm the cert cache persists across reloads/restarts (path/load in load_cached). Add a test that reload with a fresh cached cert does NOT call issue().
acceptance_criteria: Repeated gateway SIGHUP reloads with a valid cached cert issue ZERO new ACME requests; issuance happens only when the cert is missing or within renew_before of expiry.
notes: FIXED IN CODE (main, commit 7525345): real offender was the SIGHUP handler (main.rs:1525), not only the renewal loop (:247) — both now call acme::load_or_issue instead of issue(). Added should_issue/3 predicate + SAN-coverage check (cert_dns_sans/cert_covers_domains via x509-parser): reuse cache ONLY if fresh AND covers all cfg.domains; re-issue on missing/near-expiry/SAN-change. 5 new tests incl. SAN-change re-issue. 36/36 gateway tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tune LUKS KDF for host-escrowed RANDOM passphrase — argon2id memory-hardening is redundant (the real managed-boot-speed fix)
description: Managed-secrets LUKS create uses argon2id (cryptsetup default) — a memory-hard, deliberately-slow KDF. That's what blows past await_boot on small-RAM VMs (the 90s bump in commit 25fef62 is only a safety net). But argon2id exists to make brute-forcing a GUESSABLE/low-entropy passphrase expensive. mjolnir's managed passphrase is a FRESH RANDOM 256-bit key (secret_escrow.ex: @passphrase_bytes 32, :crypto.strong_rand_bytes, per-VM). You cannot brute-force a random 256-bit key with ANY KDF (2^256 keyspace) — the security is the passphrase entropy, not KDF slowness. So argon2id hardening buys ~nothing against our actual threat model (attacker has the data-volume/snapshot ciphertext but NOT the host escrow).
design: In the guest-side luksFormat (see vm.ex maybe_unlock_secrets / guest agent inject_secrets), pass a minimal-cost KDF: e.g. --pbkdf pbkdf2 --pbkdf-force-iterations 1000, or --pbkdf argon2id with small --pbkdf-memory + low --iter-time. Fast boot, no real security loss because the passphrase is high-entropy random. DOCUMENT the reasoning inline (random passphrase => KDF hardening redundant) so it reads as an intentional, reviewed security decision, not an accidental weakening. Keep the 90s await_boot as a belt-and-suspenders. Verify managed boot completes well under 30s after tuning -> then the managed-mode await_boot bump can arguably revert to default.
acceptance_criteria: A managed-secrets VM boots (LUKS create+open) in well under the default 30s await_boot with an unchanged effective security posture (random 256-bit passphrase).
notes: LANDED IN CODE (main, commit 5b23fc8): guest agent secrets.rs luksFormat now uses --pbkdf pbkdf2 --pbkdf-force-iterations 1000 (was default argon2id); cipher aes-xts-plain64/key-size 512/luks2 unchanged. Refactored to pure luks_format_args/1 + unit test. Guest-agent crate is Linux-only (tokio-vsock) so no macOS cargo gate; boot-time speedup must be verified server-side after a guest-agent rebuild (just deploy --agent). Safe: passphrase is random 256-bit (secret_escrow), KDF hardening redundant.

title: Per-domain cert provisioning: ACME-if-token-scoped, else install a provided Cloudflare Origin CA cert
description: TLS for a custom apex needs a cert the gateway serves. Gateway ACME (Let's Encrypt DNS-01) is PINNED to worldtree zones (the CF token's scope) — it can't auto-issue for arbitrary domains (e.g. identikey.io and startupcentral.build are both served via hand-installed [[cert]] blocks). So domain onboarding must support the manual/BYO-cert path as a first-class flow.
design: mj domain cert <fqdn> [--origin-ca <cert> <key> | --acme]. If the ACME token covers the zone, add fqdn to [acme].domains and let it issue. Else install a BYO cert (Cloudflare Origin CA, 15yr) to /etc/mjolnir/certs/<app>/ (owned by the gateway user 999:988, key 0600) + a [[cert]] block, SIGHUP reload. For Cloudflare-proxied apps this pairs with orange + Full(strict). startupcentral.build used exactly this (Origin CA) — codify it.
acceptance_criteria: mj domain cert installs/renews a serving cert for the fqdn; gateway presents it on SNI; Full(strict) via Cloudflare validates.
notes: LANDED IN CODE (main, commit 539b6f5): Mjolnir.Gateway.Certs — ensure/2 (mode :origin_ca default | :acme worktree-only), list/1, remove/2; injectable effects seam (file/chown/reload/openssl), writes [[cert]]+[[domain]] into base gateway.toml (header-aware chunk edit, idempotent), key 0600 owner 999:988, SIGHUP reload. 23 tests. INTEGRATION SEAM for the domain endpoint (server lane / follow-up): Mjolnir.Gateway.Certs.ensure(fqdn, mode: :origin_ca, cert: pem, key: pem). Known limits: apex_of/2 wrong for multi-part public suffixes (pass :apex); toml_acme_add_domain only handles single-line domains=[...].

title: Dynamic apex registration (add fqdn apex to :gateway_apexes + [[domain]]) without an orchestrator restart
description: For the reconciler to emit a route for a new apex, the fqdn's apex must be in :gateway_apexes (orchestrator app-env) AND have a [[domain]] (+ serving cert) in the gateway. Both are static config today; adding an apex is a config-file edit. This is the hardest piece of domain automation.
design: Investigate: Application.put_env(:mjolnir, :gateway_apexes, ...) at runtime takes effect for the next reconcile without restart (reconciler reads configured_apexes() live) — but is lost on restart, so also persist to config durably. The gateway's [[domain]] block + fallthrough=none must be added to gateway.toml (or a reconciler-managed drop-in) and SIGHUP-reloaded. Decide whether apexes become reconciler-owned (generated) vs a managed list. NOTE: the migration task (startupcentral.build -> reconciler) will produce the definitive answer on restart-need + persistence; fold its findings in.
acceptance_criteria: Registering a new apex for a deployed app requires no orchestrator restart and survives one; reconciler emits the route and gateway serves it.
notes:
MIGRATION FINDINGS (2026-07-20): Application.put_env(:mjolnir, :gateway_apexes, ...) DOES take effect live with no restart (reconciler reads configured_apexes/0 each render — verified). BUT it's EPHEMERAL: gateway_apexes is set at COMPILE TIME in config/config.exs:76 and baked into the released sys.config; there is NO env-var/runtime override. So on the next mjolnir.service restart the apex reverts and startupcentral.build's route is dropped -> downtime. Two-sided requirement per apex: Elixir :gateway_apexes (so split_fqdn matches) AND a Rust-side [[domain]] block in gateway.toml (drop-ins can't declare apexes; applies on SIGHUP, no restart). CORE FIX (biggest friction point): make :gateway_apexes RUNTIME-configurable (env var or a managed file read in runtime.exs) so adding a domain never needs an orchestrator recompile/redeploy. Durable-today fallback: edit config.exs:76 + rebuild/redeploy the release. CLI must own both the apex-list edit and the gateway.toml [[domain]] edit, and warn that persistence needs a redeploy until apexes are runtime-configurable.
LANDED IN CODE (main, commit 1c0f520): config/runtime.exs reads MJOLNIR_GATEWAY_APEXES (comma-sep), merges with the compile-time default (dedup, defaults-first); env-unset path identical to today. Set it in /etc/mjolnir/env to add an apex durably without recompile. configured_apexes/0 unchanged. 3 tests. Still needs the gateway.toml [[domain]] side per apex (12.2/12.4).

title: Cut Zine over to mj deploy + managed secrets — retire manual git deploy and tmpfs inject
description:
The capstone migration: move Zine prod (currently VM 076adf62, manual git-reset/build/restart deploy, tmpfs secrets via scripts/mjolnir-inject-secrets.sh re-run after every reboot) onto the mj deploy flow with secrets_mode: :managed. Zine is the reference stateful app: bun + SvelteKit adapter-node + better-sqlite3 (trustedDependencies committed), drizzle migrations, local.db holds subscribers + newsletter send ledger (MUST survive deploys — needs gge.7 release-dir mode), non-secret /opt/app/.env config, AWS SES + Beehiiv creds (managed secrets, seeded once at /var/lib/mjolnir/zine-secrets.json per docs/runbooks/zine-managed-secrets-migration.md).

Cutover steps: (1) registry entry takes over zine.identikey.io (custom_domain+port landed 2026-07-01; remove the hardcoded gateway_extra_domains route in config/prod.exs:17 — l79.5); (2) seed host secrets file; (3) first mj deploy, verify (send a dry-run newsletter + test-list send before trusting it); (4) copy local.db into the new home with the old app quiesced (clean sqlite copy); (5) kill old VM, retire inject script, update Zine-repo bd memories (mjolnir-deploy-state, ticket refs). secrets_mode is fixed at spawn — no in-place conversion, hence new VM. NOT to be run near a newsletter send.

title: Deploy-path managed-secrets plumbing — per-app secrets file → spawn_opts on every deploy
description: Deploy.Runtime.start already passes spawn_opts through (secrets_mode: :managed + secrets payload work today — the zine-managed-secrets-migration runbook drives it by hand via rpc). What's missing is the orchestrator wiring: the deploy pipeline (gge.1.6) reads a per-app secrets file on the host (/var/lib/mjolnir/<app>-secrets.json, 0600, off the data volume) and folds {secrets_mode: :managed, secrets: creds} into the Runtime.start spawn_opts automatically. Because release snapshots carry no LUKS volume, secrets are re-supplied on every deploy from that host file — it is the source of truth; rotation = edit file + redeploy. Apply to RUNTIME spawn only, never Deploy.Builder (a LUKS volume in a build layer would be keyed to the throwaway build VM and baked into the snapshot). In release-dir mode (gge.7) the long-lived VM is spawned managed once, and deploys just re-render env if changed. Relates: gge.3 (tmpfs render — shipped), gge.6 (recrypt end-state replaces the host-held file).
notes: Managed-secrets await_boot TIMEOUT FIXED (main, commit 25fef62): root cause = do_boot runs LUKS create (cryptsetup luksFormat argon2id, memory-hard KDF) synchronously near the tail of boot, exceeding the fixed 30s await_boot -> spawn returns {:error,:timeout} and strands an appless VM (guest actually boots fine). Fix: :await_boot_timeout spawn opt; managed mode defaults to 90s (@managed_await_boot_timeout), non-managed stays 30s. Deploy.Runtime needs no change (secrets_mode flows via spawn_opts). This unblocks managed secrets for the deploy path (the rest of gge.10 = per-app secrets file -> spawn_opts wiring).

title: deploy.sh --gateway is not gateway-only: always rebuilds + restarts Elixir
description:
scripts/deploy.sh gates the gateway BUILD behind --gateway (lines 208-214), but the Elixir release build (line 241 'mix release') and 'systemctl restart mjolnir' (line 254) are UNCONDITIONAL — they run on every invocation, including 'just deploy-gateway'. So there is no gateway-only mode: deploying the gateway also rebuilds and restarts the main Elixir process, which triggers the Cleanup-kills-VMs -> Reconcile-resumes-from-StateStore cycle (a brief downtime window for every running VM) and ships whatever Elixir code is on the tree.

EXPECTED: '--gateway' (and a 'just deploy-gateway') should build + install + restart ONLY mjolnir-gateway, leaving the Elixir service untouched. Symmetrically, a plain deploy should be able to skip the gateway. This matters for safe, isolated rollouts (validate a gateway change without bouncing all VMs).

FIX SKETCH: gate the Elixir build+restart (lines 238-254) behind a flag (e.g. default-on, but skipped when a new --gateway-only / --no-elixir flag is passed, OR make --gateway imply gateway-only unless combined with a full-deploy flag). Preserve current 'just deploy' (full) behavior; add 'just deploy-gateway' = gateway-only. Update the Justfile recipes + CLAUDE.md docs accordingly.

Found during gateway local-routing rollout (epic mjolnir-l79).
close_reason: Fixed in 462aaf6. --gateway is now gateway-only (skips mix release + systemctl restart mjolnir, so it no longer bounces every running VM via Cleanup->Reconcile); --full opts back in. Flag matrix executed rather than assumed: (none)/--agent/--rootfs/--runner/'--gateway --full' all still build+restart Elixir; --gateway and '--gateway --agent' skip it. bash -n and just --list pass. CLAUDE.md documents the new flag.

title: Fold gateway route generator into Forge (with gge.4 dynamic declarations)
description:
Replace the bespoke Mjolnir.Gateway.Routes write-file+systemctl-reload with a Forge-managed resource, so gateway routing converges/drifts/prunes like every other host resource instead of being a parallel reconciler. See docs/forge-architecture.md (Relationship to Deploy) + docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md.

Effort assessment (from code review):
- FREE: the drop-in file IS a Forge 'file' resource — apply writes content+mode, drift diffs source bytes, delete prunes.
- EASY: reload-on-change — Forge only calls apply/3 on :new/:drifted/:missing (never :converged), so putting 'systemctl reload' inside a dedicated gateway_routes resource kind's apply (per resource.ex:15 'daemon-reload, ufw reload' pattern) fires ONLY when routes changed. No notify/handler machinery needed.
- THE REAL GAP: dynamic declarations. Forge declarations are static .exs files loaded from disk (Declarations compiles forge/declarations/*.exs; reload/0 re-reads disk). No runtime API to update a declaration when a VM starts/stops. Gateway routes are dynamic.

STRATEGIC: that dynamic-declaration capability is exactly what gge.4 (Forge-over-vsock deploy) needs — Deploy generates per-app run-state resources at deploy time. So build 'programmatic/in-memory declaration source' (e.g. Declarations.put_dynamic(host, resources) merged with file-based) for gge.4, and the gateway route generator becomes its first trivial consumer. Do NOT build it standalone. Blocked-on/with: deploy epic gge.4.

title: Deploy: --domain plumbing + backfill zine into Deploy.Registry
description:
Gateway local-routing epic (mjolnir-l79) is live. Two follow-ups to fully close the loop:
1. mj deploy --domain <fqdn>: plumb a custom domain through Deploy.Runtime so Deploy-managed apps set Registry.Entry.custom_domain (+port already recorded). Until then, Mjolnir.Gateway.Routes only auto-routes apps listed in :gateway_extra_domains.
2. Backfill zine into Deploy.Registry (custom_domain=zine.identikey.io, port=3000) OR migrate zine through Deploy.Runtime, then drop the pinned entry from config/prod.exs :gateway_extra_domains (its vm_id 076adf62 is hardcoded and will go stale if zine is re-provisioned).
Also: consider fixing the deploy.sh gateway preflight (Python tomllib check over ssh with nested quotes gives false-positive 'failed to parse' warnings — it doesn't reflect the Rust parser).

title: Gateway: Elixir route generator renders gateway.d/apps.toml from live VM state
description:
Phase 2 of gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md). Depends on Phase 1 drop-in loader. Automatically keep local [[route]] entries fresh so co-located app VMs are served over local TCP (no Iroh), eliminating the ~7s cold-start (proven in Phase 0).

Design: new Mjolnir.Gateway.Routes module renders /etc/mjolnir/gateway.d/apps.toml: for each app with a custom domain whose VM is on THIS host, emit [[route]] apex/subdomain/backend where backend = <guest_ip>:<port>. Atomic write + reload (systemctl reload mjolnir-gateway once ExecReload is added, else systemctl kill -s HUP). Full re-render each time (small N), idempotent. Trigger on: deploy cutover (Deploy.Runtime after registry_put) + EventBus :vm_restored/:vm_started + Mjolnir boot.

CRITICAL findings from live validation:
- guest_ip is already exposed by GET /api/vms (and VM status) — READ IT, do not recompute Network.allocate_ip. Simpler and authoritative.
- zine is NOT in Deploy.Registry (manually provisioned). The generator must NOT assume every served app has a registry entry. Source of truth for domain→VM intent is currently only the gateway [[alias]]. Options: (a) backfill Deploy.Registry with a domain+VM for manual apps, (b) generate routes by joining existing [[alias]] entries (domain→ticket) to live VMs (ticket→guest_ip via /api/vms). Recommend: add custom_domain + port (structured) to Deploy.Registry.Entry AND make manual provisioning write a registry entry, so the registry is the single source of truth.
- guest_ip stable across restart/restore (vm_id preserved) but CHANGES on redeploy — regeneration on cutover is the point.
Acceptance: redeploy an app, gateway.d/apps.toml updates with new guest_ip, requests log route=local; restart host → routes regenerate from live state.
close_reason: Duplicate of mjolnir-l79.2/.3/.4 (existing epic). Findings folded into those.

title: Gateway: drop-in config dir loader (/etc/mjolnir/gateway.d/*.toml)
description:
Phase 1 of gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md). Let machine-generated routes live separately from the hand-maintained base so an Elixir generator (mjolnir-<phase2>) can own them without co-editing gateway.toml.

Design (native/mjolnir_gateway/src/config.rs): in load(path), after parsing the base file into FileConfig, glob <dir>/gateway.d/*.toml (sorted), parse each into a FileConfig (fields use serde renames: [[domain]]/[[route]]/[[alias]]/[[cert]]), and EXTEND base.routes/.aliases/.certs with each drop-in's before calling validate_and_normalize(merged, Toml). Drop-ins contribute routes/aliases/certs only; apexes/global config stay in the base. SIGHUP already re-runs load() (main.rs:1338-1459), so reload picks up drop-in changes for free.

Notes from live validation:
- Single-file load() today (config.rs:409); no include/merge — this adds it.
- Apex key is [[domain]] with fallthrough, not [[apex]].
- Existing config.alias_shadowed_by_route warning fires when a route shadows an alias; keep that behavior.
- Add unit tests for merge (base + N drop-ins → combined route/alias counts; dedup-by-(apex,subdomain) semantics; malformed drop-in is warn-and-skipped, never crashes load).
Acceptance: drop a file in gateway.d, SIGHUP, route appears; bad file logged + skipped; base-only still works.
close_reason: Duplicate of mjolnir-l79.2/.3/.4 (existing epic). Findings folded into those.

title: Phase 3: gateway local-dial -> Iroh alias failover (Rust)
description: On Disposition::Local dial failure, fall back to handle_iroh_connection if an alias exists for the same (apex,subdomain). Makes stale routes self-healing; multi-host migration seam.
notes: Deployed + verified live. Gateway logged 'retaining Iroh node as route fallback' for zine (was 'skipping alias'). Self-healing fallback active.
close_reason: Closed

title: Integration test + docs: managed-secrets dormancy roundtrip
description: Server-gated integration test: spawn :managed → secrets present → dormant → wake → secrets restored (verifies LUKS blob survives snapshot clone). Unit tests for SecretEscrow + protocol encode. Extend docs/secrets-architecture.md with :managed mode + escrow custody + threat row.
notes: Docs DONE (committed 42e16aa: managed mode section + path corrections). REMAINING: (1) server deploy to build Rust guest agent (just deploy-full / --agent) since tokio-vsock won't build on macOS; (2) integration test: spawn :managed -> push secrets -> dormant -> wake -> assert secrets restored (verifies LUKS blob survives snapshot clone + escrowed-passphrase re-open). This is the one empirical unknown.

Rust compiled clean with full+iroh. Guest LUKS create/open works on default base image.

title: Repair MIX_ENV=test btrfs infra on server so :integration tests run via ExUnit
description: On 45.76.77.97 the test btrfs root /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs-test has DANGLING symlinks: @base -> /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@base-test (missing) and @vms -> @vms-test (missing), and no @snapshots symlink. So 'MIX_ENV=test mix test --include integration' cannot spawn (no base image in test root). For gge.1.4 the Builder integration test was instead run live via 'mjolnir rpc Code.eval_file' inside the prod node (passed). To make test/mjolnir/deploy/builder_integration_test.exs (and the existing snapshot/vm integration tests) runnable as ExUnit on the server: populate @base-test/ubuntu-24.04 (btrfs snapshot of prod @base/ubuntu-24.04), create @vms-test, and add an @snapshots subvol on the same btrfs fs (symlink from btrfs-test). Also confirm a second test BEAM's startup Cleanup sweep won't disturb live prod VMs (scope check).
notes:
STORAGE HALF DONE 2026-08-12 (on root@45.76.77.97, no prod state touched — only new subvolumes created):
  btrfs subvolume create /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@vms-test
  btrfs subvolume create /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@snapshots-test
  btrfs subvolume snapshot /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@base/ubuntu-24.04 /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@base-test/ubuntu-24.04
  ln -s /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs/@snapshots-test /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs-test/@snapshots
All three symlinks under /var/lib/mjolnir/btrfs-test now resolve (@base, @vms, @snapshots were dangling/absent), and @base/ubuntu-24.04 carries /usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent, so a test BEAM has a spawnable base image.

SCOPE CHECK DONE, AND IT FOUND A BLOCKER — see mjolnir-0ut, now a dependency. Summary: Cleanup.sweep is config-scoped for hypervisors (ps filtered by socket_dir: test /tmp/mjolnir-test vs prod /tmp/mjolnir), sockets, and rootfs (btrfs_root), so those cannot touch prod. But clean_orphan_taps/0 (cleanup.ex:112) takes no config and deletes ANY host interface matching mj-* in state DOWN, so a test BEAM's startup sweep can cut a production VM's networking whenever that VM's TAP is momentarily DOWN (mid-boot or wedged). All 4 prod TAPs happened to be UP at inspection time, so the window is currently closed by luck, not design.

DO NOT run a second BEAM on this host until mjolnir-0ut is fixed.

title: Gateway: cert issue --manual perms + renewal reminder
description: Manual issuance writes fullchain/privkey as the invoking user (root via ssh), but the gateway runs as 'mjolnir' and can't read a 0600 root key (had to chown manually). Options: --owner flag, or write group-readable, or doc to run as gateway user. Also: manually-issued certs (e.g. zine.identikey.io, expires 2026-09-22) do NOT auto-renew — add an expiry reminder/notification. Parent mjolnir-er5.

title: Gateway: exclude BYO-cert/foreign-apex hosts from ACME SAN derivation
description: derive_san_list currently adds alias FQDNs and none-apex domains to the auto-derived ACME SAN list. For an apex whose DNS zone the Cloudflare token can't manage (e.g. identikey.io), this would make the combined cert order fail and break wildcard renewal. Workaround in prod: explicit [acme].domains pin. Proper fix: hosts served by a [[cert]] (BYO) must be excluded from ACME SAN derivation; reconsider auto-adding alias FQDNs. Parent mjolnir-er5.

title: Gateway: pre-warm Iroh connections for aliased nodes
description: Eliminate cold-start latency on domain->VM requests. When a [[alias]] is configured, eagerly open + keep-alive the Iroh connection to that node so the first request hits a warm pooled connection (no per-request lookup/dial). Keeps ports inside the VM (identity-based) while matching local-dial speed. Chosen direction after zine.identikey.io went live via Iroh alias. Parent mjolnir-er5.

title: Gateway: manual DNS-01 cert issuance subcommand
description: Add 'mjolnir-gateway cert issue --manual --domain D --out DIR' reusing acme.rs flow but printing the _acme-challenge TXT and waiting for operator confirmation instead of writing via Cloudflare API. Writes fullchain/privkey for SNI multi-cert to serve. Parent: mjolnir-er5.
close_reason: Closed

title: Gateway: SNI multi-cert serving (bring-your-own-cert)
description: Extend gateway cert resolver to select per-SNI with fallback to the ACME/static primary cert. Add [[cert]] config (host, cert, key) + SIGHUP hot-reload. Decouples serving HTTPS for a host from holding a Cloudflare API token for its DNS zone. Parent: mjolnir-er5.
close_reason: Closed

title: Gateway: vanity-subdomain → Iroh node ID aliases
description: Add [[alias]] table to mjolnir-gateway config mapping a friendly (apex, subdomain) to a pinned Iroh node ID (+optional port). Resolves in classify() before fallthrough, reusing the existing Iroh proxy path. Survives VM respawns (node ID travels with VM identity, unlike a TAP-IP pin). Motivating case: zine.identikey.io → node xebksroii…76njo. Includes config parse/validate, RouteTable.lookup_alias, SAN derivation, tests, example config.
notes: zine.identikey.io LIVE in production: HTTP 200, valid per-host LE cert via SNI, routed via Iroh alias to VM 076adf62:3000. Stack delivered: [[alias]] Iroh routing + SNI multi-cert serving + manual DNS-01 issuance. Live config pins [acme].domains to worldtree set so ACME never touches identikey.io. Follow-ups filed: pre-warm, SAN-derivation fix, cert perms/renewal, forgejo bind.

title: Ghost-record cleanup: stranded :running records churn every reconcile tick (17 stranded, 14 DEAD on restart)
description: On a server restart (root@45.76.77.97, 2026-06-24) StartupReconcile rehydrated 17 stranded :running records (s8h parallel resume working, max_concurrency=4); Health.Monitor then declared 14 distinct VMs 'DEAD, not auto-healing'. These are genuinely-dead ghosts (their GenServers exited after failed resume → not in 'mj list' → back to stranded), so each reconcile tick (every 30s) re-attempts resume → fails → DEAD, indefinitely. The durability invariant correctly PRESERVES rootfs/records (no vanishing), but there is no lifecycle end-state for a record that can never resume. mj retire/revive/forget verbs exist (5fu) to clear these by hand; consider an auto-retire policy after N consecutive failed resume attempts so the backlog self-drains. NOTE: VM 076adf62 is ALIVE (exec works) despite a false-positive :egress_blocked (see the ping bug) — do not forget it.
notes: RESOLVED the symptom 2026-06-24: the 16 'ghosts' were NOT dead records — they were live, responsive CI-runner VMs (hostname ci-runner, owner=localhost, 17 live cloud-hypervisor procs) leaked by the Forgejo runner. mj retire 404'd (token owner != localhost) then returned vm_running (they were registered+running, not stranded). Killed all 16 via the localhost API bypass (DELETE /api/vms/:id as owner=localhost); rootfs soft-deleted to @trash (recoverable ~7d). Verified: VM count 17→1, CH procs 17→1, my VM 076adf62 preserved. ROOT CAUSE remains (reframe this issue around it): the Forgejo runner does not tear down per-job VMs, and durability epic r84 then resurrects every leaked :running record on each restart — so leaked CI sandboxes accumulate durably. Fix belongs at the runner teardown path (ensure VM destroy on job completion), not in reconcile. Related: health false-positive 3h3 made them all log as DEAD.
close_reason: Resolved by the auto-retire policy this issue asked for, delivered in mjolnir-5fu/azl. Reconcile.note_failure/1 counts consecutive failures in the record's runtime map and flips intent :running -> :failed after :reconcile_max_failures (config.exs:43, default 10) or once the streak exceeds :reconcile_failure_ttl_seconds (config.exs:44, 24h); :failed records are not auto-resumed, so the backlog self-drains instead of churning every 30s tick. Verified live on root@45.76.77.97 2026-08-12: state dir holds 4 records, all intent=running, matching the 4 live VMs — no stranded ghosts remain of the original 17 — and journalctl shows zero 'DEAD, not auto-healing' or 'failed attempt' lines in 2 hours. Operator escape hatches (mj retire/revive/forget) also exist.

title: Health L2 guest_network probe false-positives :egress_blocked when guest lacks ping (iputils)
description: Mjolnir.Health.GuestNetwork.probe/1 runs 'ping -c1 -W2 1.1.1.1' inside the guest via vsock exec; on failure it returns {:dead, :egress_blocked}. The ubuntu-24.04 base rootfs has NO ping binary ('sh: ping: not found'), so the command fails with command-not-found → echoes NOPING → the VM is classified :dead even though egress works fine (verified live: default route present, DNS resolves, 'curl https://registry.npmjs.org/' → HTTP 200 in 0.6s on VM 076adf62). Net effect: every VM on this base shows overall :dead in 'mj doctor', Health.Monitor logs spurious 'DEAD, not auto-healing', and the heal path needlessly calls reconfigure_network. Found 2026-06-24 verifying a deploy on root@45.76.77.97.
design: Test the property (TCP egress), not a specific tool. Replace the ICMP ping with a no-extra-binary TCP dial, e.g. bash: 'timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/1.1.1.1/443"' → connect success = egress OK. This matches what apps actually do (TCP) and survives a base image without iputils or with ICMP filtered. Alternative/secondary: add iputils-ping to the base rootfs, but the probe should not depend on it. Keep the NOROUTE fast-path.
acceptance_criteria: A VM with working TCP egress but no ping binary reports L2 guest_network :ok; a VM with a wiped default route still reports :no_default_route; a VM with genuinely blocked egress reports dead.
close_reason: Duplicate of mjolnir-58w (same probe, same root cause), both fixed in 1f0a480 and verified independently 2026-08-12. GuestNetwork.probe/1 no longer hard-codes ping: it requires a default route, then tries curl, wget, then ping, and reports :degraded/:no_egress_probe_tool when none exists rather than falsely claiming :dead. That is exactly this issue's DESIGN note — test the property (egress), not a specific tool. Live check: all 4 VMs report state running, zero 'DEAD, not auto-healing' lines in the last 2 hours.

title: mj deploy client subcommand — tar cwd (gitignore-honoring), POST /api/deploy, print URL
description: New 'mj deploy' subcommand in native/mjolnir_client (DISTINCT from 'mj server deploy' which runs scripts/deploy.sh). Tar the current directory as the source (respect .gitignore/.dockerignore; prefer 'git archive HEAD' on a clean repo, with --dirty to include uncommitted work), POST to /api/deploy with token auth, stream build progress, print the final URL. P0: tar-the-cwd only (git-URL/deploy-key ingest is gge.2/P1).
notes:
Rust — builds on the SERVER (client cross-compile). Depends on the /api/deploy route. P0 ingest = tar cwd, the zero-auth front door.

title: P1.5 — Secrets hygiene: render env to tmpfs (/run) + re-inject secrets on wake (unblocks scale-to-zero)
description: Two cheap changes that unblock compute billing. (1) Move the rendered env render target from /etc/mjolnir/secrets.env (PLAINTEXT on rootfs → baked into every snapshot layer) to /run/mjolnir/secrets.env (tmpfs, RAM-backed, never persisted/snapshotted); service unit uses EnvironmentFile=/run/mjolnir/secrets.env. One-path change in native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/secrets.rs. (2) Wire secret re-inject on VM wake: control plane re-authorizes the peer and re-pushes secrets over the existing SECRET_INJECT_ALPN path when a dormant VM wakes — so secrets_mode: :persistent VMs (which currently REFUSE dormancy at vm.ex:657 because nobody can supply the LUKS passphrase on auto-wake) can finally scale to zero.
design: Hard rule: cut build-cache layers BEFORE any secret load; build-time secrets live outside the layer cache key AND outside the snapshotted rootfs (inject to tmpfs for the build step, discard before snapshot). Avoid render-into-LUKS (the LUKS file lives on rootfs → snapshot still carries the encrypted secret). Preserves the injector's zero-host-trust posture: passphrase/source stays external.
acceptance_criteria: No plaintext secret on the rootfs or in any snapshot layer; a secret-bearing app goes dormant and wakes with secrets re-injected.

title: P1 — Generalize detection (buildpacks) + optional mjolnir.toml manifest + deploys/logs/rollback/destroy
description: Deploy.Detector buildpack: inspect app dir → build plan. Detect package manager FROM THE LOCKFILE (bun.lock→bun, pnpm-lock.yaml→pnpm, package-lock.json→npm; default npm) — not an assumption; npm/bun/pnpm differ in install cmd, prod-dep flag, and lifecycle-script behavior. Buildpacks: generic Node, Python (requirements.txt/pyproject.toml), Procfile (Heroku-compatible process types). Optional mjolnir.toml = DECLARATIVE OVERRIDE (runtime, custom build steps, start, port, env), never a replacement, never an imperative script. CLI: mj deploys, mj deploy logs/rollback/destroy. Rollback is free (re-point to previous immutable snapshot).
design: Real-app hazards the buildpack must anticipate (field-validated vs Zine, a bun+adapter-node+better-sqlite3 app): (1) native modules + bun's blocked postinstall → detect native deps & trust install scripts, or run-with-node; build native deps ON TARGET (linux-x64), never ship from dev Mac; (2) runtime≠PM (build-with-bun, run-with-node split); (3) SvelteKit prerender treats broken links as fatal → surface as APP build failure, not platform error; (4) apps have pre-build generators → that's what manifest custom steps are for. The manifest escape hatch is load-bearing for real apps — design in from P1.
notes: Source ingest decided: tar-the-cwd is the front door (respect .gitignore/.dockerignore; prefer git archive HEAD on clean repos). Private-repo deploy-key pull is first-class (ed25519 per app, key stored via secrets injector; Forgejo API can auto-register since we own the forge).

title: Port VM/snapshot diagnostic verbs to mj binary
description: mj covers VM lifecycle (spawn/list/info/exec/kill/url, snapshot/snapshots) but lacks the diagnostic/operational verbs the Justfile still has: vm-health (L0-L4 probe /api/vms/:id/health), vm-heal (/heal), vm-stop-all (bulk delete), vm-ticket (/ticket), vm-await-pty (/await-pty), vm-message (/messages dormant-wake), snap-info (/snapshots/:name), snap-delete (DELETE /snapshots/:name), dormant (/api/dormant).
