title: Switch default base image from Arch to Ubuntu 24.04
description:
Arch is a rolling release: a baked base image drifts out of date within weeks, and Arch does not support partial upgrades, so 'pacman -S <pkg>' fails unless you 'pacman -Syu' the world. Ubuntu 24.04 LTS keeps a frozen, installable package set for years. Switch the default base image to ubuntu-24.04 and retire Arch as the assumed default.

Changes:
- config/config.exs: default_base_image arch -> ubuntu-24.04
- lib/mjolnir/cloud_hypervisor/config.ex: reconcile struct default
- Justfile: deploy-rootfs distro default arch -> ubuntu-24.04
- lib/mjolnir/vm.ex: docstring/example default
- test/chaos/*.exs: 6 tests flip base_image arch -> ubuntu-24.04
- Server: rebuild @base/ubuntu-24.04 via just deploy-rootfs ubuntu-24.04

Architecture is already distro-agnostic (no arch-specific code in lib/); both rootfs builders produce identical systemd+mjolnir-agent.service contract.
close_reason: Default base image switched to ubuntu-24.04. Verified live: VM spawned with default base booted Ubuntu 24.04 LTS with apt present. @base/ubuntu-24.04 built on server (634M, agent enabled). Justfile script-naming bug fixed (build-rootfs-ubuntu-24.04.sh).

title: Decouple API availability from VM reconcile on restart
description:
On 'systemctl restart mjolnir', the startup VM reconcile resumes persisted VMs serially (~5s each: TAP create -> guest network -> PTY ready -> resumed). Bandit (the HTTP API on :4000) is the LAST child in Mjolnir.Supervisor, so the API is unavailable until the reconcile finishes. Observed during the 2026-06-23 deploy: 17 VMs => ~17s of API downtime ('connection refused' on :4000) even though 'systemctl is-active' reported active. This scales linearly with VM count: 100+ VMs would mean minutes of API downtime per restart/deploy.

Why it matters: deploys and crashes currently incur downtime proportional to fleet size. As VM count grows (and especially once 'mj deploy' makes long-lived service VMs common), restart-downtime becomes a real availability problem.
design:
Two candidate approaches (not mutually exclusive):
1. Start Bandit BEFORE the reconcile (or move reconcile out of the critical startup path into a background Task/GenServer), so the API serves immediately while VMs resume asynchronously. Tradeoff: API may briefly report VMs as not-yet-resumed; need to handle requests for in-flight VMs gracefully.
2. Parallelize the reconcile (Task.async_stream with bounded concurrency) so N VMs resume in roughly constant time instead of N*5s. Tradeoff: concurrent TAP/hypervisor setup load; cap concurrency.

Recommended: (1) for availability + (2) for total reconcile time. Verify by restarting with many VMs and timing first 200 from /api/health.
acceptance_criteria: API /api/health returns 200 within a few seconds of 'systemctl restart mjolnir' regardless of resumable VM count; VM resume continues in background without blocking the HTTP listener.

title: CLI surface: 'mjolnir publish ./dist' — plain verb, public by default, returns URL
description:
The user-facing publish command. Zero special vocabulary for the common case.

## Why (product principle from design session)
Newcomers must be able to make a static thing public, verifiably from their IdentiKey, WITHOUT memorizing terminology. The verb is 'publish'; verifiability is automatic; recipients/keyspace are progressive-disclosure flags. No Norse codenames in the surface.

## Surface
  mjolnir publish ./dist                  # public by default → prints https://<iroh_id>.vm... + 'signed by <fp>'
  mjolnir publish ./dist --to alice,bob   # gated/recipients
  mjolnir publish ./dist --keyspace team  # group
Only words a newcomer meets: publish, public, recipients, your IdentiKey, a URL.

## Tasks
- Drive Publisher.build_snapshot + publish protocol from the CLI (mjolnir escript / forge-style subcommand).
- Public default; emit the resulting URL + signing fingerprint.
- Wire --to / --keyspace to the keyspace seam.

## Acceptance
- 'mjolnir publish ./dist' on a fresh dir yields a working public URL signed by the user's IdentiKey, with no other flags or jargon required.

Depends on storage + crypto + transport seams.
design: DE-SCOPED by scout: a publish CLI already exists — lib/mix/tasks/mjolnir.sites.publish.ex (Mix.Task, OptionParser, calls Publisher.publish/5) + mjolnir.sites.alias.ex + HTTP router lib/mjolnir/api/sites_router.ex (POST /:fp/:name/snapshot, /head). .6 is now: add lib/mix/tasks/mjolnir.publish.ex mirroring sites.publish.ex but PUBLIC-BY-DEFAULT with friendly output (print URL + signing fingerprint); flags positional dir, --public default | --to | --keyspace. Reuse Publisher.build_snapshot/4 + publish/5. WAIT for .3 to settle publisher.ex signing signature before wiring.
notes: CODE COMPLETE (cannot close: beads blocks on open .1/.4). lib/mix/tasks/mjolnir.publish.ex + test (6 pass). Public-by-default, auto-creates IdentiKey at ~/.config/mjolnir/identikey.json on first run, signs via .3, prints URL+fingerprint. --to/--keyspace rejected with pointer to .5. Will close when .1/.4 close.

title: Keyspace/recipients seam: gated + group modes via identikey-storage-auth + recrypt PRE
description:
Wire the non-public disclosure modes so 'publish --to <recipients>' and 'publish --keyspace <id>' are real, using recrypt's existing primitives.

## Why
This is the architectural payoff: public/gated/group differ ONLY by key disclosure. recrypt already implements keyspaces (identikey-storage-auth: keyspace.rs, capability.rs, grant.rs) and post-quantum proxy recryption (recrypt-core).

## Tasks
- Gated (recipients): encrypt to recipient IdentiKey PRE pubkey(s); per-file wrapped_key in manifest; serve ciphertext+outboard to authenticated caller (Iroh node-id → IdentiKey binding, or capability).
- Group (keyspace): associate site with a recrypt keyspace; server holds per-member recryption keys; recrypt wrapped_key on each authenticated read; atomic revocation by deleting the rk.
- Map CLI flags --to / --keyspace onto these.

## Acceptance
- A recipient can decrypt; a non-recipient cannot.
- Revoking a keyspace member blocks their next read.
- Server never sees plaintext or owner secret in gated/group.

Depends on storage + crypto seams.

title: Transport seam: real Iroh endpoint binding in Sites.Endpoints (reuse VM Iroh path)
description:
Make Sites.Endpoints (lib/mjolnir/sites/endpoints.ex — currently a scaffold tracking intended bindings in memory) actually bind an Iroh endpoint per (identikey_fp, site_name), reusing the existing VM Iroh endpoint code path.

## Why
'Get an Iroh address' is step one of the user story. Without a real bind there is no address to publish to. Gateway already resolves <iroh_id>.vm.worldtree.network — this is the missing host-side listener.

## Tasks
- Bind stable Iroh endpoint per site (explicit registration per design §11 decision 1).
- On dial: resolve endpoint → identikey_fp/site → HEAD → serve via Sites.Server.serve/3.
- Confirm gateway round-trips HTTP-over-Iroh to the bound endpoint.

## Acceptance
- A published site is reachable at https://<iroh_id>.vm.worldtree.network.
- Endpoint survives restart (binding persisted as signed record).
design: Scout map (full: scratchpad/scout-map-transport-cli.md). Host-side Iroh bind does NOT exist yet — only guest agent (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/iroh.rs run_iroh_server) and gateway (native/mjolnir_gateway) speak Iroh. Sites endpoints.ex:32-35 bind/2 is a stub. Real bind needs a HOST Rust Iroh binding (NIF/sidecar) — same integration decision as .1, so genuinely blocked on .1. Use identikey_fp+site_name as ALPN/routing key.

title: Crypto seam: real MultiSig signing of manifest + HEAD via IdentiKey (replace <<>> stubs)
description:
Replace placeholder signatures (Manifest signatures: <<>>, HeadRecord signature: <<>> — see publisher.ex 'Signatures (Phase 1 stub)') with real signing, and verify on accept.

## Why
The signature IS the 'verifiably from your IdentiKey' value prop. Without it the whole pitch is hollow. Identikey module (lib/mjolnir/sites/identikey.ex) already does ED25519; ML-DSA-87 leg comes from recrypt.

## Tasks
- Sign canonical manifest body + canonical HEAD record body with IdentiKey ED25519 now.
- Verify signature on manifest accept + HEAD update (reject bad sigs; today server would serve unsigned).
- Wire decrypt_public/3 seam (server.ex STUBBED decryption) to real HKDF-derive + XChaCha20.
- Layer ML-DSA-87 (dual-stack MultiSig) once recrypt signing path is reachable — can be a follow-up.

## Acceptance
- Publish produces a signed manifest + signed HEAD.
- Tampered manifest/HEAD is rejected.
- Public-mode serve decrypts real bytes end-to-end (no stub).
close_reason: Closed

title: B2 durability: local hot tier + write-through to Backblaze B2 via recrypt-storage S3
description:
Guarantee the invariant: every published chunk + manifest eventually lands in Backblaze B2 (durable offsite).

## Why
User requirement: 'everything eventually backed up into Backblaze.' B2 is S3-compatible; recrypt-storage's S3 backend already points at custom endpoints (endpoint_url + force_path_style, see its minio() ctor) — B2 is a config change, not new code.

## Decide
Tiered store shape: (a) local FS/BTRFS hot read tier + write-through to B2 directly, or (b) Minio local cache replicating to B2 (matches Duke's prior setup, location currently unknown). Lean (a) — fewer moving parts; Minio only if a local S3 API is independently needed.

## Tasks
- Add B2 credentials/endpoint config (runtime.exs env: B2 key id/app key/endpoint/bucket).
- Write-through or async-replicate chunks+manifests to B2 on publish.
- Reconcile/audit job: confirm every live manifest's chunks exist in B2.

## Acceptance
- A published site's chunks are verifiably present in B2.
- Serve path still reads from local hot tier (B2 is backing, not hot).
notes: DEPLOY STEP (after just deploy): install scripts/backup-sites-b2.sh -> /usr/local/bin/ (chmod +x); cp scripts/systemd/mjolnir-sites-backup.{service,timer} -> /etc/systemd/system/; systemctl daemon-reload; systemctl enable --now mjolnir-sites-backup.timer. Verify: systemctl list-timers | grep sites; /usr/local/bin/backup-sites-b2.sh --dry-run.

title: Investigate PTY-based exec for CI steps (replace vsock request-response)
description:
Current CI exec uses vsock request-response: send command, block until complete, receive full stdout as one blob. This causes problems for long-running builds:

1. **Output buffering**: stdout is returned as a single string after command finishes. With tail -c 50KB truncation to avoid 64KB vsock frame limit, we lose most build output. No real-time streaming to Forgejo logs.

2. **Connection fragility**: during a 45s+ cargo build, the vsock connection appears idle (no data flowing). OOM kills or any guest agent issue drops the connection, losing the entire exec result with no partial output.

3. **Timeout complexity**: GenServer.call with :infinity timeout works but masks connection drops. A PTY channel would detect disconnects immediately.

4. **No interactivity**: can't ctrl-c a hung build, can't stream progress bars, can't tail logs in real-time.

Mjolnir already supports PTY channels (vsock channels 1-255 for binary streams). The guest agent has PtyOpen/PtyResize/PtyClose handling with full terminal multiplexing. The runner could:

- Open a PTY channel per step via POST /api/vms/:id/pty
- Send the command as input to the PTY
- Stream output in real-time over the binary channel
- Detect exit via shell prompt or exit code sentinel
- Forward each line to Forgejo's UpdateLog RPC as it arrives

This would also enable the syslog-based log streaming we designed (Mjolnir.Syslog.Listener routing to EventBus) to complement PTY output for background processes.

Alternatively, add a streaming exec endpoint to the Mjolnir API (SSE or chunked HTTP) that wraps the vsock exec with progressive output forwarding, avoiding the frame size limit entirely.

Ref: vsock connection drop during cargo build (session 2026-06-08), Vsock.Connection.exec timeout, PTY support in guest agent (src/pty.rs).

title: Support Node.js actions (actions/checkout, etc.) in VM executor
description: The VM executor can run shell steps (run:) but fails on JavaScript actions (uses: actions/checkout@v4). The runner clones the action on the host, copies it into the VM via Copy(), then tries to execute 'node dist/index.js' inside the VM. Failure mode: the action directory gets copied but node execution fails (likely path/permission issue in Copy or missing node_modules). Fix: (1) Ensure Copy() correctly transfers the full action directory tree into the VM, (2) Verify node is at expected path in CI image, (3) Test with actions/checkout which is the most common JS action. Current workaround: replace 'uses: actions/checkout@v4' with 'run: git clone http://10.255.255.1:3000/owner/repo.git . --branch $FORGEJO_REF_NAME --depth 1'. Ref: run 22 log shows 'executing remote job container: [node .../dist/index.js]' then immediate failure.
notes: Progress: CopyDir works (116 files via host rootfs), env vars sourced from /.forgejo/.env.sh, invalid var names (hyphens) skipped, workspace path dedoubled (GetRoot=/). Node.js actions now execute (exit changed 2→1). Remaining: checkout action exits 1 with no stdout captured. Likely needs: (1) pre-create GITHUB_WORKSPACE dir, (2) create GITHUB_EVENT_PATH file, (3) debug why action stdout isn't captured (guest agent may not pipe subprocess stdout). Remove debug logging before closing.
close_reason: actions/checkout@v4 works in Mjolnir VMs. Fixes: CopyDir via host rootfs, env vars via .env.sh file, workspace dir pre-creation, event.json creation, exit code wrapping for stdout capture, skip invalid shell var names (hyphens). Job succeeded with full repo checkout.

title: VM metadata tags for CI correlation
description: When the Go executor spawns a VM via POST /api/vms, include metadata tags: {purpose: ci, job_id, repo, run_id}. Elixir VM module stores tags in state, exposes via VM.list/0 filtering. Enables: resource accounting (max N CI VMs), preemption policy (interactive > CI), observability (correlate EventBus events to CI jobs). Small change: add optional 'tags' map to spawn opts, store in VM struct, expose in API responses.
notes:
SUBSTRATE HALF DONE by mjolnir-oux (commit 81d713b, 2026-08-07): VMs now carry an opaque string=>string `metadata` map, set at spawn via POST /api/vms {"metadata": {...}}, persisted on the StateStore record, filterable via GET /api/vms?metadata.k=v and `mj list --filter k=v`. Survives reboot/resume (put/1 carries it forward). Bounded + control-char-free at the API boundary. Records also carry a monotonic generation for compare-and-delete fencing (If-Match on DELETE). See docs/vm-metadata-and-generations.md.

REMAINING for this issue: the Go forgejo-runner executor must actually SEND {purpose: ci, job_id, repo, run_id} when it spawns a VM, and whatever consumes it (resource accounting / preemption policy / EventBus correlation) must read it back. The substrate no longer blocks any of that.
close_reason: Remaining half done: the Go executor now sends metadata on spawn (identikey/forgejo-runner eb5d41e5, built and live). SpawnConfig gained a Metadata map; run_context.go populates {purpose: ci, repo, run_id, run_number, job, workflow} from the job's github context, skipping empty values. Verified end-to-end on run 15: the runner-spawned VM carried {job: build, purpose: ci, repo: identikey/mjolnir, run_id: 61, run_number: 15, workflow: Build mj client} and GET /api/vms?metadata.purpose=ci matched it alone. Also confirmed the API accepts the exact shape (well inside the 32-key/512-byte limits) and that metadata is NOT what made run 14 fail — that was mjolnir-pry. Unblocks mjolnir-urp (lease-based reaping needs this ownership handle) and mjolnir-5xn.

title: bootstrap-adjuncts.sh: optional service installer
description: Create scripts/bootstrap-adjuncts.sh for installing optional Mjolnir services on a server where the core bootstrap has already run. Flags: --postgres (apt install, mjolnir_pg user, pg_enabled config), --forgejo (binary install, app.ini, sqlite, admin user, systemd), --runner (Go toolchain, clone upstream runner, apply patches, build, register with Forgejo, systemd), --ci-image (build CI base image via build-ci-image.sh), --all (everything). Each section is idempotent. Forgejo must be running before runner registration. Add corresponding Justfile recipe: just bootstrap-adjuncts [flags]. Ref: docs/plans/forgejo-runner.md
notes:
STALE IN PARTS as of 2026-08-12 — re-scope before building:

- The --runner section as written ('clone upstream runner, apply patches') describes the approach mjolnir-400 REPLACED. There is no patching any more: deploy.sh --runner clones the FORK (identikey/forgejo-runner, branch mjolnir) at /opt/forgejo-runner-build and builds it. The in-repo mirror native/forgejo-runner/ that the old flow implied was deleted in mjolnir-6vm. Any adjuncts script must clone the fork, not patch upstream.
- --ci-image is already covered by 'just build-ci-image' -> scripts/build-ci-image.sh, which as of 2026-08-12 is reproducible end to end (guest agent baked in per mjolnir-0e8, mise + rust/zig per mjolnir-xx5, tmux added for CI). A wrapper flag is fine, but the work is done.
- --postgres overlaps mjolnir-o9k, which puts postgres install + mjolnir_pg user + dirs into the CORE host bootstrap rather than an adjuncts script. Decide which owns it; doing both invites drift. o9k is the narrower, already-scoped one.
- --forgejo is the only section with no existing home.

Also worth deciding before writing it: whether an 'adjuncts' script is the right shape at all now that the core bootstrap is growing these responsibilities anyway. This issue predates that drift.

title: Host bootstrap: install postgres binaries + mjolnir_pg user
description: Update scripts/bootstrap-host-ubuntu.sh and bootstrap-host-arch.sh to: (1) install postgres 15+ client/server binaries (NOT the systemd unit — mjolnir manages lifecycle), (2) create system user mjolnir_pg with no login shell, (3) chown /var/lib/mjolnir/pg and /var/run/mjolnir to mjolnir_pg. Required for prod deploy of the OTP-managed postgres sidecar.
close_reason:
Fixed in ae20e69. Both bootstrap-host-ubuntu.sh and bootstrap-host-arch.sh now install postgres server+client, create the mjolnir_pg system user (no login shell, idempotent), and create+chown /var/lib/mjolnir/pg (0700), /var/run/mjolnir (0750) and /var/log/mjolnir/pg. The distro cluster is stopped, disabled and masked — Ubuntu's postinst auto-starts one, and a second postgres beside Mjolnir's data dir is a conflicting process, not just waste.

Also closes a gap the issue did not name: config.ex defaults pg_bin_dir to /usr/bin, which is WRONG on Ubuntu (server binaries live in /usr/lib/postgresql/<major>/bin; only client tools are linked into /usr/bin). Prod worked solely because MJOLNIR_PG_BIN_DIR was hand-written into /etc/mjolnir/env. The script now discovers the highest installed major and writes that var — the channel config/runtime.exs already reads, so this closes a half-wired loop rather than adding a mechanism.

Verified without running either script: bash -n clean on both; discovery against the live host yields /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin, identical to the hand-written value and to the running process's path; version discovery picks 16 over 14 and 9.6; the env rewrite is idempotent across re-runs and slash-safe. shellcheck reports no new warnings.

The agent's /var/run-is-tmpfs warning was investigated and is a NON-issue: Mjolnir.Postgres.Server.ensure_dirs/1 (server.ex:167-177) mkdir_p's all three dirs on every start and chowns them to pg_run_as, so the socket dir is rebuilt with correct ownership before postgres spawns. The misleading comment was corrected rather than filed as a bug.

title: add-base-image-pins: immutable pins + moving aliases
description: ADR 0009 D6. v0 in-place rebuild of ubuntu-24.04 is OK while we own every app. Before a second tenant: recipe writes @base/<alias>-<date> (pin, never overwritten), retargets alias ubuntu-24.04 / ubuntu-latest, spawn/deploy resolve alias→pin and record the pin on the VM/release and as deploy CacheKey parent. Redeploy keeps the pin unless --pull-base (bikeshed). node-latest is the alias pattern, not a Node OS-root (D1). Do not put pins only in @snapshots/ (mjolnir-97c). Leave mj bases room for kind/resolves_to. Not tonight.
acceptance_criteria:
- Recipe produces a new pin subvolume under @base/ and does not delete the previous pin
- Alias ubuntu-24.04 resolves to the new pin; mj spawn --base ubuntu-24.04 clones that pin
- mj deploy of an existing app without pull-base clones the recorded pin, not today's alias
- Deploy cache parent_layer_id is the pin name, not the alias string
- mj bases lists alias and pin separately (kind / resolves_to)

title: Admit seam between durable accept and thaw (future proxy reader)
description:
## Why

Keep durability (A) and wake-policy (B) as a structural split. Today Admit is a host predicate. A per-VM proxy, if ever built, is a mailbox READER after fsync, never the accept point.

## What

Explicit seam at the Admit call site. Optional. Depends on durable accept. Do not build the proxy VM.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Policy evaluator can sit between queued and thaw without changing 200 meaning
close_reason: Out of this epic. kick_consumer is the thaw seam; queued-but-don't-thaw is a later Admit change if needed

title: Reconcile LUKS tier: loopback-on-virtio-fs (shipped) vs virtio-blk (designed)
description:
Doc/implementation drift found while writing docs/plans/initiatives/multi-tenant-snapshots.md.

initramfs-verified-boot.md Layer 3 specifies tier 3 as a virtio-blk device so
dm-crypt operates on a real block device with no loopback indirection, and
explicitly argues this avoids virtiofsd's DAX-mapped shared memory region.

Shipped implementation is a LUKS loopback container on virtio-fs:
/var/lib/mjolnir/secrets.luks + losetup (guest_agent/src/secrets.rs:21, :519).

At-rest confidentiality still holds — the host sees only ciphertext in the
container file. But the documented rationale for virtio-blk is not being
honoured. Either reconcile the doc to the implementation (and re-examine whether
the DAX argument was overstated) or move the implementation to virtio-blk.

NB one incidental benefit of the current shape, relied on by the memory-snapshot
child of mjolnir-k8y: because the LUKS container is a loopback device and NOT
the root filesystem (root is virtio-fs), it can be luksSuspended without
deadlocking the guest. Moving to virtio-blk preserves this; moving tier 3 to
BE the root would not.

Adjacent to mjolnir-k8y, not blocking it.

title: The boot-agent bin target has not compiled for some time — vsock.rs references modules boot_main.rs never declares
description:
cargo check on native/mjolnir_guest_agent fails with E0432/E0433 for the second [[bin]] target, boot-agent:

  error[E0432]: unresolved import crate::tmux            vsock.rs:7
  error[E0433]: could not find syslog in the crate root  vsock.rs:523
  error[E0433]: could not find secrets in the crate root vsock.rs:711
  error[E0433]: could not find tmux in the crate root    vsock.rs:885

Cause: boot_main.rs declares only mod protocol, mod pty, mod vsock, while main.rs additionally declares agent, iroh, secrets, syslog, tmux. vsock.rs is shared by both bins and reaches for modules that exist in only one of them.

PRE-EXISTING, not from mjolnir-azm: boot_main.rs is untouched by that work and the mismatch is structural.

Nothing is broken in production because deploy never builds this target — it builds the main binary — and run_boot_listener/handle_boot_connection in vsock.rs are flagged dead code, so the boot agent's listener is not in use either.

THE REAL COST IS THE DIAGNOSTIC ONE: a bare 'cargo check' cannot be used as a green light on this crate, because it is red for reasons unrelated to whatever you just changed. That is how a broken check gets normalised. Verify with 'cargo check --bin mjolnir-agent --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl' until this is fixed.

FIX OPTIONS: either give boot_main.rs the missing mod declarations, or cfg-gate the shared regions of vsock.rs, or delete the boot-agent target if the initramfs boot agent is genuinely retired (check scripts/ and the initramfs build first — 'just build-boot-agent' exists).
acceptance_criteria: cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl exits 0 with no errors for all targets.
close_reason:
Not a broken crate — a wrong invocation. vsock.rs was already gated with #[cfg(feature = "full")]; the mjolnir-boot-agent bin simply had no required-features, so a default check (default = full) compiled boot_main.rs with full on and the full-only regions of the shared vsock.rs activated.

Fixed in 93b8d25: required-features = ["boot"] on the bin, plus a compile_error! in boot_main.rs under cfg(feature = "full") naming the correct command, because Cargo can demand a feature but cannot forbid one. Added 'just check-agent' to check both binaries with their own feature sets.

VERIFIED on the server: plain cargo check 0 errors (was 5); boot bin with --no-default-features --features boot 0 errors; boot bin with full on emits the guidance with the exact command.

title: Seed-dependent test pollution: a leaked :running StateStore record fails the empty-VM-list API tests
description:
Mjolnir.MCP.ServerTest 'GET /api/vms still returns 200' and Mjolnir.API.RouterTest 'GET /api/vms returns 200 with empty VM list' both assert body['vms'] == [], and both fail on some seeds because an earlier test left a :running StateStore record behind. The record surfaces as a stranded VM with state='recovering'.

Reproduced on seed 825279 (2 failures) and 309429 (2 failures); passes on 853672. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING: reproduced on a stashed tree with no local changes at seed 825279, so it is not from mjolnir-y32.

Observed leaked id was 'vm-3364', i.e. an id built as "vm-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}". Candidate writers use that shape: test/mjolnir/event_bus_test.exs, test/mjolnir/vm_exec_nonblocking_test.exs, test/mjolnir/health/busy_vm_test.exs.

Two things worth fixing:
1. Find the test that persists and does not clean up; delete the record in on_exit.
2. The assertion itself is fragile — an async test asserting on process-global StateStore contents will keep breaking. Prefer asserting the VM under test is absent over asserting the whole list is empty.

Precedent for the fix: test/mjolnir/vm_secrets_unlock_test.exs (added in mjolnir-y32) is async: false and deletes its records in on_exit for exactly this reason.
acceptance_criteria: mix test passes on seeds 825279, 309429 and 853672.
close_reason: Closed

title: A managed-secrets VM can be spawned with no owner and no provisioned secrets
description:
Found while fixing mjolnir-3v2, and deliberately NOT the cause of that issue's timeout (SecretEscrow.get_or_create/1 synthesizes a passphrase when no escrow exists, so a missing escrow never blocks).

Two related gaps in POST /api/vms (lib/mjolnir/api/router.ex ~line 240): the 'secrets' body param is optional even when secrets_mode == "managed", and nothing requires an owner. Production VM 2da0e442 is in exactly that state — spawn_config secrets_mode: "managed", owner_id: null, metadata: {} — which suggests it did not go through normal provisioning.

Whether that is a bug depends on intent: a managed VM with no entries is legitimate if the guest just wants an encrypted volume it will populate itself. A managed VM with no OWNER is harder to justify — ownership is what Authz.authorize_record/3 keys on, so an unowned VM is reachable only via the localhost bypass.

DECIDE: should secrets_mode: managed require (a) an owner, (b) at least one secrets entry, or (c) neither, with the current behaviour documented as intentional? Then enforce or document accordingly.

title: tmux pane-idle detection pattern-matches shell names; an unlisted shell breaks send_and_read
description:
send_and_read now gates sentinel matching on whether the pane looks idle (mjolnir-xrv) — necessary, because a lookalike and the real sentinel are textually identical as bare whole lines, and idleness is the only thing that separates them.

Idleness comes from tmux's #{pane_current_command} compared against a hardcoded list of shell names in is_idle_shell/1 (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/tmux.rs). If a pane's shell is not in that list, the pane NEVER looks idle, so send_and_read never accepts its sentinel and every call waits out its full timeout.

The failure direction is safe — a timeout is honest, a wrong exit code is not — but it is a real loss of function, and shared sessions are precisely where someone's login shell is not bash. The list was widened (dash, ash, busybox, fish, ksh, mksh, pdksh, tcsh, csh, elvish, nu, xonsh) but a hardcoded list of names cannot be right in general.

DURABLE FIX: ask tmux what the pane's OWN shell is rather than guessing from a name list — compare #{pane_current_command} against the pane's shell, so 'idle' means 'running nothing but its own shell' regardless of what that shell is called. Worth checking what tmux 3.4 actually exposes (#{pane_start_command}, or deriving from #{pane_pid}'s child processes) before committing to an approach.

Also note the two tmux invocations in capture_pane are not atomic; ordering was fixed so idleness is sampled BEFORE content (erring toward 'busy'), but a single atomic query would be better if tmux can provide one.

title: pg_bin_dir defaults to /usr/bin, which has no postgres on Debian/Ubuntu
description:
Split from mjolnir-o9k, whose bootstrap fix works around this rather than fixing it.

lib/mjolnir/postgres/config.ex:51 does get(:pg_bin_dir, "/usr/bin"). On Debian/Ubuntu that directory contains NO server binaries — postgres and initdb live in /usr/lib/postgresql/<major>/bin, and only client tools (psql, pg_dump) are linked into /usr/bin. So the compiled-in default cannot work on the distro Mjolnir actually runs on in production. It is correct on Arch, where pacman symlinks everything into /usr/bin.

Production is fine because /etc/mjolnir/env sets MJOLNIR_PG_BIN_DIR, and as of ae20e69 the host bootstrap writes that automatically. The default remains a trap for anyone running the release without a bootstrapped host — a manual install, a container, or a dev box — where it fails with a confusing missing-binary error pointing at a path that was never plausible.

OPTIONS (a decision, hence not done): (a) make the default OS-aware — glob /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin and take the highest, falling back to /usr/bin; (b) leave the default but fail at startup with a message naming the likely correct dir and MJOLNIR_PG_BIN_DIR; (c) leave as-is and treat the bootstrap as the only supported install path. (a) is the least surprising, but it puts platform detection in config resolution, which may not be where you want it.
close_reason: Fixed in ebafe6a. Took option (a), OS-aware detection. Confirmed the premise on 45.76.77.97: /usr/bin/postgres and /usr/bin/initdb do not exist; the server is at /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin, which is what MJOLNIR_PG_BIN_DIR already points to. Detection picks the highest-numbered /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin CONTAINING a postgres binary, else /usr/bin. Two traps handled: versions compare numerically (a string sort puts 9 above 16, wrong exactly on a host with both clusters), and a candidate must hold the server binary — postgresql-client-16 creates a version dir with only client tools. Explicit config always wins, so production behaviour is unchanged.

title: send_and_read can be fooled by a resolved-sentinel lookalike in the command's own output
description:
Found and reproduced while adding coverage for mjolnir-7hf. A failing test exists, marked #[ignore], at native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/tmux.rs (sentinel_discrimination_ignores_lookalike_resolved_shapes_in_own_output) — run with 'cargo test -p mjolnir-guest-agent --bin mjolnir-agent --features full -- --ignored' on a Linux host with tmux.

send_and_read appends 'echo __MJOLNIR_DONE_<id>_$?__' and polls capture_pane. It discriminates the ECHOED command line from the RESOLVED output line purely by shape: after the prefix, '$?__' means echoed, digits mean resolved (tmux.rs ~366-382). That is the ONLY check. Any text anywhere in the pane matching __MJOLNIR_DONE_<id>_<digits>__ ends the wait.

REPRODUCED (verified independently on root@45.76.77.97, tmux 3.4): a command printing a resolved-shaped lookalike with the real sentinel id, then sleeping 1s before truly finishing with exit 0:

    printf '%s999__\n' '__MJOLNIR_DONE_<id>_'; sleep 1; true

returns in ~318ms with exit_code Some(999) instead of Some(0). So the caller gets a WRONG exit code and truncated output, and the command is still running.

LIKELIHOOD is low — the id is unique per call, so this needs the command to emit that id, which it can only do by reading its own argv/history. It is not a plausible accident. It IS reachable deliberately, and it means a command's own output can control the reported exit status of the terminal_* API.

RELATED DEFECT, same lines: the finder matches by SUBSTRING (line.find(&sentinel_prefix), any column) but the exit-code parser then does sentinel_line.trim().strip_prefix(&sentinel_prefix) — a sentinel not at column 0 yields exit_code: None despite having matched.

FIX DIRECTION (a decision — do not implement blind): require the sentinel to be its own whole line (line.trim() == full sentinel) rather than a substring, which fixes both the lookalike and the finder/parser mismatch. Needs care: a prompt or partial redraw sharing the line would then stop matching, so verify against a real pane before changing behaviour.
close_reason:
Fixed in a862cc4. A match now requires the sentinel to be a WHOLE LINE and the pane to be IDLE. Whole-line alone was proved insufficient by dumping a real pane (tmux 3.4 on the server): the lookalike '__MJOLNIR_DONE_expid1_999__' and the true sentinel '__MJOLNIR_DONE_expid1_0__' are both bare whole lines, textually identical in shape. The discriminator is pane_current_command — 'sleep' while the lookalike prints, returning to a shell strictly after our appended echo runs. Finder and parser now share one parse_sentinel_line, closing the second defect where a sentinel matched at any column but only parsed at column 0 (exit_code: None).

TWO ISSUES I FOUND REVIEWING THE FIX, both fixed in the same commit: (1) capture_pane makes two non-atomic tmux calls and sampled content BEFORE idleness — a command finishing in between would let idleness vouch for stale content, precisely the race the gate closes. Idleness is now sampled first, erring toward 'busy' at a cost of one 250ms poll. (2) idleness pattern-matched bash/sh/zsh only; that was presentational before and harmless when wrong, but as a correctness gate an unlisted shell never looks idle and every send_and_read in that pane times out. Widened and pinned by a test, since shared sessions are exactly where a login shell is not bash. Name-matching still cannot be right in general — mjolnir-40c tracks the durable fix.

The previously-#[ignore]d reproduction now passes for the right reason: asserts exit 0 AND duration >= 900ms, so the ~320ms lookalike shortcut fails it. 24 tests pass on the server, run twice, no order-dependence, no leftover tmux sessions.

title: mj bases: no API endpoint lists base images
description:
Split out of mjolnir-97c, whose --base half is done. 'mj bases' cannot be implemented client-side: a route survey of lib/mjolnir/api/router.ex found /api/health, /api/vms*, /api/storage, /api/trash*, /api/snapshots*, /api/dormant, /api/deploy, /api/apps* — nothing enumerates @base/. Only POST /api/vms validates a base_image name (router.ex:85-93) for path traversal.

Needs a GET /api/base-images returning the @base/ subvolumes (name, size, created), mirroring how /api/snapshots exposes @snapshots/, then a thin 'mj bases' on top. Without it, discovering a valid --base value still means ssh + btrfs subvolume list.

title: No scriptable way to download a CI artifact; consider publishing to Releases
description:
Artifacts are only reachable through the Forgejo web UI (browser session). The REST artifacts API does not exist on Forgejo 15.0.0+gitea-1.22.0: /api/v1/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/artifacts and .../runs/{id}/artifacts both 404, while .../actions/tasks returns 200. Web routes reject a token (404 on a private repo, since Forgejo hides unauthorized private resources). Today the only non-browser path is reading the blob off disk at /var/lib/forgejo/data/actions_artifacts/<run>/<id>/*.chunk (a zip) — fine for verification, useless for 'curl the latest mj'.

Two ways forward, not mutually exclusive:
  a) Upgrade Forgejo and re-probe — UNVERIFIED that any current release adds these endpoints; check before planning around it.
  b) Publish to RELEASES instead. /repos/{o}/{r}/releases and .../assets DO exist on this version, giving a stable token-authenticated download URL. For a CLI binary people install this is the better artifact anyway: durable, versioned, and not tied to a run that ages out (artifacts default to 90-day retention).

Recommend (b) on a tag, keeping the per-run artifact for debugging.

title: Forgejo CI: publish mj binaries as artifacts/releases
description: build-client.yml currently only sha256sums the binary. Forgejo has no [actions] section in app.ini so defaults apply and artifact-API support for actions/upload-artifact is unverified. Confirm which version works (v3 vs v4) against Forgejo 15.0.0+gitea-1.22.0, then attach mj builds so they are downloadable rather than rebuilt.
close_reason: CI delivers the binary. Run 9 (commit 6170ee9) published artifact 'mj-x86_64-linux', 11,865,329 bytes, Artifact ID 3. Verified by extracting the stored blob: sha256 53e03ec3e25e716eab61a4e0b1826e71fc8c645f3a64b49923b2a3e8ebc140dd — byte-identical to the sha256sum printed inside the build VM — ELF 64-bit x86-64, and './mjolnir --version' runs. Required forgejo/upload-artifact@v4 (upstream refuses non-github.com hosts) plus fixes mjolnir-176 and mjolnir-7c4.

title: send_and_read assumes the shared pane is at a shell prompt
description:
tmux::send_and_read builds 'CMD; echo __MJOLNIR_DONE_<uuid>_$?__' and types it into the pane with send-keys -l, then waits for the sentinel. That only works if the pane is sitting at a shell prompt.

The premise of the terminal_* family is that a human and an agent share one tmux session. So the pane may well be inside vim, less, a REPL, or a running foreground process when the agent sends. Then:
- The text is typed into THAT program, not a shell. In vim, an unlucky prefix is interpreted as editor commands.
- No sentinel ever appears, so the call burns its full timeout_ms and returns timed_out:true with whatever the pane happens to show.
- Whatever got typed stays in the human's terminal.

Related pollution: on timeout the command is left RUNNING, so its sentinel surfaces in the pane later and the human sees raw __MJOLNIR_DONE_<uuid>_0__ text.

Options: probe the pane's running command before sending (capture_pane already returns running_command — currently discarded at every call site via '(content, _, _, _)'), and refuse or warn when it is not a shell. Cheaper stopgap: document the precondition on the endpoint and the MCP tool description so an agent knows to check terminal_read first.

Not urgent — needs a human and an agent actively sharing a pane — but it is the failure mode the shared-session design makes most likely, and it is untested (mjolnir-7hf).

title: Fold terminal/open into send and read via ensure_session
description:
ensure_session is called from exactly one place — VsockRequest::TerminalOpen (vsock.rs:1018). TerminalSend and TerminalRead do not auto-create, so POST /api/vms/:id/terminal/open is mandatory before any other terminal_* call works. The endpoint is load-bearing by omission rather than by design, and it costs every agent interaction an extra round trip.

The PTY path already solved this ten lines away: tmux::attach_argv uses 'new-session -A -s', idempotent create-or-attach, which is exactly why several PTY clients converge on one terminal. Same tmux primitive, two different philosophies in one codebase.

Change: have TerminalSend / TerminalRead / TerminalSendAndRead call ensure_session first, making them idempotent create-or-use. Then POST /terminal/open (and the open_terminal MCP tool) become optional convenience rather than a required handshake — keep them for explicit lifecycle, or deprecate.

DO THIS AFTER mjolnir-7hf. This refactors a public, MCP-exposed API that currently has zero tests; the safety net should exist first.

title: mj connect exits 1 with 'connection lost' on a clean shell exit
description:
Typing 'exit' in an mj connect session (or detaching from tmux) ends with 'Connection error: connection lost' and exit code 1 instead of a clean exit code 0.

Pre-existing, NOT introduced by mjolnir-690: reproduced with the OLD pre-change mj binary on the unmodified sessionless v1 Iroh path against a new agent.

Likely the agent's Frame::Exit races the QUIC connection teardown, so the client sees the stream drop before it reads the Exit frame. Worth confirming whether the agent sends Exit at all when the PTY child reaps.

Impact: scripts wrapping mj connect cannot distinguish a normal shell exit from a real connection failure.
design:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED 2026-08-12 (code-level, incl. reading vendored quinn-0.11.11 / iroh-1.0.0 sources on the server; no live repro needed).

1. The agent DOES send Frame::Exit. Both detection paths in handle_shell_connection (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/iroh.rs) do it: PTY read returns Ok(0) at 279-285 -> wait_exit_code() then write_frame(Exit) at 283; and WouldBlock + try_wait() showing the child gone at 286-292 -> write_frame(Exit) at 290. The issue's open question ('does it send Exit at all?') is answered: yes, unconditionally.

2. Nothing waits for delivery. After the break, the fn returns Ok(()) at iroh.rs:304. conn/send/recv are locals moved in at iroh.rs:141 and are dropped immediately, with NO await between the Exit write and the drop. quinn's write_all only guarantees bytes reached the local send buffer, not the wire (send_stream.rs:70-77). Dropping the last ConnectionRef calls implicit_close (connection.rs:929-945 -> 1238-1240), an immediate local close. So whether the queued Exit bytes make it out before teardown is a scheduling race against the QUIC driver task — which is why this is intermittent, not deterministic.

3. Client side: run_shell_loop (native/mjolnir_client/src/connect.rs:250-271) read_frame fails with quinn ReadError::ConnectionLost, whose Display is literally 'connection lost' (recv_stream.rs:546-549 — the only occurrence of that string in the entire dependency tree). It propagates via connect.rs:268-269 to connect_to_vm's match at connect.rs:232-235, which prints 'Connection error: {e}' and std::process::exit(1). A clean exit and a genuine transport failure are indistinguishable there: Frame::Exit is the ONLY graceful-exit signal, and it is exactly what the race drops.

MINIMAL FIX (agent-side, where the bug is): after write_frame(Exit) at BOTH call sites, call send.finish() and then await delivery — e.g. send.stopped() — bounded by a short timeout, before returning and letting conn drop.

DECISIONS NEEDED before implementing: (a) the stopped() timeout, so a client that never acks (already killed) cannot hang the agent's handler task; (b) whether handle_tcp_forward (iroh.rs:330, which calls finish() but likewise never awaits it) gets the same treatment; (c) whether the CLIENT should additionally treat ApplicationClosed(0) right after an established session as clean exit 0 — belt-and-braces, but too loose a version would mask genuine failures, so it must distinguish 'never spoke to the agent' from 'spoke, shell was running, then it vanished'.

title: Add a virtio-rng device to the CH config
description:
Mjolnir.CloudHypervisor.Config emits NO rng device — grep -i rng finds nothing. The guest kernel DOES carry the virtio_rng driver, so the device is simply absent from vm.create.

Prerequisite for any resume-time reseed (mjolnir-3y6.5). Also worth having on its own merits: a VM with no entropy source stalls on first use of blocking randomness.

Note this does NOT by itself force a reseed on resume — it only makes entropy available.
acceptance_criteria: vm.create includes an rng device; the guest shows a virtio-rng hwrng source; no regression in boot time.
notes: CORRECTION: a virtio-rng device DOES exist. Mjolnir.CloudHypervisor.Config never emits one, but CH adds a default — vm.info shows rng: {src: /dev/urandom} and the guest reports virtio_rng.0 as its hw_random source. So there IS an entropy source to reseed from and this bead is much smaller than filed: it is about making the device EXPLICIT in Config rather than relying on a CH default that could change across the v52 upgrade.
close_reason: Done as the prerequisite for mjolnir-3y6.5 (c30f25d). Config.rng_config/1 emits {"src": "/dev/urandom"} in the vm.create payload; every VM previously booted with no RNG device at all despite the guest kernel having the virtio_rng driver. /dev/urandom rather than /dev/random on the HOST side deliberately — host urandom is already CSPRNG-seeded and never blocks, so /dev/random there would stall VM boot on a freshly-booted host for no gain. Note this does NOT by itself fix snapshot cloning: it supplies entropy but does not force a reseed at any moment. That is Mjolnir.Entropy.

title: Spike: validate CDN (Bunny) edge before adopting — HTTP/1.1-origin pull + traffic geo
description:
Prereqs before pulling the CDN lever from ADR 0001 (docs/decisions/0001-edge-strategy.md). Do NOT adopt a CDN until these resolve:
1. Live test Bunny.net HTTP/1.1-origin pull against mjolnir-gateway (architecturally near-certain per research, but undocumented — verify a pull zone caches immutable _app/immutable/* correctly and passes SSR HTML through, with BYO/origin-LE cert).
2. Measure real traffic geography + asset:SSR byte ratio to size the win and monthly cost (research assumed ~90% cacheable, NA/EU, ~100KB objects — confirm for our actual traffic).
3. Design a CDN-purge-on-publish hook for Sites HEAD updates (so cache invalidation is correct when a site republishes).
Decision context: reject gateway-rewrite (option C); Bunny is sanctioned low-lock-in choice when a trigger justifies it; steer static assets to IdentiKey Sites (option B). See ADR 0001.

title: Research/impl: self-hosted Iroh relay for multi-host cloud
description:
Today both the guest agent (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/iroh.rs) and the gateway use iroh::endpoint::presets::N0 — number0's PUBLIC relay network — for connection rendezvous + NAT-traversal fallback. The gateway↔co-located-VM cold-start (~7s) is being fixed by local TCP routing (epic mjolnir-l79), which removes Iroh from the co-located path entirely, so a self-hosted relay buys NOTHING for the single-host case (direct beats even a LAN-local relay).

Self-hosted relay becomes valuable ONLY once we run a multi-host cloud:
- Faster cross-host connection establishment (relay RTT drops from public-internet to our own regional/backbone).
- No hard dependency on number0's relay infra (reliability, privacy, control).
- Enables the 'any local Mjolnir VM routes globally without Tailscale' vision on our own rendezvous.
- Pair it with Iroh direct-address hints (connection_info/1 already returns IP hints, not just relay URLs) so cross-host dials skip the relay when a direct path exists.

Scope when picked up:
- Stand up iroh-relay (DERP-like) on our host(s); configure guest + gateway endpoints to use it (relay map / custom preset) instead of / in addition to N0.
- Decide relay placement/topology for the fleet; health + failover to N0.
- Measure cross-host cold-connect latency vs N0 baseline.

GATED ON multi-host. Not actionable while single-host. See docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md (self-hosted-relay analysis) and docs/forge-architecture.md (multi-host direction).

title: Self-hosted Iroh relay for multi-host cloud
description:
Once Mjolnir spans multiple hosts, stand up our own Iroh relay instead of relying on number0's public relays (iroh::endpoint::presets::N0). 

WHY (from gateway local-routing investigation, docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md): the ~7s zine cold-start was Iroh global-overlay connection setup (relay rendezvous + hole-punch) to a CO-LOCATED VM. That specific case is now fixed by direct local TCP routing (epic mjolnir-l79) — Iroh is removed from the co-located hot path. So a self-hosted relay does NOT help the single-host case and is explicitly NOT needed now.

It becomes valuable in the MULTI-HOST future:
- Faster cross-host connection establishment (relay RTT drops from internet-scale to our own regional/LAN relay).
- No dependency on number0's public relay infra (reliability, privacy, control, no rate limits).
- Enables 'any local Mjolnir VM routes globally without Tailscale' (the hole-punch/discovery rendezvous is ours).

Pair with: injecting direct socket-address hints into the Iroh EndpointAddr (connection_info/1 already returns IP hints, not just relay URLs) so cross-host dials that CAN go direct skip the relay entirely. The relay is the fallback for NAT-blocked paths.

Scope when picked up: deploy iroh-relay binary (host config via Forge systemd_unit), point guest+gateway endpoints at our relay (replace/augment presets::N0), TLS/domain for the relay, health monitoring. Blocked on multi-host cluster layer (roadmap: 'Multi-node cluster').

Not a priority until multi-host lands.

title: Gateway: local-route dial failure falls back to Iroh alias (self-healing)
description:
Phase 3 of gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md). Make a stale local [[route]] non-fatal and establish the multi-host seam (local-first, Iroh-for-remote).

Today (main.rs:868-881) a Disposition::Local dial failure returns 502 — it does NOT try Iroh. Goal: if the local backend is unreachable AND an Iroh alias exists for the same (apex, subdomain), fall back to handle_iroh_connection.

DESIGN WRINKLE found in live validation: the config loader DROPS an alias that is shadowed by a route (logs config.alias_shadowed_by_route; alias_count→0). So there is no alias left in the RouteTable to fall back to. This is therefore primarily a LOADER change, not just a handler change:
- Retain shadowed aliases in a side map (apex,subdomain)→Alias instead of dropping them, OR
- Let a [[route]] carry an optional fallback node z32.
Then in handle_connection, on Local dial failure, look up the retained alias and call handle_iroh_connection; only 502 if no fallback exists.
Multi-host relevance: the generator writes local routes only for VMs on this host; VMs elsewhere stay aliases; this failover covers VM migration and the moment a route goes stale before regeneration. Pairs with Phase 2.
Acceptance: kill the app VM's :3000, request still succeeds via Iroh (logs route=local then fallback=iroh); with no alias, returns 502 as today.
close_reason: Duplicate of mjolnir-l79.2/.3/.4 (existing epic). Findings folded into those.

title: Research: VM TAP IP hash collisions at scale (Network.allocate_ip)
description:
Network.allocate_ip/1 (lib/mjolnir/network.ex:149-179) derives a VM's TAP IP from SHA256(vm_id) into the 10.200.0.0/10 range (~4M usable addrs), avoiding .0/.255 last octet. It is deterministic (good: stable across restart/restore) but does NOT check for collisions — two distinct vm_ids can hash to the same IP. At current scale (handful of VMs) the birthday-bound collision probability is negligible, so this is NOT urgent. File for when we scale.

Scope of research:
- Quantify collision probability vs concurrent-VM count (birthday problem over the usable address space).
- Decide mitigation: (a) collision detection + linear probe / rehash on allocate, (b) registry-backed IP leasing instead of pure hashing, (c) widen range / restructure subnetting, (d) per-host IP namespaces once multi-host lands.
- Consider interaction with gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md): if a generated [[route]] points at a colliding/stale IP, the Iroh-alias fallback (Phase 3) should cover it, but routing correctness still needs a unique IP.
- Note multi-host: deterministic-from-vm_id is attractive for stateless routing, but collisions become more likely and cross-host IP reuse needs thought.

Not a priority right now — /10 is generous. Revisit at ~thousands of concurrent VMs/host or when multi-host routing is designed.

title: Host: forgejo binds 0.0.0.0:3000 — restrict to 127.0.0.1
description: forgejo listens on 0.0.0.0:3000 (all host interfaces incl. TAP networks) though the gateway only proxies to it via mimir.worldtree.network -> 127.0.0.1:3000. Bind 127.0.0.1:3000 to shrink reachable surface. Not internet-exposed (INPUT DROP) but reachable from VM TAP subnets. Minor hardening, surfaced during VM port-exposure investigation.

title: Bind host forgejo to 127.0.0.1:3000 instead of 0.0.0.0:3000
description: The host's forgejo service binds 0.0.0.0:3000 (all interfaces), but the web gateway only ever proxies to it via mimir.worldtree.network → 127.0.0.1:3000. Because it listens on all interfaces, forgejo:3000 is currently reachable from the VM TAP networks (10.0.0.0/8) as well, which is unnecessary attack surface. Rebinding to 127.0.0.1:3000 shrinks its reachable surface to just the gateway's loopback proxy path. This is a host-service config tweak (forgejo app.ini HTTP_ADDR / listen address), not a Mjolnir VM change. Surfaced during a listener/port scan of the host.
notes:
Investigated on host (45.76.77.97). NOT actioned — premise was incorrect. Findings:
1. UFW is active with INPUT policy DROP. The only allow rule for :3000 is '10.0.0.0/8 -> 10.255.255.1:3000' (# VMs to Forgejo). There is NO rule permitting the public interface 45.76.77.97:3000, so despite the 0.0.0.0 bind the public exposure is already firewalled off at the packet layer.
2. TAP reachability is REQUIRED, not surplus: the forgejo-runner registered its instance address as http://10.255.255.1:3000, and CI jobs inside VMs reach forgejo over the TAP gateway IP for git checkout. Binding 127.0.0.1 would break Actions.
3. HTTP_ADDR takes a single address, so it cannot serve both loopback (gateway proxy, gateway.toml backend=127.0.0.1:3000) and 10.255.255.1 (VM jobs) at once. The only defense-in-depth variant (bind 10.255.255.1 + repoint gateway) was considered and declined as not worth the restart/coupling given UFW already covers the public surface.
Conclusion: current posture (0.0.0.0 bind + UFW default-deny + single VM-subnet allow) is acceptable. Closing as already-mitigated.
close_reason: Closed

title: Parallel track — Recrypt integration: host a recryption proxy, map keyspace to VM keypair, build guest recrypt-client
description: End-state secrets transport, replacing P1.5's re-inject. Host a recryption proxy on Mjolnir (recrypt engine at ~/work/IdentiKey/recrypt: lattice PRE via OpenFHE + classical EC, KEM-DEM, Gordian Envelope, multi-sig auth — transforms ciphertext-for-owner into ciphertext-for-VM without decrypting). Map a keyspace to the VM's OWN keypair; recrypt the secret bundle to the VM key on wake; the guest decrypts in RAM with a key only it holds. Host/proxy never see plaintext; revocation = drop the re-encryption key; and the persistent LUKS volume can go away ENTIRELY — removing the dormancy refusal at its root. Build the guest-side recrypt-client (currently a stub).
notes: Its own initiative; NOT gated on P0–P3. Engine substantially built and under active hardening; greenfield work is the Mjolnir integration (proxy hosting + keyspace→VM-key mapping + guest client).

title: P3 — Operability: layer GC/prune (qgroup metering), health-gated releases, multi-process apps
description: (1) Layer GC/prune: meter EXCLUSIVE bytes via BTRFS qgroups (not du — reflink layers share blocks, du double-counts). Two GC classes: cache layers (LRU-evict freely under pressure, light/no billing) vs release layers (never auto-deleted, user prunes via mj deploy prune --keep N, billed). Bake owner_id + qgroup attribution into the layer schema from day one — retrofitting onto already-shared snapshots is painful. (2) Health-gated releases: probe GET / (or configured healthcheck) in the new VM before flipping the URL; enables rollback-on-failure. (3) Multi-process apps (Procfile web+worker): start with one VM, multiple systemd units.
notes: Don't ship P1 broadly without at least prune — snapshot sprawl fills disk. mise/npm egress depends on host NAT being bootstrapped (it is today) — document as prerequisite.

title: P2 — Run-state via Forge-over-vsock: replace ad-hoc systemd-by-exec with real Forge reconciliation + drift detection
description: Replace the P0/P1 ad-hoc 'write the systemd unit via VM.exec' with real Mjolnir.Forge reconciliation of the guest run-state (systemd_unit / file / user) driven over the guest agent's vsock exec transport (a cleaner transport than the currently-stubbed SSH one). Gives drift detection for free: 'someone SSH'd in and edited the unit' becomes detectable and re-convergeable — a property a shell-script deploy can never offer. Forge is a SECOND consumer of the same resource library, against guest targets; the host-self-config use case is unchanged.
design: De-risk with a spike before committing: concrete shape of running resource apply/3 against a guest via the agent exec (this was the 'validate Forge-over-vsock' open question). Forge's observable+idempotent invariant holds for run-state resources; build steps stay in the snapshot builder, never as a Forge exec resource.

(3) Mutable pointers — HEAD record like Sites (duke/myapp/latest → hash)? (4) API shape — POST /api/packages for registration, GET /api/packages/<hash> for download. (5) Metadata envelope — Gordian envelope wrapping: artifact hash, source repo, commit SHA, build timestamp, signer. (6) OpenTimestamps integration — auto-timestamp build artifacts? (7) Forgejo storage adapter feasibility — can we make Sites.Store a backend for Forgejo packages (single source of truth)? (8) Garbage collection — when are old versions pruned? title: Native Mjolnir workflow engine (Elixir DAG executor)
description: Design and implement a native Elixir workflow engine for Mjolnir-specific orchestration (NOT GitHub Actions — those stay in the Go runner). GenServer-per-task model with EventBus-driven dependency resolution. Targets: deploy pipelines, multi-VM integration tests, infrastructure provisioning. Simple DSL (Elixir terms or JSON) for DAG definition. OTP supervision provides fault tolerance (task crash → retry or abort). Does not need expression language or matrix strategies initially. Complements the Go runner rather than replacing it. Ref: architect review recommending hybrid architecture (Go for Actions compat + Elixir for native DAGs).

title: Warm VM snapshot caching for CI jobs
description: After first CI job installs dependencies, snapshot the VM as ci-cache-<repo>-<deps-hash>. Subsequent jobs restore from snapshot instead of re-installing. BTRFS reflink makes this near-instant and space-efficient. This is Mjolnir's killer differentiator vs Docker runners. Implementation: (1) Go executor checks for existing snapshot before spawning fresh VM, (2) after successful job, snapshot if deps changed (detect via hash of lockfiles), (3) expire cache snapshots after N days or on manual purge. Requires: snapshot naming convention, cache eviction policy, executor awareness of cache hits.

HOW ENV REACHES A STEP: POST /api/vms/:id/exec accepts ONLY 'command' and DROPS 'env' (router.ex reads body_params["command"] and calls VM.exec/3, which has no env param). The executor works around it by writing 'export K=V' lines to /.forgejo/.env.sh on the HOST-side rootfs — the guest sees it via virtio-fs — and sourcing it from each step script, so env persists across exec calls for post-steps. Names bash cannot export (every hyphenated action input: INPUT_FETCH-DEPTH, INPUT_INCLUDE-HIDDEN-FILES) are passed as an 'env K=V ...' prefix on the command (fix 9a3efce7, mjolnir-176 — before it they were silently SKIPPED, so steps ran with inputs absent). Relative working-directory is joined to GITHUB_WORKSPACE by the same commit (mjolnir-7c4); before, cd failed and a '|| cd $GITHUB_WORKSPACE || true' fallback silently ran the step in the repo root.

GUEST AGENT VERSION TRAP (fixed 2026-08-13, commit 225a007 — keep this note for diagnosis, not for the bug itself).

Until 2026-08-13, Mjolnir.VM.maybe_inject_guest_agent/2 skipped injection when resume_mode was true. Because a deploy restarts Elixir and Reconcile RESUMES every VM, any long-lived VM was frozen at the guest agent version its rootfs was born with, forever. VM 2da0e442 was running a 2026-06-23 agent on 2026-08-13. Fresh spawns always got the current agent; resumed ones never did.

SYMPTOM SHAPE TO RECOGNISE: a host request to the guest that TIMES OUT rather than erroring, on one VM but not on freshly spawned ones. The old guest could not deserialize the unknown action and sent NOTHING back, so the host blocked its full bound. A timeout reads as a wedged guest and sends you looking at the subsystem (cryptsetup, in this case) instead of at the agent version.

DIAGNOSTIC THAT CRACKED IT — compare fresh vs resumed, do not just read code:
  spawn a new VM with the same feature; if it works in seconds while the existing one times out, suspect the binary, not the feature.
  stat -c %y VMS/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent   (VMS = btrfs_root/@vms/<uuid>)
  strings that binary and grep for the action name (e.g. inject_secrets); 0 means the agent predates it.
  compare against btrfs_root/@base/<image>/usr/local/bin/mjolnir-agent AND the current build at /opt/mjolnir/native/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/mjolnir-agent. NOTE the @base copy can also be stale — fresh VMs get the current build injected over it at boot, so base mtime is not evidence.

The guest now replies with a typed error (VsockResponse::Error, ok:false) for unparseable requests, so this class fails fast instead of timing out — but only agents new enough to HAVE that fix will, which is precisely the gap the skipped injection created.

Managed secrets (secrets_mode=managed) VERIFIED end-to-end across a VM restart INCLUDING the deployed app unit, 2026-08-13, prod 45.76.77.97. Both mjolnir-azm and mjolnir-c6s are closed.

THE MECHANISM: a :managed app unit is WantedBy=mjolnir-secrets.target, NOT multi-user.target. That target has no Install section so nothing pulls it in at boot. The guest agent starts it from secrets::inject() once the volume is mounted AND load_env_vars succeeded. This is why it works: systemd evaluates a condition when the job runs, and at boot the passphrase has not arrived - so there must be no boot-time job at all. Adding only ConditionPathIsMountPoint made the app fail closed AND permanently.

HOW TO RE-VERIFY (about 5 min, no service restart):
1. Spawn managed with a probe secret. Response secrets_unlock_failed must be null.
2. Confirm the AGENT wrote and started the target with no deploy involved: cat /etc/systemd/system/mjolnir-secrets.target and systemctl is-active mjolnir-secrets.target.
3. Install an app unit whose ExecStart echoes the probe var, enable --now. Confirm the symlink lands in /etc/systemd/system/mjolnir-secrets.target.wants/.
4. POST /api/vms/ID/reboot. Do NOT restart the mjolnir service for this.
5. THE DECISIVE CHECK: read the LIVE process environment, not a file. Get MainPID via systemctl show APP -p MainPID --value, then tr NUL to newline over /proc/PID/environ and grep the probe var. A file on disk could be stale; a running process environ cannot be.
6. NEGATIVE TEST: systemctl stop APP, then umount /secrets, then cryptsetup luksClose mjolnir-secrets, then systemctl start APP. Expect ConditionResult=no and the journal line: was skipped because of an unmet condition check. Ordering covers boot; the condition covers a hand-start. Both must hold.

Observed timing: hypervisor kill to app active with secrets = 5 seconds.

TRAP when scripting these checks: nested quoting through ssh + curl + JSON mangles multi-line shell. Write the script to a file, wrap it with python3 json.dumps into a payload file, scp it, then curl -d with an @file reference.

DO NOT trust a /tmp probe-file line count as evidence - an unclean hypervisor kill can lose an unflushed rootfs write, so a pre-reboot append may simply be absent. Use the process environ.

How to verify 'mj connect' (interactive PTY) from an agent/script on macOS:
  ( printf 'cmd\n'; sleep 12; printf '\002d'; sleep 2 ) | script -q /dev/null mj connect <vmid> --p2p --session <name>
'script -q /dev/null' allocates the tty mj requires; \002 is Ctrl-B so '\002d' detaches from tmux. Expect exit code 1 + 'Connection error: connection lost' even on a CLEAN exit — that is a pre-existing bug (mjolnir-lmx), not a test failure.

BLOCKER-CLASS FINDING for Buzz provider work (epic mjolnir-e70).

Block-HOSTED Buzz communities (*.communities.buzz.xyz) REFUSE provider-deployed agents.
